## Cache serialization vocabulary

LCE1 envelope carries a type identity and body version; CacheDecode distinguishes Hit from a reasoned Miss. CacheEntryWriter/Reader manage typed-body sections and absolute offsets, independently of the16-byte key digest. See [cache module](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md) and [format reconstruction](L3-symbols/format-spec.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:144-228; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:28-38; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:117-126)


## Weighted cache budgets

Moka and Quick are in-memory CacheBackend implementations. Their eviction weights include fixed key cost plus declared entry size; shared-buffer-aware deep traversal is a separate callback-based metric. Quick can partition a budget among shards or use a single shard, so fitting the total cache does not imply admission to one shard. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:25-47; rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:186-199; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:40-50; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:101-106; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:216-229)


## Typed cache handles

LanceCache clones and child namespaces share backend, counters and type-aware memory callbacks. WeakLanceCache preserves namespace without a strong state reference and can compute a sized value after expiry without caching it. CacheStats counts successful coalesced loads as hits and excludes loader errors; these semantics differ from a raw request success/failure counter. [Full cache surface](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md). ## Encoded row identity and operation disposition

InlineRowIds keeps byte content and a shared lazy digest memo together so clones reuse both and replacing the wrapper does not carry an old digest into new bytes. Its digest identifies encoded content, not decoded-row equivalence. RowIdMeta chooses inline bytes or hidden-column storage. (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:27-98; rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:141-166)

The format-layer Transaction is a public protobuf wrapper; its schema-change classification is a conservative operation disposition used to decide where validation may be needed, not validation itself. It has no commit lifecycle in its local body. (rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs:16-82)


## Three version domains and manifest ownership

Dataset version is Manifest.version (with bit63 identifying a detached version), writer version is library-specific semver metadata, and data storage version is an exact ConcreteFileVersion. Treat these as separate domains. A Manifest is an in-memory snapshot with shared fragments and private cached logical offsets; its protobuf serialization is not a complete file or a commit. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:39-128; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:547-557; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:702-748)

Fragment metadata ties columns of the same physical rows to base DataFiles, ordered overlays, optional deletion and inline/column lineage. Every-file operations must account for overlays; lineage lookup intentionally uses base files only. These metadata rules now connect the flag policy to manifest decoding and shallow cloning; dataset IO and transaction publication are still untraced. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:519-558; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:589-725; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:242-313; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1011-1045)


## Three distinct coverage domains

Index fragment_bitmap tracks fragment IDs; overlay bitmaps track physical offsets within a fragment; key-existence Bloom data tracks encoded join keys for conflict detection. They cannot substitute for one another. Unknown index coverage is None, sparse overlay coverage is positional per field, and a Bloom overlap is only a possible key conflict. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:62-67; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:65-74; rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:175-212)

Covered index fields are dependencies whose values are carried with results; keyed fields decide which search the index can answer. Physical metadata currently validates a suffix representation. The protobuf's future independent-covering feature must not be assumed implemented by that validator. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:36-51; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:160-247; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:86-97)


## File-version request, identity and footer

Caller Stable/Next selectors resolve to exact2.2/2.3 in this snapshot. Persisted identities have no ordering; use explicit capabilities instead of comparing release numbers. V2.0 standard footer is(0,3), embedded footer and DataFile metadata are(2,0), while manifest string is2.0. These spellings describe the same exact identity. Footer-only detection reads8 bytes and does not certify a valid complete file. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60)

Overlay staleness is a metadata-derived conservative exclusion set: union newer changes to indexed dependency fields or their ancestors/descendants, then consumers must re-evaluate affected rows. This differs from resolving the newest value and from deleting rows; the helper only returns/accumulates physical offset sets. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:4-13; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:35-158)


## Positional lineage glossary

- **RowDatasetVersionRun / Sequence:** one dataset version per positional span, stored as runs aligned with row-ID order. Numeric span coordinates are not stable row IDs; consumers use cumulative lengths. [Version module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:272-311)
- **SpilledRowLineage:** preloaded row IDs/creation/update sequences keyed by fragment ID, allowing synchronous manifest preparation to preserve column-stored lineage. Loading itself remains a caller responsibility. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:750-769)
- **HoleRuns:** maximal missing-offset runs plus present-count prefixes, supporting offset-to-ordinal rank and inverse selection. It represents holes in a row-ID segment, not dataset-version runs or deletion-file IO. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:132-190)


## Row-ID representation terms

- **Bitmap:** internal presence bits indexed LSB first within each byte; logical length is separate from byte capacity. Constructors normalize padding, raw construction does not. The schema comment disagrees on bit order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-105; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)
- **EncodedU64Array:** owned U16/U32 relative offsets plus a base or plain U64 values; compressed does not imply sorted. Wire packed integers are little-endian. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-26; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-230)
- **Range folding:** decoder merges adjacency and groups ascending separated ranges through the segment helper; sequence writer expands the compact Ranges form back into plain wire Range arms. This changes in-memory representation without adding a protobuf arm. [Codec overview](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:60-96; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-255; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:376-398)


## Segment coordinates and scan state

- **U64Segment:** one of six in-memory representations of an intended distinct u64 sequence. Numeric values, present ordinals and enclosing numeric bounds are separate coordinates. Selection chooses five forms; compact Ranges comes from explicit range grouping/bitmap conversion. [Module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:16-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:196-299)
- **SegmentCursor / SegmentCursorState:** a public borrowed segment reader and its crate-visible bitmap byte/rank state. The wrapper fixes the source; reusable state alone does not. Dense expansion batches contiguous set-bit runs, while selection indices count present values. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)


## Row-ID sequences and ordinal selection

RowIdSequence preserves fragment row order across segments. Stable numeric IDs, ordinal positions and tree-map set membership are distinct: set conversion discards order, while masks translate selected IDs back into ordinal ranges. Public checked construction rejects duplicates within one input; raw range/slice conversions and extend do not enforce table-wide uniqueness. [Sequence analysis](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:39-52; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:209-265; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:302-319; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-797; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905)

RowIdSeqSlice is a borrowed positional view. RowIdSequenceCursor instead owns scan counters without a source lifetime: it rewinds for decreasing requests and resets segment state at boundaries, but callers must keep its sequence stable across calls. Internal selection clips at EOF; the public ReadBatchParams adapter has separate bounds/error behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:54-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:456-494; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:559-592; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:908-943; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:1055-1127)



## Creation lineage during transaction preparation

Creation version records first appearance; last-update version records the commit changing values. The reviewed transaction helper resolves stable IDs back to source physical offsets, preserves known creation versions, falls back to1 for unavailable creation of a found source, and stamps new IDs with the supplied commit version. Writer-placed lineage means row-ID Column or creation-version Column; it is a metadata predicate, not a provenance check. [Table details](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) and [local scenario](L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) separate these synchronous metadata mutations from the separately documented [IO](L3-symbols/protocol-io.md) and [publication](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md) protocols. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:21-79; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:258-295)




## Transaction intent and one-attempt preparation

A Transaction stores read_version,UUID,Operation,optional tag and shared string properties. An Operation names one of16 change kinds with typed payloads. PreparedIndices separately carries current-attempt original/prepared index metadata and fragment-reuse intent; it is not persisted by these containers. Retry/conflict/publication behavior is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). [Transaction API](L1-modules/rust-lance-table-transactions.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/builder.rs:12-25; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:37-262; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:4-18; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:44-100)

CoverageIdentity means UUID plus optional fragment bitmap, with other index metadata excluded from equality. ReadVersionState means borrowed manifest/index evidence from a transaction's fixed read version; it carries no runtime check that the pair matches. UpdatedFragmentOffsets means per-fragment physical offset bitmaps for partial column-update lineage. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:62-102; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:277-282)




## Equality versus conflict compatibility

Operation equality compares represented intent; different operation kinds always differ. Separate metadata predicates compare config upserts/deletes or table/schema/field metadata scopes. Their bool results are consumed by the commit conflict resolver, whose directional matrix is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). Durable commit-outcome identity uses protobuf forms in the inspected path, not these in-memory payload comparisons. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:18-29; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:863-991; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2225-2238; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:257-297)




## Operation pre-validation

Pre-validation checks operation shape against an optional current manifest. It is synchronous metadata inspection with no storage IO; its success does not certify physical files, schema completeness in modern formats or transaction compatibility. Merge field-binding protection and a separate base-file rewrite detector serve different purposes: binding safety versus latest-version stamping. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:18-200; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:301-462; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1196-1255)




## Durable transaction representation

Operation intent converts to a generated protobuf transaction before storage. Rust optional-empty states and transient rewrite metadata may disappear; unknown update-mode values decode as row rewrite, and empty rewrite groups take a legacy fallback. Therefore in-memory equality, decoded operation equality and persisted protobuf identity are distinct contracts. Byte storage/outcome recovery is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). ## Structural glossary refinement

A dense structural entry is a leaf slot or an invisible null/empty list. Repetition marks list starts with outer levels higher; definition0 is valid. Leaf-first DefinitionInterpretation distinguishes null versus empty. A control word packs levels into0/1/2/4 little-endian bytes and reports row-start, visibility and validity separately. FSL validity is broadcast on write and decimated on read. [Encoding module](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:4-107; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:426-451; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:593-645; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:2334-2340; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:2412-2548)


## Encoder orchestration glossary

A field encoder buffers a logical Arrow field and may emit several physical columns. A field strategy selects it before data; an array strategy selects a page encoder. EncodeTask produces one page asynchronously. OutOfLineBuffers reserves absolute padded positions but retains unpadded payloads; actual writers must implement the reservation. FieldEncodingContext carries the complete recursive strategy and root metadata. The in-memory encode_batch helper is a separate test/IPC path with sequential polling and unpadded appends. ## Decoder facade glossary

Scheduling selects byte ranges and produces page messages; decoding materializes Arrow arrays through tasks. Array and structural message grammars are distinct. A ReadBatchTask carries a future plus expected row count. Structural byte targets adapt using reported decoded size and can overshoot; array i32-offset limits are a separate mechanism. RequestBatch aggregates I/O calls while preserving each caller's buffer order. [Module contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). ## Primitive index and value terms

A mini-block has distinct byte, top-level-row and leaf-value coordinates. A trailer begins a row continued in the next block; that next block has a preamble. Constant pages retain one scalar plus repetition/definition levels, then materialize selected leaf positions. Dictionary normalization moves null dictionary entries into key validity before encoding; physical null-key repair prevents invalid hidden indices when validity is removed. [Helper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). ## Blob decode view and representation

Original BlobLayout stores position/size descriptions plus same-file payload buffers; descriptor-only reads and binary materialization use separate cache views. Blob-v2 prepared records become kind/position/size/blob_id/blob_uri descriptors, with sidecar/URI handling outside this encoder. A payload shard is a byte-targeted group of original Blob reads, distinct from dataset fragments or MemWAL shards;32MiB is a target that can be exceeded. [Blob contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). ## Fixed slots and map entries

A fixed-size-list dimension gives the number of child slots per outer row. Null outer rows still reserve those slots; variable-size descendants under them can be cleared with a garbage mask. Map entries are Struct key/value rows whose offsets and parent validity are reconstructed through rep/def layers. The current complex FSL path requires immediate Struct children, while Map requires unsorted entries and a nonnullable key. [Nested wrapper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). # Lance engine orientation

> Refresh 2026-10-09, `db684d1f0726c00b6defb7963a604a7719e82b5a`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-09.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

> Refresh 2026-10-07, `84d1681e07af565837f2d97e72ff1b8b040cd15c`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-07.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

**Navigation and contracts; source access is expected.** Start here, choose a path, and open its ordered source set. Deep format details live in the [format contract](L3-symbols/format-spec.md), terminology in the [engine glossary](L0-glossary.md), and exact retained declarations in the [frozen symbol snapshot](L3-symbols/symbol-index.md). [Scope and trust](V21-PROTOCOL.md).

## Architecture and state ownership

Lance presents a versioned Dataset over immutable data files and versioned metadata. A fragment groups physical columns for the same rows; its manifest entry carries deletion, overlay and lineage metadata. A Dataset handle owns a manifest snapshot plus stores, commit handler and session/cache handles. Publishing a new manifest makes a mutation visible; finishing a data file alone does not publish a dataset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-87; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-572; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:1-264)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  API[Dataset / Scanner / write and index builders] --> Plan[Scan planning and execution nodes]
  API --> Tx[Transaction preparation and commit]
  Plan --> Index[Scalar / vector / full-text indices]
  Plan --> Fragment[Fragment reads and row identity]
  Fragment --> File[lance-file exact-version readers]
  API --> Writer[Fragment / file writers]
  Writer --> File
  File --> Encoding[lance-encoding page and buffer mechanisms]
  File --> IO[lance-io stores and scheduled reads]
  Tx --> Table[lance-table manifests, operations and conflicts]
  Table --> Publish[CommitHandler publication]
  Publish --> IO
  Index --> IO
  Core[lance-core schemas, errors and common data structures] --> API
  Core --> Table
  Protos[Handwritten protobuf schemas] --> Table
  Protos --> File
```

The arrows identify ownership/call boundaries rather than a claim that every request crosses every box. Scanner creates a physical plan; the DataFusion adapter executes it and returns a RecordBatch stream. Encoding describes pages and schedules their bytes through an I/O seam; it does not commit Dataset versions. Index creation writes index state before committing CreateIndex metadata. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2889-2905; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-134; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:687-734)

## Read path

**Entry:** `dataset.scan().try_into_stream().await?`. The stream must be consumed to execute reads. This is a trace of the public Rust path; it is not a command that was run during KB work.

1. `Dataset::scan` clones the snapshot into `Scanner`. Configure projection/filter/vector/limit before planning. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704)
2. `Scanner::create_plan_impl` validates options, resolves full-text/query filters, chooses vector, full-text, MinHash or filtered read source, and adds filtering, ordering, limit and final projection. Scalar index use is conditioned on prefiltering or absence of nearest search. Conflicting search modes error. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3498-3663)
3. `try_into_stream` passes the plan, batch size and statistics callback to `execute_plan`. Multiple output partitions are merged with order preservation when ordering exists; execution starts at partition 0 of that final plan. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2889-2905; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)
4. The selected source reads fragment metadata/deletions/lineage and reaches exact-version file readers. File open loads footer/global/column metadata; prepared reads schedule pages, decode selected values and materialize batches. The local contract is in the [frozen shared-reader record](L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs.md); source ranges are rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028. No guarantee is made that every query reads every column or uses an index.

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2889-2932,3498-3663` → `rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761` → `rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028`. For a particular scan operator, follow the scanner's selected source rather than opening all execution nodes.

## Write path

**Entry:** `Dataset::write(reader, destination, Some(params)).await?`.

1. `Dataset::write` constructs `InsertBuilder`, applies params and calls `execute_stream`; the input reader is converted into stream/schema. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-120)
2. Resolve destination/store/version, validate the write, resolve target bases and write fragments. A fixed data filename combined with target bases is rejected. `execute_uncommitted` stops after building a transaction: data objects may exist, but no manifest has been published. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:144-265)
3. Create and overwrite produce `Operation::Overwrite`; append produces `Operation::Append`. The transaction's read version comes from the destination snapshot or 0 for a new destination. File assembly/flush belongs to the fragment writer, and its exact bytes to the selected file-version writer. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:267-315; rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1733-1839)
4. `do_commit` configures `CommitBuilder`. Existing datasets use the retrying transaction path (or the explicitly selected detached path); new datasets use `commit_new_dataset`. Detached new-dataset creation is rejected; detached commit cannot use V1 manifest naming. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:148-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)
5. Successful publication returns a Dataset carrying the committed manifest/location and caches. Data-file existence is not commit evidence; error/outcome recovery belongs to `io/commit.rs`. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:516-572; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:269-297)

**Ordered initial read set (5 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-315` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1733-1839` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-572` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1649-1869`. The exact persisted manifest contract is already available through the [frozen table I/O record](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs.md).

## Compaction path

**Entry:** `compact_files(&mut dataset, options, remap_options).await?`.

1. Construct and run the compaction planner. Reject eager index remapping on a tagged fragment-reuse history. No planned tasks means no new committed version. Execute planned rewrites with bounded concurrency and collect successful results. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152)
2. Each rewrite validates its target exact file version, refreshes required fragment statistics and chooses binary-copy or scan/re-encode. A forced binary-copy request cannot silently fall back. Capture old physical row addresses only when a consumer needs remapping; stable row IDs use their own lineage. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2494-2569; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2693-2789)
3. `commit_compaction` validates tagged-history/remap requirements and takes the **minimum RewriteResult.read_version**, so conflicts since task planning remain visible even if the caller opened a newer Dataset handle. Address-style outputs reserve fragment IDs; remap indices now or produce deferred fragment-reuse metadata according to the selected protocol. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3227-3337)
4. Commit a Rewrite operation through Dataset's normal commit boundary. Old files are not made safe to delete merely by writing replacements; retain manifest/version retention policy. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3662-3693; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:74-123)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152,2494-2789,3227-3337,3662-3693` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1649-1869` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1424-1691,2851-3107` → [frozen manifest application](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs.md). Split copy mechanics or a specific index remapper into a separate task instead of expanding this read set without bound.

## Index build and query path

**Entry:** `DatasetIndexExt::create_index` / `create_index_builder`; query through Scanner.

1. The Dataset extension constructs `CreateIndexBuilder`; optional name and replace settings are applied before awaiting it. The builder validates one-column admission and reserves names against all stored indices, including unsupported ones. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2053-2087; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:167-216)
2. Build/train through the selected scalar/vector index implementation; `execute_uncommitted` yields metadata without publication. Multi-segment FM-Index construction has a separate atomic multi-index path. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:167-216; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:687-704)
3. On replacement, collect same-name metadata to remove, then commit CreateIndex with newly built metadata. Reload the committed index by UUID so the return value reflects commit-time changes; missing UUID after commit errors. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:697-734)
4. Scanner later selects index-backed or scan-backed sources from query/filter options. Data not covered by an index must be accounted for by that query path; never equate a stored index bitmap with all current rows. The distinctions are in the [frozen index metadata contract](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3578-3663)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/index.rs:2053-2087` → `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:167-216,687-734` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3578-3663` → [frozen index metadata](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). Concrete scalar/IVF-PQ implementation choices belong to the M2 index Module Map, not an assumed universal build pipeline.

## Essential distinctions

- File format version, Dataset manifest version, per-row creation/update version and index version are different domains. Never compare them interchangeably. [Exact version matrix](L3-symbols/format-spec.md); [glossary](L0-glossary.md).
- Stable logical row IDs differ from physical `(fragment_id, offset)` addresses; compaction changes physical addresses. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:6-79; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81)
- Declaration in a protobuf union does not establish acceptance in every exact file version. Reader grammar and writer selection are independent checks. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:93-110; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:93-118)
- Stable format compatibility is durable; unstable formats may change; frozen legacy paths are not new-feature extension points. (AGENTS.md:5-20)

This orientation completes M1's architecture and four public paths. Detailed subsystem/API contracts and navigation tests remain independently tracked in M2–M4; no build or runtime execution is claimed.

## Development entry

Choose a task in the [ordered navigation index](L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md), then read its contract and bounded implementation set. API-only questions start at [public contracts and bindings](L3-symbols/public-api.md).

## Dependencies and extension boundaries

ANN imports table identity, table index metadata, and index metric types; filtered read imports table identity; index imports protobuf Any and historical index details. These are schema type dependencies. Build-time generators, crate boundaries, and runtime registrations remain pending. (protos/ann.proto:8-10; protos/ann.proto:87-90; protos/filtered_read.proto:8-8; protos/index.proto:8-9)

Add new detail kinds in index.proto; do not relocate existing lance.table types solely for naming consistency because serialized identities matter. Extending existing historical messages is explicitly allowed where needed. The explanatory comment abbreviates the new namespace as lance.index, but the actual package is lance.index.pb. (protos/index_old.proto:8-17; protos/index.proto:6-6)

There are no environment-variable declarations or Cargo feature definitions in the reviewed schema bodies. Manifest feature requirements occur as explicit numeric contracts: overlays need 64, and hidden column lineage needs 2048. Actual supported flags, their stability, and read/write gates must be established from table and Rust code. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:19-27; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51)

Decoder failure modes are not executable in these files. Notable required validations include MinHash field ranges before allocation, unknown signature-version rejection, and exact lineage column cardinality. (protos/index.proto:332-382; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305)

Table imports Any, Timestamp, shared file schema and publicly re-exports fragment metadata. Transaction imports file/table/Any. file2 imports Any and Empty but only uses Empty in declarations; old encoding schema imports Empty for plain column encoding. ## Architecture and ownership

The low-level trait stores Arc<dyn Any+Send+Sync> under16-byte InternalCacheKey. It delegates logical-key construction/type safety to LanceCache. Optional codecs allow persistence only for serializable entries; None requires memory retention. The wrapper and its typed adapters are covered below; production type-specific bodies are still pending; typed downcasts and Moka/Quick wrappers are covered below. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:45-76)

The configuration path is synchronous: build_from_uri -> parse_backend_uri -> build_from_config -> chosen BackendBuildFn. A process-global OnceLock holds a mutex map of constructor function pointers; options are owned string maps cloned before dispatch. Construction happens after the registry guard is released. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend_uri.rs:51-54; rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:80-95; rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:153-171)

## Key identity

Root namespace is deterministic32-byte BLAKE3 derive_key output for a fixed context and empty material. Each child hashes one framed segment under the parent's keyed hash; nested dataset/index differs from a single dataset/index segment. Entry key hashes the entry domain, key-format version, stable value-type id, logical-key schema id/version, then typed fields, retaining the first16 digest bytes. Namespace32/key16 are asserted locally. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:19-28; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:124-179; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:288-314; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:336-341; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:398-404)

CacheKeySchema::new does not enforce nonempty/unique ids or positive versions. Option/sequence/variant writers emit markers and counts without validating grammar or ordinals; callers must keep their logical schema unambiguous and update version when meanings change. No usize writer exists. Stable framing is a local cache protocol contract; it is not a data-file format version or an authentication boundary. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:4-15; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:56-84; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:140-144; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:252-287)

## Backend contract

get is Option-only, insert returns unit, and get_or_insert accepts a pinned boxed Send future producing Result<(entry,size)> and returns Result<(entry,was_cached)>. Docs request concurrent-load deduplication except for disabled caches. Counts/bytes may flush pending work; approximate defaults0 can mean unavailable; capacity None can mean unknown. A custom deep traversal should include key footprints and reuse a Context to avoid counting shared buffers twice, falling back to declared entry weights for unregistered types. The interface requirements are compared with the concrete wrappers below; dependency internals remain outside reviewed source. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:56-145)

Physical persistence must namespace keys with blake3-128-v1 and store canonical16 bytes; one-way digests provide neither prefix invalidation nor inventory. Migration docs offer shared-backend clear or versioned namespace rotation. Rotation leaves old entries to age out rather than reclaiming them immediately. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:11-31; rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:19-23)

## Configuration and registry behavior

Kind syntax is ASCII letter then zero or more ASCII alphanumeric/plus/minus/dot, lowercased without trimming. Config fields remain public; dispatch repeats validation to handle direct struct construction. with_option silently replaces same-key entries; URI query duplicates instead return InvalidInput after percent decoding. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:24-78; rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:153-159; rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend_uri.rs:70-104)

The URI parser splits first colon, then first question mark, strips exactly one initial// from hierarchy and stores nonempty remainder as path. Host:port/path remains intact; paths are not percent-decoded;# has no fragment role. Query skips empty ampersand-separated pairs and splits each at first=. Empty key/value are allowed. Percent escapes must decode to valid UTF-8; plus stays literal. A query path conflicts with a nonempty hierarchy path. Error messages may include the full supplied URI, including query values. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend_uri.rs:59-171)

Built-in discovery only recognizes MOKA_BACKEND_KIND; local docs/tests identify this as moka, and the constant and constructor are now analyzed below at rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:317-366. register_backend permits replacement for built-ins and rejects other duplicates. ensure_builtin_backends inserts only missing defaults on every dispatch, preserving overrides; it runs before requested-kind validation. Registry poison becomes Internal error; test locks recover inner state without clearing poison. Constructor errors pass through directly. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:91-109; rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:126-193; rust/lance-core/src/cache/registry.rs:314-319)

## Codec wrapper and body IO

[Codec evidence](../L2-files/rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs.md) · [Entry IO evidence](../L2-files/rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs.md). A Copy codec descriptor holds static type id,u32 version and two plain function pointers. from_impl binds concrete CacheCodecImpl callbacks; serialization downcasts with expect and can panic for the wrong erased type. Custom new adapters are accepted without checking type coherence. Deserializing through a typed adapter allocates Arc<T>. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:235-307)

Serialize writes LCE1 envelope first then invokes body writer with absolute entry position; failures can leave partial output. Decode checks framing, exact type id, then input version<=current version before calling body decoder. InvalidEnvelope/TypeMismatch/VersionTooNew/BodyError all become Miss; success becomes Hit without EOF or type revalidation. No panic catch, checksum or authentication exists here. Backend eviction/recomputation is documented intent, not executed by this wrapper. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:120-138; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:144-175; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:317-370)

The outer envelope is called stabilized and stability-critical, while CacheCodecImpl docs explicitly call its serialized format experimental, describe future stability rules, and also say TYPE_ID must not change once shipped. These statements do not establish a latest-released stable contract by themselves. Existing synthetic old-shape rejection tests are recorded as current source; they do not authorize designing migrations for earlier unstable revisions. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:22-36; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:51-60; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:191-225; rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:459-476; AGENTS.md:7-18)

Body writer tracks absolute offset for IPC64-byte alignment, buffers each protobuf header using encode_to_vec, and streams other operations through supplied Write/delegated helpers. raw_writer does not advance position and must not interleave with aligned IPC. Reader stores unchecked offset/version; read_header performs checked prefix/payload bounds and advances only after successful decode; body() slices without advancing and can panic if public new was given invalid offset. IPC/raw implementations delegate to lance_arrow and still need exact algorithm/zero-copy verification. All-read-zero-copy prose does not mean allocation-free protobuf decoding or an allocation-free Vec<RecordBatch> result. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:28-114; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:117-202)

## Memory estimator boundary

Insert and executed loaders register a callback keyed by concrete Rust TypeId. Fresh hits do not register one. Registration recovers poisoned lock guards and releases them before user DeepSizeOf runs. Declared eviction weight uses a new deep-size context plus two outer Arc counters for each entry independently. Whole-cache deep traversal marks state once, clones the accessor table outside callback execution and traverses with one shared Context; missing callbacks fall back to backend-declared bytes. It excludes separately counted CacheState/backend/accessor-map metadata, and nested Arc sizing excludes its own counter overhead. This is an explicit estimator, not a resident heap measurement. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:189-248; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:273-294; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:362-402; rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:38-44; rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:182-189)

The shared1024-byte fixture expects eviction weights to count shared storage twice but deep traversal only once; a second prefixed handle in the same Context adds0 children. Reentrant insertion checks a one-second deadlock bound, but its strongly referenced cache value can form a retention cycle and no leak assertion exists. Use the weak handle deliberately where ownership should not retain cache state. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:824-844; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:1204-1268; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:570-583)

## Representation and responsibility

`Field` is a public, mutable tree whose public members include name/id/parent_id, logical string, metadata, encoding, nullability, children, optional dictionary and primary/clustering key positions. `LogicalType` hides its String member, but `From<&str>` accepts arbitrary text. Consequently public construction does not guarantee validity; `Field::data_type` is infallible in signature and can panic when parsing malformed logical strings or indexing absent children. Arrow-to-Field conversion is a fallible boundary with partial validation; it is not a substitute for the separate Schema validation layer described in the schema supplement. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-195; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:250-291; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1317)

Private `field` and `schema` modules are hidden behind `lance_core::datatypes` re-exports. `Field` owns local tree operations and metadata transformations. It performs no storage IO, asynchronous work or synchronization in its defined methods. It depends on Arrow datatypes/array casts, `lance_arrow` extension/type helpers, core errors/truthy parsing, and schema comparison/projection helpers. Lazy blob statics use `LazyLock` and shared `Arc` fields; loaded dictionaries share `ArrayRef` values. ## Logical type strings and conversion failures

Primitive spellings and the complete grammar are in [the format supplement](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md). Utf8View/BinaryView normalize to Utf8/Binary. `json` and `blob` decode as LargeBinary. Containers require separately retained Field children except scalar/nested fixed-size-list logical strings. Timezones are verbatim strings joined after `timestamp:unit:`; `-` is the no-timezone sentinel, and timezone validity is not checked. Size/precision integer parsing does not enforce all Arrow semantic bounds. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:323-565; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:170-195)

Dictionary logical strings are `dict:value:index:false`, with exactly four colon-delimited components on decode. The last component is ignored by the parser. The encoder probes successful inverse parsing, rejecting colon-bearing or child-dependent components early; it allows view normalization and is not an exact-identity or integer-key validator. The tests cover every integer key and representative supported/rejected values. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:360-376; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:508-519; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:818-922)

`Dictionary` equality compares loaded values only when both are present, unloaded offset/length when both are absent, and rejects mixed states. `Field::set_dictionary_values` stores an Arc clone with zero placement after a dictionary-type assertion. Recursive `set_dictionary` supports integer-key dictionaries, Struct, List and LargeList; it does not descend into Map/FixedSizeList. It uses Arrow casts, indexing and unwrap, so a mismatched array/schema may panic. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:567-599; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:455-522)

## Comparison and tree operations

Derived `Field::PartialEq` compares the representation. Default `SchemaCompareOptions` instead ignores metadata, dictionaries and IDs, uses Strict nullability, and delegates child structure to schema helpers. OneWay nullability means a non-null actual can satisfy a nullable expected; not the reverse. Recognized minimal and complete v2 logical shapes compare only their shared prefix; two complete forms compare all four children. Parent IDs, encoding and separate key-position members are not directly compared by `compare_with_options`. ## IDs, metadata and boundary checks

Arrow import removes `lance:field_id`, parses i32 and clamps any negative to -1. Map import requires sorted=false, Struct entries, at least two children and a non-null first key, but does not enforce exactly two children or entries-field nullability here. Primary/clustering position parsing silently drops invalid u32 text; a truthy legacy primary-key flag supplies position0 when no parsed position exists. Schema import enforces primary-key leaf/non-null/List/LargeList/Map ancestry constraints, but not one-based position validity; see rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:835-908. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:37-60; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1270)

`set_id` rewrites parent IDs, assigns only negative IDs and increments a caller-owned seed; it does not advance the seed for retained IDs or validate collisions/overflow. `reset_id` leaves parent IDs intact. Arrow export reconstructs datatypes and metadata but does not restore field-ID metadata or derive key-position metadata from the separate members. Moving through Arrow can therefore change representation details even if logical types remain equal. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1087-1111; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1327-1348)

Tests pin dictionary equality/parse-back behavior, timestamp offsets, blob classifiers, view normalization, map rejection, comparison diagnostics and repeated descriptor projection. Local uncovered edges include intersection child-error suppression, several partial map-validation constraints and non-integer-but-parseable dictionary keys; this is a statement about these test blocks, not the entire repository. ## Construction and validation

Public `Schema` stores `fields: Vec<Field>` and `metadata: HashMap<String,String>`. Arrow import converts each Field, copies metadata, assigns missing IDs, runs `validate`, then `verify_primary_key`. A borrowed Schema conversion simply clones, while Arrow export converts fields and copies metadata without validation. Public member mutation can therefore create states not accepted by Arrow import. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:24-31; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:889-928)

`validate` rejects dotted/duplicate top-level names, unapproved negative IDs, duplicate IDs anywhere and nonpositive fixed-size-list dimensions. Only matching top-level lineage names/IDs establish the reserved-ID exceptions; their datatype/nullability is not checked here. It does not check parent IDs, nested name uniqueness or primary keys. Dimension validation recursively follows nested FixedSizeList types because primitive nested lists collapse into a single Field leaf; the surrounding Field traversal handles other containers. Malformed Field reconstruction can still panic before these checks return an error. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:113-134; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:328-383; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:170-195)

Primary-key verification requires a leaf, non-null ancestry and no List/LargeList/Map ancestry. It does not enforce data uniqueness, position uniqueness/contiguity or explicitly reject a primitive-element FixedSizeList leaf. Clustering keys have no corresponding structural verifier here and may be nullable, as tested. Positive primary-key positions sort before legacy position0; the positive u32 position is cast to i32 in its sort key, so very large positions do not sort in ordinary u32 order. Clustering positions sort directly as u32. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:136-172; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:835-871; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:3142-3225)

`set_field_id` starts after the greater of current and supplied persisted maxima, assigns negative IDs only, and rebuilds parent IDs. It does not guard integer overflow. Dataset callers should provide `Manifest::max_field_id` to avoid reusing dropped IDs. `merge` resets incoming IDs but leaves new fields unassigned until an explicit later assignment. `extend` appends converted fields before checking duplicate names; an Internal error leaves the mutation in place. Neither operation runs full validation. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:663-766; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:2370-2413)

## Lookup and field-path grammar

`FieldRef::ById` verifies existence and produces InvalidInput on absence; `ByPath` produces FieldNotFound with suggestion candidates. Schema ID lookup includes roots, unlike Field ID lookup. Ancestry lookup ignores stored parent IDs and traverses the actual tree in reverse sibling order using cloned path vectors. `field_paths` joins ancestry names with raw dots for diagnostics; use `field_path` or `field_path_minimal` when escaping matters. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:33-80; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:417-436; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:606-661; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:768-833)

`parse_field_path` uses backticks, doubles embedded backticks, separates unquoted dots and rejects empty/malformed segments. Double quotes, spaces and brackets are ordinary characters; earlier resolver doc examples using double quotes are inconsistent with this parser. `resolve` hides parse errors as None. Case-insensitive lookup prefers exact matches, then the first ASCII-folded match; ambiguity is not rejected. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:224-257; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:543-587; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1567-1663)

| Formatter | Exact rule | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| format_field_path | Quote any segment containing a non-alphanumeric/non-underscore character; Unicode alphanumeric is accepted | Does not separately handle leading digits, SQL reserved words or empty segments; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1665-1691 |
| format_field_path_minimal | Quote only literal dots/backticks; double embedded backticks | Roundtrip promise assumes nonempty valid segments; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1693-1735 |
| escape_field_path_for_project | Preserve exact wildcard `*`; otherwise parse and quote every segment | Parse failure becomes one literal segment instead of an error; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1737-1758 |

## Comparison and schema set operations

`Schema::PartialEq` ignores schema metadata but compares Field representations. Configurable comparison optionally includes schema metadata and delegates Field policy. Default field comparison is equal length plus ordered zip; allowing nullable omissions, arbitrary subschema or ignored order switches to name maps. Extras are always rejected. Missing expected fields are accepted only under the selected omission policy; order remains checked unless explicitly ignored. Duplicate names can produce different results across fast/slow comparison and explanation paths because one maps the last actual name while the explanation chooses the first. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:174-215; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:930-1076)

Schema `project` follows requested root order and merges repeated root selections. Missing roots error or drop according to wrapper, while missing nested paths can inherit Field's empty-child success. System columns are dropped by ordinary projection and appended by the preserving variant; that variant includes rowoffset. `project_by_schema` rejects requested root names containing dots, follows the requested schema order and delegates type matching. `intersection` follows Other root order and propagates root errors; Field child intersection follows Self order and can discard errors. `merge` preserves Self field order/metadata precedence and appends new roots. These APIs do not all apply BlobHandling or atomic selection. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:259-326; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:385-407; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:470-525; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:730-766; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:959-984)

## Projection selection model

`Projectable: Debug + Send + Sync` exposes a borrowed Schema. Projection owns an Arc of that trait, public HashSet<i32> IDs, four metadata flags (rowid, rowaddr, last-update, creation-version) and BlobHandling. There is no rowoffset flag. Empty uses no selections and default BlobsDescriptions; full unions a clone of the base schema. Selection methods consume/return Self. Debug omits the base. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1099-1130; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1191-1267)

`union_column` resolves a path, inserts all ancestors and descendants of the target, and recognizes four exact raw system strings separately. Predicate methods insert/remove only matching IDs, without maintaining tree closure. Set union/intersection/subtraction operate directly on IDs/flags and retain Self's base/blob mode without checking that bases match. `union_schema` and `subtract_schema` do not enforce the base-membership checks promised in their docs: nonnegative IDs are inserted/removed directly; only unexpected negative IDs trigger debug assertions. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1269-1497)

`to_bare_schema` applies Field projection in base order. `to_schema` then appends metadata fields in fixed rowid/rowaddr/last-update/creation order through `extend(...).unwrap()`, so duplicate existing names can panic and appended IDs remain unassigned. `into_schema`, `into_schema_ref` and `to_arrow_schema` delegate that materialization. This is schema construction, not scan execution or IO. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1499-1564)

## Blob policy and a local discrepancy

`returns_description` exposes the private unload predicate; this is documented for early/late materialization heuristics. AllBinary loads marked blobs. BlobsDescriptions unloads marked blobs. AllDescriptions chooses every binary-like or blob field. The two set modes retain selected IDs as binary, with SomeBlobsBinary limited to marked blobs. IDs are cast from i32 to u32 for these sets. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1110-1166)

`unload_if_needed` first loads a chosen blob via `binary_blob_mut`, otherwise unloads via `unloaded_mut`, otherwise recurses into children. For an ordinary non-blob binary field, AllDescriptions can return true from `returns_description` while `unloaded_mut` leaves the field unchanged. This follows the two reviewed functions; caller or reader behavior beyond this local discrepancy still requires investigation. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1144-1188; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:648-658)

## Established API contracts

`row_lineage_field_id(&str) -> Option<i32>` maps only _rowid, _row_created_at_version and _row_last_updated_at_version to -3/-4/-5. `is_system_column(&str) -> bool` recognizes these plus _rowaddr and _rowoffset. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. The root's UInt64 Arrow metadata fields are nullable for scan/selection use, while hidden persisted lineage columns have a separate non-null contract. (rust/lance-core/src/lib.rs:22-98; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305)

`DatasetTakeRows: Debug + Send + Sync` supplies `schema(&self) -> &Schema` and async `take_rows(&self, row_ids: &[u64], projection: &Schema) -> Result<RecordBatch>`. It is an extension boundary for internal consumers, not a promise of stable public behavior merely because Rust visibility is pub. No ordering or missing-ID policy is defined by the trait itself. (rust/lance-core/src/traits.rs:12-27)

`RowAddress(u64)` privately stores high-32 fragment and low-32 offset. The maximum fragment and all-ones row are tombstone constants, but constructors accept them. `address_range` computes fragment+1 without an overflow guard, so its maximum-u32 input is an unresolved caller-boundary risk, not evidence that every call is unsafe. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:23-79)

`blob_path(&Path, &str, u32) -> Path` constructs base/stem/32-bit-reversed-binary-id.blob without IO. Changing the bit reversal, width or suffix changes stored sidecar lookup identity. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/blob.rs:32-41)

## SIMD API and dispatch policy

Public `#[non_exhaustive] enum SimdSupport` has None, Neon, Sse, Avx, AvxFma, Avx2, Avx512, Avx512FP16, Lsx and Lasx. Its Display implementation emits lowercase labels (AVX512 FP16 uses `avx512_fp16`). ## Stream API and extension boundaries

Public `enum Capacity { Bounded(u32), Unbounded }` controls cloned-item backlog, not bytes. `SharedStream<'a,T:Clone>::new(inner:BoxStream<'a,T>,capacity:Capacity)->(Self,Self)` returns two handles with shared private mutex state. `impl<T:Clone> Stream for SharedStream<'_,T>` has Item=T. `Bounded(0)` is accepted but cannot acquire a permit, even after dropping one side. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:21-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-170)

```rust
pub trait SharedStreamExt<'a>: Stream + Send where Self::Item: Clone {
    fn share(self, capacity: Capacity)
        -> (SharedStream<'a, Self::Item>, SharedStream<'a, Self::Item>);
}
```

Only `BoxStream<'a,T>` implements the sharing extension here. The two consumers must advance sufficiently evenly under bounded capacity; unbounded capacity can retain the entire input. Dropping a lagging side discards its pending clones/releases permits; dropping a pending polling owner releases ownership and wakes the parked peer outside the mutex. Upstream panics and clone panics have no recovery guarantee. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:249-275)

Both callback wrappers are public structs generic over `S: Stream, F: FnOnce()`, expose `pub fn new(stream:S,f:F)->Self`, and implement Stream<Item=S::Item>. `FinallyStream` calls F synchronously on the first observed None; early destruction does not call it. `OnDropStream` calls F at destruction, including unpolled or early-dropped instances, and does nothing special at EOF. Callback panics propagate. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:277-361)

```rust
pub trait FinallyStreamExt<S: Stream>: Stream + Sized {
    fn finally<F: FnOnce()>(self, f: F) -> FinallyStream<Self, F>;
}
pub trait StreamOnDropExt: Stream + Sized {
    fn on_drop<F: FnOnce()>(self, f: F) -> OnDropStream<Self, F>;
}
```

These are signature-only excerpts: both methods have default bodies, and blanket implementations cover stream types. FinallyStreamExt's default body constructs fields directly, while its blanket implementation calls FinallyStream::new; StreamOnDropExt's default calls OnDropStream::new. Exact bodies and pin projection are preserved in L2. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:309-322; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:363-370)

## IO extension contract and async lifecycle

EncodingsIo requires Debug + Send + Sync. submit_request returns a static boxed future with one Bytes per requested range, including empty ranges. Its priority documentation uses the lowest delivered row to prioritize late indirect reads. The trait itself supplies no scheduler, response-count check, range validation or cancellation policy. Implementations own those obligations. submit_single submits immediately and maps a successful vector to its last element with pop().unwrap(): an empty success panics when polled; surplus results are discarded. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-76)

Both optional derivation hooks default to None: bypass for indirect IO and additive per-scope statistics. Their documented fallback is the original service; the default stats implementation creates no recorder wrapper. BufferScheduler inherits these defaults. Its private Bytes owns the backing handle; new moves it into the scheduler. satisfy_request casts u64 endpoints to usize without checked narrowing and delegates to Bytes::slice without a Lance error conversion. submit_request eagerly slices and collects in input order before constructing a ready future, ignores priority, and owns the resulting vector independently of self. Dropping the future cannot undo this already executed work. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:78-134)

The reviewed lance-file implementation splits large ranges, omits physical IO for empty ranges and reinserts empty results; it checks returned chunk count before reassembling. Single chunks clone Bytes handles and multiple chunks copy into a combined allocation. These adapter checks are not checks in the trait or BufferScheduler. The broader FileScheduler queue and cancellation lifecycle remains pending. A contextual decode_batch call creates BufferScheduler from EncodedBatch.data; that partial caller read does not cover the rest of decoding. ### Configuration precedence and validation boundary

CompressionParams first merges an exact DataType::to_string key, then either an exact column key or the first matching wildcard entry in HashMap order. An exact empty record suppresses patterns, several matching patterns have no specificity priority, and None cannot clear inherited values. Pattern syntax is one simple prefix/suffix/middle star branch, not general globbing. Field-level parameters carry optional values without validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:45-169)

The reviewed V2.2 strategy then overlays field metadata. Its parser copies compression strings, silently drops invalid numeric level/threshold parses, warns and skips invalid BSS/chunk-size values, and returns partial fields. Thus the comment "using default" on invalid BSS can mean preserving an inherited setting after merge, not necessarily forcing Auto. Full compression selection and version-specific restrictions still require the complete policy files. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-38; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:554-585; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:122-141)

Metadata keys and two dictionary-value environment identifiers are literal public constants. They do not read the environment themselves. One contextual dictionary caller reads both env variables and delegates precedence to a resolver still pending full analysis. BSS default string is auto; CompressionFieldParams default contains no chosen BSS mode. (rust/lance-encoding/src/constants.rs:9-65; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6381-6392; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:55-73)

### Memory ownership and row accounting

AccumulationQueue tracks Arrow-reported memory and caller-supplied top-level row counts. insert flushes only above the budget, includes the overshooting array and keeps that triggering array without copying. Retained arrays at/below budget are copied unless keep_original_array is set. The queue is synchronous and holds exclusive mutable state; callers separately synchronize rep/def builders. Row order/count validity and avoidance of the u64::MAX first-row sentinel collision are caller obligations. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:10-105; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7976-8007)

BytepackedIntegerEncoder stores 1/2/4/8-byte LE integers selected from declared maximum. Zero omits every appended value and carries no count. Checked append validates storage width, not the original maximum; trusted append has debug assertions only. ByteUnpacker requires external width1/2/4/8 and panics on an incomplete last integer; there is no zero-width decoder. Full-zip deliberately uses the Zero mode to omit repetition indices when repetition is absent. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/bytepack.rs:73-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6555-6607)

### Codec extension seam and errors

BufferCompressor is Debug+Send+Sync with compress/decompress/config. GeneralBufferCompressor creates feature-gated Zstd or LZ4 implementations, or a no-op copier; FSST is rejected because it has a separate path. Zstd initializes a reusable compression context lazily in OnceLock<Result<Mutex<_>,String>>: failure is cached and poisoning can panic. Compression is serialized on that mutex, while decompression creates no shared context here. Every implementation appends to output; failures after resizing/appending do not roll it back. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:141-432)

CompressionConfig::default is always Lz4,Some(0). CompressedBufferEncoder::default instead chooses Zstd,Some(0), otherwise Lz4,None, otherwise None,None according to features. A no-op buffer codec can work yet fail to build structural General metadata because pb21 conversion permits only LZ4/Zstd. A feature-disabled request returns an explicit InvalidInput; a Zstd factory success may still fail at lazy context initialization. These defaults and errors are distinct API contracts. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:65-110; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:183-200; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:394-509; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:406-431)

Whole-block compression preserves selected configuration, including level presence, in the descriptor. Per-value compression uses runtime config, which normalizes absent Zstd level to Some(0) and discards LZ4 level. GeneralBlockDecompressor composes any recursively selected inner decoder; CompressedBufferEncoder's own BlockDecompressor always delegates to BinaryBlockDecompressor and is only the variable-block convenience path. Do not decode arbitrary fixed-width output with that convenience implementation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:433-675; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1213-1231)

Per-value helpers require valid monotone in-bounds offsets and representable cumulative output offsets. They append into caller storage but start the returned offsets at zero, so ordinary standalone output requires an initially empty destination. Unsupported bit widths panic in typed adapters. No file IO, async cancellation, allocation cap or numeric version check is implemented by these codecs. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:512-677)

## Buffer ownership, chunk framing and general mini-block composition

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs.md): Public Arrow-backed owned byte-buffer abstraction, typed views, byte slicing, concatenation, raw-pointer interleaving and owned iteration. Alignment, ownership and unsafe preconditions are separate contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs.md): Full-zip value-compression extension trait and fixed/variable owned result union; no concrete compression or file-version dispatch.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs.md): Parent-module-visible lazy automatic sparse-candidate selector. Eligibility is based on an optional explicit setting and dense rep/def budget, not directly on format version.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs.md): Mini-block page/chunk records, owned compression trait and process-wide maximum-value policy. Records describe framing but do not enforce their invariants.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs.md): Metadata-only constant/all-null decompressor with distinct whole-block and fixed-per-value input contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs.md): Outer general-purpose compression of the first mini-block buffer, accepted only for an aggregate size improvement; decoder unwraps that first buffer before inner dispatch.

### Buffer ownership and unsafe preconditions

LanceBuffer owns Arrow Buffer storage. Consuming conversion, cloning and valid byte slicing preserve shared ownership; deep_copy and ordinary concat allocate/copy. concat_into_one preserves a singleton allocation. reinterpret_vec preserves the typed allocation through Arrow; reinterpret_slice retains Arc ownership through custom allocation. No conversion byte-swaps; the crate rejects big-endian targets. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:12-60; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:111-142; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:205-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:283-295; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:11-16)

borrow_to_typed_slice returns an owning ScalarBuffer, sharing only when aligned. borrow_to_typed_view returns Cow, borrowing only when aligned and otherwise copying. Both panic on nondivisible byte lengths. from_bytes conditionally copies on misalignment, but its Vec<u8> branch does not explicitly request the supplied alignment; typed access checks again. Width0 is not rejected and reaches problematic arithmetic/alignment. as_spaced_hex(0) divides by zero. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:62-109; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:144-203; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:8-17)

zip_into_one is a safe API containing unchecked raw copies. It validates bit-width divisibility by8, but not source length, sums, multiplication or usize conversion. Correct execution requires every buffer contain at least num_values*width bytes and all arithmetic/addressing fit. Malformed inputs can produce out-of-bounds raw access; this is a source-derived safety finding, not a reproduced failure. Its older packed-struct caller only debug-checks equal field counts in the inspected slice. Do not extend that frozen path while designing new format features. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:226-260; rust/lance-encoding/src/array_encoding/physical/packed_struct.rs:172-249; AGENTS.md:15-20)

### Chunk representation and layout selection

PerValueCompressor promises independent value decoding and returns Fixed or Variable data plus descriptor; variable size includes offsets. MiniBlockCompressor promises chunk-level decoding, nonfinal power-of-two counts and owned parallel buffers. These traits/records do not enforce metadata/data agreement. MiniBlockChunk log0 means total minus previous; otherwise1<<log, with unchecked subtraction/shift and no final-position check. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs:20-54; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:214-217; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:972-975; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:45-144)

MAX_MINIBLOCK_BYTES=8186 concerns value data. LANCE_MINIBLOCK_MAX_VALUES defaults4096, accepts integer input then clamps1..32768 and is cached once by LazyLock. Non-power-of-two inputs are retained. Rep/def budgeting separately computes min(131072/bits_per_level,65535); zero is invalid and huge widths can yield0. The private fields of MiniBlockCompressionContext are stored by new but repository lexical search found no field reads, so their names are not evidence of active enforcement. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-78; [lexical reference inventory](../analysis/iteration-073-lexical-use-sites.json))

Automatic sparse selection is lazy: any explicit setting suppresses it; only RequiresPageSplit or SingleRowOverBudget invokes the candidate. WithinBudget avoids work. The helper has no format-version argument: v2.2 composition installs rejection and dense_u32; v2.3 installs sparse planning then constant and dense_u32. Sparse planning returns dense fallback for unsupported values or preparation errors; planning errors still propagate. Explicit sparse follows a separate branch. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs:8-24; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:121-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:129-139; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7802-7877)

### Metadata-only and outer-compression decode

ConstantDecompressor whole-block mode requires absent payload, including rejecting Some(empty); scalarNone returns AllNull and scalarSome returns compact Constant with caller count. Fixed-per-value mode ignores the supplied block and uses the separate count. Some(empty) is distinct from None despite both reporting width0. These outputs do not allocate one scalar copy per value. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs:14-62; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:934-960)

GeneralMiniBlockCompressor first runs inner compression, then skips outer work when there is no buffer or first-buffer length<4096. Otherwise it compresses each first-buffer chunk independently; only aggregate strict savings are accepted. Remaining buffers move unchanged, sizes[0] are rewritten, count/logs retained and selected configuration wraps inner metadata. Missing sizes, invalid slices or arithmetic overflow are not converted to validation errors. Factory/config failures may be hidden by early fallback. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs:20-115)

GeneralMiniBlockDecompressor reconstructs the outer codec on each call, expands buffer0 and delegates with all remaining buffers and unchanged count. It expects an already separated chunk; the enclosing descriptor strategy recursively creates the inner decoder. decoded_size_bytes delegates to inner. Codec feature availability remains a factory-time concern; neither wrapper constructor validates it.
