## Compressive grammar: required children versus unchecked attributes

Across V2_1/2/3, Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant compression variants succeed without inspecting widths, optional buffer-compression descriptors, literal bytes or other fields. Variable requires offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking, Fsst, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and PackedStruct require values. Dictionary validates indices first, then items. Each required child is recursively validated; missing compression oneof is InvalidInput. General does not require a compression descriptor here; cardinalities, dimensions, schemes, levels and numeric bounds are not generally checked by these visitors. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:18-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:18-106; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:18-89)

V2_1/V2_2 RLE require direct Flat values of8/16/32/64bits with data=None and direct Flat8 run lengths with data=None. They reject wrappers, 128-bit values and any present Flat.data buffer-compression descriptor, including a default descriptor. Flat.data is metadata, not a byte payload (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:419-425). V2_3 instead recursively validates both child trees with the full grammar; it imposes no special Flat8 requirement. V2_1 rejects VariablePackedStruct outright. V2_2/V2_3 validate each packed field.value recursively and accept an empty field list at this gate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:56-98; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:56-104; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:56-87)

These are local structural acceptance checks, not proof accepted data will decode. Recursive visitors and Blob-layout nesting have no explicit local depth limit; protobuf decoder restrictions are a separate, still unqualified boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199)

## Page-layout matrix

| Layout | V2_1 | V2_2 | V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniBlock | has_large_chunk must be false | must be true | must be true |
| FullZip | required value compression | same | same |
| Constant | inline_value absent; rep/def compression absent | validate optional rep/def; inline value unchecked | same as V2_2 |
| Blob | required recursively validated inner layout | same, exact2.2 grammar | same, exact2.3 grammar |
| Sparse | rejected | rejected | large-chunk and selective nested checks |
| Missing layout | InvalidInput | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |

MiniBlock checks large-chunk flag first, then optional repetition, optional definition, required value and optional dictionary encodings. This is an exact grammar boundary; selecting a newer reader does not mean it accepts the prior miniblock flag. V2_1 can read all-null ConstantLayout even though its composition page list has no constant() mechanism. Read acceptance and writer policy must be documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:102-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:108-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:148-199; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134)

V2_3 Sparse requires has_large_chunk and value_compression. Positions are validated only when Explicit; missing sets, missing oneofs and other variants pass here. Validity delegates optional positions. List layers inspect nonempty positions, explicit counts and optional validity; FixedSizeList layers inspect optional validity only. A missing structural layer arm errors, but zero layers pass. Slot totals, ordering, ranges, dimensions and actual buffers are not checked by this visitor. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:91-146)

## Projection differences

V2_0 consumes a header column for every ordinary parent and then its children. Blob/packed fields are opaque. Schema-name selection computes the original whole-schema ID map before pruning, preserving original file indices. Missing mappings are silently omitted; complete schema is still retained. V2_1+ projection wrappers use the shared leaf algorithm with original schema mapping. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:177-232; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:193-213; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:195-215; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:233-253)

For V2_0, a comparable struct's child lengths must match its own header length; the error text about children also covers header/child mismatch. For nonstruct containers, child comparisons become disabled below that node, but the returned length remains the parent header length. The shared leaf algorithm instead derives a container's length from its first child. Both reject too few indices; production helpers reject surplus indices and require equal top-level normalized lengths. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:234-310; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:278-357)

V2_0 prepare_projection accepts Full metadata after normal projection validity checks and clones metadata/projection, ignoring IO/cache. Indexed input gets structural validity errors first, then unconditional NotSupported. Its ReadProjection trait method awaits this no-IO preparation and then computes length. Accepting a V2_0 metadata index in finish_metadata_index does not imply indexed loading is usable. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:150-175; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:312-348; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:384-395)

## Local tests and change surface

V2_0 test_projection_length omits production's surplus-index check. V2_1 test helper delegates the shared version, which includes that check. Neither helper is a test case. The V2_1 single grammar test places empty VariablePackedStruct under General then FullZip and checks rejection text. V2_2 rejects a nested RLE using Flat16 run lengths; V2_3 accepts the same shape. These last names mention variable width, but construct fixed-width Flat children, not a Variable node. Tests inspect grammar only, no file bytes or decompression; rejection tests do not assert error variant. No sparse validation fixture appears in the V2_3 file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:397-415; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:260-304; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:262-308; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:300-341)

Changing nested grammar requires visiting every location that can contain a compressive child, including dictionary indices/items, optional level encodings, packed fields and explicit sparse sets. Keep read acceptance separate from the version writer cascade and maintain all stable contracts. These readers expose no plugin registration seam or environment configuration; ordinary module/trait composition is the extension boundary. ## Schema reconstruction and persistence conversion

Fields(pub Vec<pb::Field>) and FieldsWithMeta{fields:Fields,metadata:HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>} are public. From<&Field> recursively flattens parent then children; From<&Schema> concatenates root subtrees. They preserve supplied IDs/parent IDs and do not validate or assign them. TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema reconstructs iteratively and supplies empty schema metadata; TryFrom<FieldsWithMeta> adds lossily decoded metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:95-129; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:157-314)

```text
protobuf list, parents before children
|-- arena: childless Field + child node indices
|-- ID map: unique ID -> node; duplicate ID -> ambiguous
|   '-- ambiguous parent -> first pre-order DFS match
|-- reverse arena order: take children into parent
'-- roots in input order -> Schema(fields, empty metadata)
    '-- FieldsWithMeta adds the converted schema metadata
```

Unique IDs use expected-linear hash lookups; ambiguous references allocate a DFS stack and may lead to quadratic work. Parent-before-child is enforced, strict flat pre-order is not. Historical duplicates are intentionally retained: a nested duplicate under an earlier root can win over a root encountered earlier in the flat list. Missing parents produce Schema errors with name/IDs; internal arena failures are Internal. No Schema::validate or key/type check follows. Iterative reconstruction does not make recursive flattening or Field destruction stack-safe. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:102-245; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:502-520)

Field metadata bytes are decoded with UTF-8 replacement; nonempty dedicated extension_name overrides its metadata key. Unknown numeric encodings become None; encoding numbers1..4 map Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary/RLE, and encoding writes None as0. The legacy field-kind number is ignored on read and forced0 on write. Primary presence uses positive position or legacy bool->Some(0); clustering uses positive position only and writes its legacy bool=false. Dictionary i64 locations cast unchecked to usize and back; loaded dictionary values are discarded. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:11-94; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:316-344)

Minimal local conversion example, derived from the source doctest (not compiled here):

```rust
use lance_core::datatypes::Schema;
use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};
fn decode_root() -> lance_core::Result<Schema> {
    Schema::try_from(&Fields(vec![pb::Field {
        id: 0,
        parent_id: -1,
        name: "value".to_owned(),
        logical_type: "int32".to_owned(),
        ..Default::default()
    }]))
}
```

The example only establishes reconstruction; it does not validate a complete dataset schema. The source metadata roundtrip unit test uses Schema equality, which ignores top-level metadata, so that test alone cannot prove metadata preservation. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:139-156; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:394-410; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878)

## Encoding IO and retained memory

LanceEncodingsIo is public through the crate reexport. It owns a FileScheduler and starts with an8MiB read chunk target; the consuming setter accepts zero without validation. EncodingsIo promises one Bytes per input range including empties. This adapter preserves empty positions and original order, delegates priority unchanged to FileScheduler and always returns Some for optional bypass/stats handles. Stats replaces the extra recorder on a cloned scheduler; it does not reopen the file. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:16-17; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:12-50; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:40-104; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1336-1352)

For a range of length n>limit, generate k=ceil(n/limit) chunks: k-1 chunks of floor(n/k), then a final remainder. This is a target, not a strict cap: n=10,limit=3 yields2,2,2,4. Zero limit divides by zero for nonempty requests; reversed bounds subtract unchecked. No sort/dedup occurs. FileScheduler checks actual split start order, coalesces nearby requests and can split again, so this adapter does not determine physical IOP size. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:51-98; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264)

Scheduler submission occurs before returning the adapter's boxed async block, including for an empty split list. Await errors propagate; result-count mismatch is Internal. Unsplit requests return the scheduler Vec directly. Reassembly groups returned Bytes per original request, inserts empty Bytes, cheaply clones single chunks and allocates/copies multiple chunks. It does not verify individual result lengths; retained source chunks overlap the combined allocation. Scheduler queue/cancellation lifetime remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:98-148)

## Exact-version dispatch matrix

Every dispatch takes ConcreteFileVersion; callers resolve Stable/Next separately. There is no ordered comparison or implicit nearest-version fallback. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:4-48)

| Operation family | V1 | V2_0 | V2_1, V2_2, V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field/name/whole-schema projections, physical counts and data-file column mapping | Own v1 module | Own module | Each own module |
| Current read projection / finish raw metadata | Internal | Own module | Each own module |
| Finish metadata index | VersionConflict(0,2) | Own module | Each own module |
| Decode embedded column metadata | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |
| Validate global buffers | Successful no-op | Own module | Each own module |
| Copy external column | NotSupported, closure unused | Conditional callback | Always await callback |
| Finalize copied pages | NotSupported | Normalize pages | Successful no-op |
| Open projected reader | NotSupported | Full opener only | Eligible indexed attempt, then full on None |
| Create current/lazy writer; encode embedded/mini batch | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |

Matrix evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:38-277; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:285-401. Per-version byte grammars and concrete mechanisms are not inferred from this routing table.

External metadata validation checks whole-schema physical count, projection validity, sequential column.index values, then delegates rectangularity/normalized row count to the exact read projection. Indexed reader opening requires preference plus structural eligibility; an indexed error propagates, while None falls back. V2_0 never invokes the indexed closure. Self-described opening delegates optimistic-tail detection; OpenedFileReader::V1 only retains footer numbers, while Current owns FileReader. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:50-107; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:279-326; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1555)

## Writer facade and diagnostics

FileWriter stores one boxed exact V2 writer. FileWriterOptions defaults all three Option fields to None; its local validator rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0). The Arrow C-interface retention warning is documentation; current structural resolution uses 8 MiB per top-level field or a divided supplied budget, explicit max-page size before environment/default32 MiB, and keep_original_array=false. V2_0 uses the same local option resolution formulas (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-356). (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-439) PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 and LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES are declared here but used by concrete writers. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-77)

write_batches awaits batches sequentially, stops at first error and does not roll back earlier effects. External-column initialization converts every ColumnInfo to protobuf first: both page encoding forms and column encoding become serialized prost Any in DirectEncoding; descriptor pairs unzip in order, page row counts/priorities persist, ColumnInfo.index is omitted. Only then is the concrete initializer called. The facade does not establish schema/column or state consistency. finish returns FileWriteSummary{num_rows,size_bytes}; abort returns unit; tell reports delegated position. Their durability/cleanup guarantees require concrete analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:79-115; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:160-289)

ExpectedTypes is effectively crate-internal despite pub declarations in its private module. It converts expected core fields to Arrow once, remembers the last successful SchemaRef, and compares schemas by value equality. It matches expected columns by name (same-position fast path, name-search fallback); absent fields and extras are outside this checker. It does not inspect array values/nulls. A failed check leaves the prior accepted schema cached. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-21; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:67-114)

The recursive checker compares extension name/metadata when enabled, pairs Struct/List/LargeList/Map/FixedSizeList children by position, ignores names/nullability in those arms and ignores Map sortedness. Blob-v2 Struct/Struct short-circuits child validation after the extension gate; the blob encoder is responsible for descriptor checks. Utf8<-Utf8View and Binary<-BinaryView are directional exceptions. Other types use exact DataType equality, potentially including stricter embedded-field equality. Bare column writes skip only the top-level extension comparison; nested children still compare extensions. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:115-193)

FieldTypeMismatch is publicly reexported and downcastable through Error::InvalidInput source. It retains expected/actual FieldRef and a path constructed from expected names. Dot separators are unescaped. Display prints type plus extension; metadata without an extension name prints as no extension even though comparison can reject it. Contextual concrete writers call type checks before encoder preparation/nullability checks; invalid bare column indices are guarded there rather than in ExpectedTypes::check_column. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:21-65; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:120-193; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-630; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:663-689; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:458-477; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:544-572)

## Responsibility and ownership

FileReader owns a DecodeEngine plus Arc<CachedFileMetadata>, exposing synchronous metadata/statistics and asynchronous or blocking reads. ProjectedFileReader owns only the engine and can use Full or Indexed metadata. ReadProjection is the crate-private version-selected behavior seam for indexed validation, normalized length and asynchronous preparation. EncodingsIo, decoder plugins and LanceCache are shared Arcs; scheduling/decoding algorithms are delegated. There is no explicit spawning, cancellation guard or unsafe block in the production portion of this file. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:392-455; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1166-1417; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1680-1940)

```text
FileScheduler
|-- tail + footer + GBO -> full schema + all CMO/protobuf columns
|   `-- exact finish_metadata -> FileReader / Full provider
`-- tail + footer + GBO + schema-or-known-schema + CMO
    `-- exact finish_metadata_index -> ProjectedFileReader / Indexed provider
        `-- requested column metadata: cache hits + sorted missing ranges
            `-- exact decode_column -> compacted prepared projection

requested projection -> exact ReadProjection.prepare -> selected read length
`-- row bounds -> RequestedRows + SchedulerDecoderConfig
    |-- async schedule_and_decode -> ReadBatchTask stream -> ordered buffered futures
    `-- blocking schedule_and_decode_blocking -> RecordBatchReader
```

These are the local call routes; “one submitted request” does not establish one backend IO, and task-stream lifetime is implemented by the delegated decoder. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:954-1115; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1620-1677; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1948-2283; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:393-431)

## Metadata loading and byte layout

The initial read awaits object size and requests at most the reader's last block at priority0. Footer decoding requires40 bytes and reads LEu64 column-metadata start, CMO start and GBO start; LEu32 global-buffer/column counts; LEu16 major/minor; then four MAGIC bytes. It checks length and magic, not offset ordering or the version. The invalid-magic diagnostic prints the expected magic. Dispatch parses exact identity and can return legacy tags before decoding current metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:691-700; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-792; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:954-967)

GBO decoding may extend the tail backward, parses declared LE(position,size) pairs, invokes exact-version global validation and checked-ranges every descriptor against actual file length. At least one descriptor is required; buffer0 supplies the schema. FileDescriptor.schema is unwrapped, so a missing schema can panic. CMO entries require exact16-byte-per-column table length and checked position+length within the column-metadata region; overlapping, unsorted and zero-length entries are not explicitly rejected. Footer-order arithmetic and several Bytes slices remain unchecked. These are source-derived malformed-input concerns, not reproduced crashes. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:795-953; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:969-996)

Full loading expands back to schema, decodes all column protobufs, and passes raw values into exact-version finish_metadata. Its accounting fields are overlapping, not disjoint sections: num_footer_bytes=file_size-schema_start; num_global_buffer_bytes=sum(descriptor.size); num_data_bytes=column_meta_start-global_sum; num_column_metadata_bytes=GBOstart-column_meta_start, including CMO. Actual file_size_bytes remains the authoritative store-reported size. The footer-byte and column-statistics field comments overstate or misdescribe these formulas. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:120-167; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:978-1028)

Indexed loading fetches schema only when no caller-supplied (Arc<Schema>,u64 rows) is present, and fetches the exact CMO interval. Supplied schema/row count is trusted, even though GBO must still exist and pass descriptor checks. It does not decode per-column metadata at open. The initial tail may incidentally contain schema/column bytes; avoiding a dedicated fetch is not proof those bytes were never read. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1031-1115; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:2067-2080)

## Cache identity, retention and statistics

Reader factories prefix the supplied cache with path text. Column metadata keys then encode only the physical u32 column index under schema(lance.file.column-metadata-key,1), diagnostic type ColumnMetadata. The caller's parent namespace must supply any store/authority isolation. Injecting a new scheduler preserves cache and metadata with no identity check. FileReader::try_open itself always loads raw metadata; it does not consult a whole-file metadata cache first. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:253-276; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1701-1711; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1976-2049; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:2186-2257)

Indexed prepare checks keys in projection order, sorts missing ranges by file offset, submits them together, decodes through the exact-version callback and caches each result. It restores projection order before returning. Fewer IO results cause an Internal missing-column error, extra results are ignored by zip, and earlier cache inserts survive a later error. No single-flight load or rollback occurs locally. Current LanceEncodingsIo separately checks its range-chunk result cardinality; custom EncodingsIo remains a trust boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1597-1677; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:102-147)

Only user globals fully inside the original tail window are copied into retained_global_buffers; index0 is excluded. The public global-buffer API still permits index0, validates index, returns retained bytes without IO, or submits one checked range and takes the first returned Bytes. Fallback bytes are not cached here; no response-length assertion is added. Copying retained bytes permits the larger tail allocation to drop. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:718-738; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1721-1751)

CachedFileMetadata deep sizing uses4*protobuf encoded length plus inline slice size, schema/normalized-info/retained-map children. Iterating only descriptor child sizes omits the file_buffers vector backing allocation. CachedColumnMetadata also adds inline protobuf slice size through the shared estimate. These are estimates, not allocation measurements. File statistics sums only page.buffer_sizes and counts pages, excluding serialized metadata, column buffers, padding, globals and footer despite the public size_bytes comment. Indexed provider statistics returns None without eager loading. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:170-209; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:240-251; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:659-685; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1532-1540)

## Projection and row-selection contracts

ReaderProjection pairs requested schema with physical indices. Full/indexed basic validation rejects empty roots, duplicate indices and out-of-bounds columns, but not schema/index count mismatch or type disagreement. Indexed shape eligibility recursively counts childless fields, rejects blob/packed nodes and checks total matches index count. Preference additionally requires four times selected count strictly less than total, with saturating multiplication; it is not a version-capability check. Direct projected open does not apply that selectivity threshold or fall back to full loading. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:284-362; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:512-532; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1595; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:2159-2219)

The ProjectedFileReader type comment promises later projections remain within the base, but read_tasks simply uses the base as a default. It never compares a supplied projection against the base, and exact structural prepare receives only the requested projection plus whole provider. Likewise schema() and num_rows() return provider file-level values, not projected schema/normalized length. Treat base-subset enforcement as absent at this local boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:438-448; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1713-1719; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1888-1940; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:2263-2283; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:393-431)

Normalized column lengths checked-sum page counts, replacing sparse page counts with first structural layer num_slots when present. verify_uniform_lengths requires complete selected roots to agree even for a short common-prefix request. Public column_num_rows instead sums raw protobuf page.length with ordinary arithmetic. Preserve these three distinct values: file descriptor row count, raw physical-column count and normalized projection length. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:539-577; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:628-653; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:274-357)

| Request | Local validation | Filter passed to decoder |
|---|---|---|
| Indices | Reject null; every value<selected length; no local empty/order/dedup check | Async replaces with no_filter; blocking preserves caller filter |
| Range / Ranges | end<=selected length only; no local start<=end or overlap check | Preserved |
| RangeFrom | start<selected length, so start==EOF is rejected | Preserved |
| RangeTo | end<=selected length | Preserved |
| RangeFull |0..selected length, including0..0 | Preserved |

Both paths cast/copy selections before calling decoder scheduling APIs. Multi-range helper ordinary-sums end-start; debug-enabled take/range logging indexes first/last without empty guards. Downstream may impose additional contracts, but those pending algorithms must not be inferred here. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1211-1377; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1419-1482; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1776-1885)

FileReaderOptions defaults to8MiB read chunks, DecoderConfig::default() and no byte target. Reader-created LanceEncodingsIo receives the chunk option; already-injected EncodingsIo is used unchanged. Row batch size and optional approximate byte target pass into SchedulerDecoderConfig without local positivity checks. Ordered buffered futures preserve task order and use caller readahead with no local nonzero check. with_io_stats replaces IO only when the scheduler supports scoped instrumentation. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:364-390; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:457-468; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:611-626; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1189-1208; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1997-2047)

## Embedded formats and diagnostics

EncodedBatchReaderExt supports external-schema mini and self-described input. Both retain complete Bytes, decode columns by exact version, derive projection, and obtain num_rows by summing the first column's page.num_rows, or0. Self-described mode discards FileDescriptor.length; neither normalizes sparse slots nor requires uniform root lengths. Mini mode does not validate GBO/schema. Direct slices can panic for bad offsets; describe_encoding can panic on malformed outer Any despite returning String. Its recognized URLs are /lance.encodings.ArrayEncoding and /lance.encodings21.PageLayout; inner decode failure becomes text. (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:2286-2422)

## Ownership and initialization

Each public concrete Writer privately owns a StructuralFileSink, EncodingPipeline and CompressionParams. Its exact parent supplies encoding_strategy; the shared components do not select a version. Eager construction creates the same lazy object and initializes it before returning. Lazy construction only stores inputs. Initialization validates explicit options, computes runtime encoding options, validates schema, constructs BatchEncoder, then moves its encoders/mapping into the pipeline and initializes sink columns. The first write_batch infers a missing schema from Arrow, including for an empty batch. write_column only requires an already stored schema; it never infers one from a bare array. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:442-458; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-683)

```text
exact Writer
|-- CompressionParams -> exact field/page/compression strategy
|-- EncodingPipeline
|   |-- schema + ExpectedTypes + schema metadata
|   |-- field encoders + field-ID/physical-column mapping
|   '-- per-field row counts + maximum/aggregate row count
'-- StructuralFileSink
    |-- ObjectWriter + column metadata + user-global descriptors
    '-- optional page spill: Pending -> Active sidecar/chunk lists
```

These are ordinary owned fields with no local mutex, task spawn or Drop implementation. Both sink and pipeline expose crate-internal mechanisms that assume the wrapper maintains their relationship; they do not encode lifecycle state in the type system. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:50-58; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:132-177; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:381-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:32-36)

## Runtime options and validation

| Input | Actual local resolution |
|---|---|
| data_cache_bytes absent | 8 MiB per top-level field |
| data_cache_bytes present | integer division by top-level schema field count; remainder dropped |
| max_page_bytes present | supplied value; explicit Some(0) rejected before initialization |
| max_page_bytes absent | parse LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES as untrimmed u64; otherwise 32 MiB |
| invalid environment value | warning and 32 MiB; missing/non-Unicode value silently uses default |
| environment value 0 | accepted by this resolver; it is outside explicit-option validation |
| keep_original_array absent | false, distinct from EncodingOptions::default's true |
| buffer_alignment | 64 bytes |

The budget is divided by logical top-level fields even though one field may map to multiple physical columns. A supplied cache budget and zero top-level fields divide by zero before the wrapper reaches schema.validate. These are local formulas, not measured peak-memory bounds. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:410-439; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:78-84; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:277-285; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:332-365)

ExpectedTypes validates written fields by name, and encode_batch also selects by name; nullability instead zips batch columns against schema fields positionally. A reordered batch can therefore have nulls judged against another field's nullable flag. Recursive validation uses logical_nulls, intersects struct validity with inherited reachability, and ignores child nulls under a null struct parent. Nonstruct child-data recursion resets reachability and checks all exposed child slots; zip does not enforce equal child counts. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:87-128; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:461-543; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:570-595)

## Batch and column mutation order

For write_batch: verify types/nullability; return for zero rows; reject a single batch longer than u32::MAX; collect all name-selected fields; call each encoder with its old field row number and a fresh RepDefBuilder; write out-of-line buffers; check aggregate u64 addition; advance every field counter and aggregate; await ordered page tasks and writer flush. The overflow check is after encoder mutation and possible buffer writes. A page or flush error leaves counters advanced. There is no rollback transaction around the batch. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-650)

write_column checks schema/index and the single array's u32 limit, then type/nullability and empty input. It encodes only that field, writes external buffers, performs unchecked per-field addition, and updates aggregate rows with max before awaiting pages. Unequal field lengths are supported locally; finish does not require equality. A contextual test writes lengths five and one, then expects a single-column projection to read one row and a joint projection to fail. That test covers V2_0/V2_1 and has not been executed here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-703; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/writer_tests.rs:1084-1176)

FuturesOrdered preserves task output order; the sink writes one returned page at a time and stops at the first task/page error. Dropping remaining futures is visible here, but cancellation of any work they may have spawned is not established. The final flush comment describes observing already-failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend durability remains outside this analyzed scope. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:247-259)

## Alignment and metadata boundaries

Ordinary page, batch external, column and user-global buffers receive trailing padding of byte 0x48 to round their **length** to 64. This does not repair a misaligned starting position. write_external_buffer instead inserts leading zero padding based on current position and writes payload without trailing padding. Its returned start is aligned, but its end can leave the next ordinary buffer misaligned. Descriptors record payload lengths excluding padding. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:41-45; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:187-229; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:262-284; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Two finish-path assumptions are explicit in the source. First, finish_encoders writes out-of-line buffers raw, while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding without modifying the payload. Second, column-buffer recording advances a local position by payload length while actual writes include trailing padding. Producers supplying multiple unaligned buffers would violate these recorded-position assumptions. This is a source-level deduction, not a reproduced failure or a claim that current producers emit that shape. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-765; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

Page metadata is constructed after its payload IO. Both Legacy and Structural descriptions are Any-wrapped into Direct encoding without exact grammar validation; length is encoded_page.num_rows and priority is row_number. The version reader later owns grammar acceptance. External metadata initialization replaces sink metadata and pipeline schema/declared rows without validating or resetting encoders, mapping, expected types or field counters. This path requires coherent caller-managed state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:179-185; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:206-244; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:783-788; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:135-145)

## Page metadata spill

Configuring spill only stores Pending. The next write_page first writes payload bytes, then takes Pending and creates the sidecar. Creation failure/cancellation leaves no pending spill state in the sink. The sidecar encodes length-delimited Page messages into per-column buffers; each threshold is max(256 KiB / max(columns,1),64). A single page can overshoot, Vec clear retains capacity, and chunk descriptors keep growing. This is not a strict aggregate memory cap. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:47-112; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:170-172; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:231-243)

Finish takes all metadata/spill state, flushes and shuts down the sidecar, opens it, reads each column's chunks sequentially and reconstructs the entire page Vec for that column before serializing it. Existing metadata.pages are replaced, so enabling spill after pages have accumulated does not preserve them through this path. No local sidecar deletion occurs on success or failure. Errors after taking state do not restore it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340)

## Finish ordering and exact footer

All three wrappers perform the same sequence: flush buffered encoder pages; consume and finish field encoders; merge schema metadata and unload blob fields; write descriptor raw; serialize column metadata; write column offset table; write global offset table; append footer; shutdown object writer. The returned row count comes from pipeline accounting and size comes from shutdown. A never-initialized lazy writer reaches descriptor creation only after the empty flush path, then errors because schema is unknown. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:705-801)

Offset tables have no prefix: each entry is (position:u64 LE,length:u64 LE). The global table starts with descriptor entry0, then user globals in insertion order, even though their payloads were written earlier. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf messages located by these tables; neither receives a length prefix or alignment padding here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:279-309; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:343-350)

| Bytes relative to footer start | Value |
|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata region start, u64 LE |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, u64 LE |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, u64 LE |
| 24–27 | number of global buffers, u32 LE |
| 28–31 | number of physical columns, u32 LE |
| 32–33 | major version 2, u16 LE |
| 34–35 | exact minor 1, 2 or 3, u16 LE |
| 36–39 | ASCII LANC |

The footer is 40 bytes, with no checksum or count-range validation in these wrappers. The three minor literals are owned by their respective concrete writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:33-33)

concat_lance_footer copies batch.data and appends an optional descriptor, per-column metadata and both offset tables before that same exact footer. It preserves supplied page/column offsets, ignores ColumnInfo.index and batch.top_level_columns, and does not check alignment, exact page grammar or buffer bounds. In mini mode the global table is empty. In self-described mode it clones the existing core Schema; unlike pipeline descriptor creation, it does not unload blobs or validate that schema. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:813-921; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:922-927; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:204-224)

## Errors, ownership and change consequences

finish is mutable rather than consuming, but is not made idempotent: field encoders and metadata are taken, schema metadata is drained, footer writes can partially succeed, and no finished flag guards another call. Each public abort(&mut self) is an empty async body. It does not drop the object writer; its comment about multipart cleanup on drop is not an implementation of abort. Backend cleanup behavior must be established separately before callers rely on it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-191)

Private indexing/unwrap assumptions require schema, encoders, counts and physical columns to stay coherent. The final physical-column mismatch uses an unconditional panic; per-encoder counts use a debug assertion. No equal-field-length assertion is added. A new mechanism must preserve output count/order, address/padding correspondence and caller row accounting, and must not assume errors rewind state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-568; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-649; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:697-701; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-776)

## Local tests and usage

Four helper-level tests cover hidden child null acceptance, visible child null rejection, dictionary logical-null rejection, and sliced-parent mask alignment. The two rejection cases inspect field-name text rather than Error variants. They do not test persistence, IO, spill, abort, overflow, footer bytes or reordered batch validation. Compatibility test/generator sources are now covered separately; writer_tests.rs is now fully analyzed in the [writer-test catalog](archive/rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md), with its distinct integration oracles and limits. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:924-1025)

The following example uses the reviewed V2_2 API and was not compiled or executed:

```rust
use arrow_array::RecordBatch;
use lance_core::{Result, datatypes::Schema};
use lance_file::{versions::v2_2, writer::{FileWriteSummary, FileWriterOptions}};
use lance_io::traits::Writer as ObjectWriter;

async fn write_batches(
    output: Box<dyn ObjectWriter>,
    schema: Schema,
    batches: &[RecordBatch],
) -> Result<FileWriteSummary> {
    let mut writer = v2_2::Writer::try_new(output, schema, FileWriterOptions::default())?;
    writer.write_batches(batches.iter()).await?;
    writer.finish().await
}
```

Construction, ordered borrowed batches and finish signatures are defined at rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:39-58, rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:101-115 and rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-186. The caller still owns Dataset publication and failure cleanup.

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. ## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. ## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. The complete reader is now covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), including sorted grouping, selector differences, cache assumptions and constructor validation limits. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Two metadata tests assert one index-group example and four valid range splits. Three page-table tests assert set/get, missing-cell zeros after write/read and three error variants/messages. The roundtrip test starts expected from actual.clone and overwrites fourteen holes; six populated values lack independent expectations. No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. Dependencies are core Schema/Field/error/DeepSizeOf, file protobuf/schema adapters, Arrow arrays/builders/type predicates, IO Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct/ReadBatchParams, Tokio write extension and async-recursion. No local feature flag, environment variable or global mutable cache is declared. Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct are existing boundaries; these five files introduce no new extensible trait. Preserve historical behavior under the repository's frozen legacy policy, and use released historical fixtures for any explicitly required legacy repair. ## Ownership and opening

FileReader shares its Reader, Metadata, ordinary PageTable and optional statistics PageTable through Arcs, while owning the supplied Schema. Clone retains shared underlying dictionary arrays through Schema's Clone behavior. object_reader is public and can be replaced without refreshing stored metadata. fragment_id is retained for Debug; this file does not generate row IDs. There is no custom Drop or shutdown protocol. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:41-66)

~~~text
try_new(store, path, supplied_schema)
`-- try_new_with_fragment_id(fragment=0, min=0, max=schema.max_id, cache=None)
    |-- ObjectStore.open
    |-- read_metadata
    `-- try_new_from_reader(metadata=Some)
        |-- ordinary PageTable load/cache using supplied path and bounds
        `-- statistics PageTable load/cache using Reader.path/stats
            `-- read_metadata again unless cache serves it
~~~

The two table futures are polled concurrently with try_join. Supplied metadata is trusted for ordinary-table loading; the statistics loader independently obtains metadata from the reader. Without a cache, ordinary construction reads metadata twice. The separate path, reader path, metadata, schema and field bounds are not reconciled. An error returns before construction; no rollback or explicit abort guard is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:139-208; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-294)

Every constructor here requires Schema. It neither discovers schema nor hydrates dictionary values, despite stale documentation about an optional manifest. Self-describing opening is a separate table-layer trait: it reads Metadata, requires manifest_position, reads Manifest, populates schema dictionaries, then calls try_new_from_reader. Dataset fragment opening supplies its schema and file field bounds; the full Dataset wrapper remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:126-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1154-1210; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:1374-1401)

## Cache and metadata contract

The private typed string key has stable schema `lance.file.previous.string-key`, version 1, and writes one string. Stable value IDs are `lance.file.previous.Metadata`, `lance.file.previous.PageTable` and `lance.file.previous.OptionalPageTable`; compiler type names are diagnostic only. The key contains no explicit schema, field bounds, fragment ID, object-store identity, ETag or file version. The supplied LanceCache may add a namespace; this local adapter adds no invalidation or persistent codec. Cached statistics absence is an Option value. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:68-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:181-198; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-288)

A cache miss reads the last min(file_size, block_size) bytes, extracts the eight-byte metadata position at footer[-16..-8], and either fetches the earlier framed struct or decodes its tail slice. That helper checks at least 16 tail bytes but does not check magic/version. Tail-position arithmetic and in-buffer framing do not locally guard malformed offsets/lengths; they can panic before decoding returns an error. Do not infer current-reader footer validation from this V1 path. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:210-234; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263)

Statistics opening loads one batch covering field IDs 0 through max(leaf_field_ids), panicking on an empty leaf-ID list. page_stats_schema matches requested data IDs against parsed statistics root names, then projects their IDs and immediate children. It retains schema order and can return Some(empty). read_page_stats returns None for absent table or empty projection; otherwise reads batch 0. A disagreement between caller metadata and the independently loaded statistics table can reach an unwrap. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-267; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:398-445)

## Read APIs and scheduling

The method and free read_batch use the explicit per-call schema, rather than the stored reader schema promised by the method comment. Empty projection returns InvalidInput; the free-function comment about a with_row_id flag and panic is obsolete. No upfront subset/type validation occurs. Root fields are read with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), and RecordBatch construction performs the final assembled-array check. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:324-335; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:485-507)

read_range immediately accepts any empty/reversed range as an empty batch, even beyond the end. Otherwise metadata splits across batches; reads are ordered and all results are retained. A single result is cloned; multiple results are concatenated in spawn_blocking. take first uses metadata grouping, which copies and sorts input, preserving duplicates but losing original order. It checks grouped batch IDs afterward, and its secondary offset check compares against whole-file length rather than batch length. Both APIs materialize the complete result; no local abort-on-drop mechanism is provided for blocking concat. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-194)

batches_stream lazily filters ascending batch IDs and requests complete batches with fixed outer concurrency 2. It owns reader/projection through Arcs and advertises the supplied Arrow schema. Inner field reads retain their own Reader parallelism. This function does not spawn a Tokio task; a separately inspected Dataset ranges_to_tasks wrapper does spawn per-range tasks. Do not merge their cancellation or scheduling contracts. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:448-483; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:158-186)

## Recursive reconstruction and edge cases

read_array dispatches by reconstructed DataType, not field.encoding: fixed stride first, then Null, the four byte-array types, Struct, Dictionary and the two variable-list widths. Unsupported types reach unimplemented. Every FSL enters fixed-stride dispatch regardless of its child; Interval has a width helper but is absent from that predicate. get_page_info reports missing field/batch entries as InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:509-576; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181)

| Type/path | Local reconstruction | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed stride | Page position/length and selector go to plain codec | No field-nullability bitmap passed |
| Binary/string | Same, plus field.nullable | Equal offsets become null only when nullable |
| Dictionary | Plain keys plus cloned loaded values Arc | Missing dictionary/values unwraps |
| Struct | Sequential recursive child reads | No parent page/validity restored |
| Null | Synthesize count, no payload IO | End/max checks differ from plain; reversed range can underflow; Ranges panics |
| List/LargeList | Read offsets, read child values, normalize and build | Parent validity absent; reconstructed child is item/nullable=true |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:559-808; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229.

List range offsets include the terminal endpoint. Direct empty Indices accesses first/last and panics; public empty FileReader.take avoids per-column reads because grouping yields no groups. List Indices reads the whole first-to-last offset span, then sequentially reads each selected child range and concatenates; duplicates repeat those reads. Its offset lookup uses reader.page_table even when the function received another table, while child recursion uses that argument. Null selector validity is ignored on list and Null paths. Sortedness, arithmetic, child existence and offset coherence are caller/file assumptions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:370-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:578-623; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-807)

The list constructor chooses a child field named item with nullable=true from actual child data type. It does not preserve arbitrary child metadata/name/nullability or parent nullness. Struct reconstruction similarly supplies no parent validity. These are frozen representation and reconstruction limits, not promises made by current-format readers. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:671-686; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:724-738; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:795-807; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Twelve active tests pin stable cache discriminator strings; seven-row multi-batch numeric/string/dictionary take; nullable empty-string conversion; combined-input struct/list roundtrip; one-row struct/list slice; Null lengths and weak is_err boundaries; List/LargeList take; sliced list equality plus file size<1000; one-batch numeric range; even-batch stream order; Boolean take with 256-byte blocks; and a narrow file opened under a wider schema with explicit field bounds. They do not prove malformed-file safety, cache invalidation, cancellation, parent-null preservation, arbitrary selectors or full multi-fragment behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:827-1562)

The Boolean test is active reader-level coverage: 5,000 modulo-5 bits, indices [2,4,5,8,4555], expected [false,false,true,false,true]. It supplements the commented-out codec-local test and does not assert actual IO request counts. The projection test writes only f50 from a 100-field schema, then opens with full schema but min=max=f50; it does not test projection from a physically 100-column file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:1459-1561)

Dependencies provide Arrow arrays/arithmetic/concat, borrowed async Reader/ObjectStore IO, Lance typed cache and metadata framing, tracing and boxed recursion/ordered futures. There is no local environment variable, Cargo feature, runtime registry, mutable global, unsafe block, durability commit or writer lifecycle. The generic offset type and private cache trait adapt existing implementations; they are not new-format plugin seams. Preserve historical behavior unless legacy repair is explicitly in scope. ## Ownership and configuration

FileWriter<M: ManifestProvider + Send + Sync> owns a Box<dyn Writer>, Schema, signed next batch ID, ordinary page table, cumulative metadata and optional statistics collector. Only object_writer is public; the provider is a PhantomData marker, not a runtime instance. The writer has no closed flag, custom Drop, abort guard or ownership-consuming finish. Replacing the public writer does not reset stored state. The ignored example is obsolete: actual calls are try_new, write with a slice, and async finish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:66-87; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:98-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:255-290)

FileWriterOptions has one field: collect_stats_for_fields. None selects every schema ID; Some(empty) disables statistics; nonempty IDs are projected with include_all_children=true before supported fields become collector builders. Unknown IDs are not explicitly rejected here. The collector may return None even after a nonempty request. The fully analyzed support predicate accepts Boolean, signed/unsigned integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, UTF8/Binary with both offset widths and Decimal128; it excludes several types that collect_statistics can independently dispatch, including timestamps, duration, dictionary and fixed binary. Do not equate dispatcher support with automatic collection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:89-137; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:440-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:550-633)

try_new creates the target object before constructing local state. with_object_writer accepts an arbitrary writer position and supplied schema without validation or dictionary hydration. There is no local environment variable, version selector, compression setting or memory budget. Store creation/overwrite policy and backend cleanup are delegated and still require IO implementation analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:99-137)

## Per-call state transitions

| Stage | Effects and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| Empty input slice | Returns Ok without validation, stats, IO, flush or counter changes |
| Validate every input batch | Convert Arrow schema; compare with stored schema ignoring declared nullability, metadata, field IDs and dictionary contents; recursively reject actual nulls in stored nonnullable fields |
| Collect stats | One row per supported selected field for the entire slice; mutates builders before writes |
| Write roots sequentially | Clone schema fields, find batch columns by name, recursively encode all arrays at current batch ID; earlier page entries and bytes survive later failure |
| Append logical length | Unchecked i32 row casts/sum and cumulative offset mutation |
| Flush | Polls in-flight writer requests before caller regains control; a failure leaves cumulative metadata advanced |
| Advance batch ID | Happens only after successful flush |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:166-236. A single call with several batches creates one stored batch. A nonempty slice containing a zero-row batch still traverses encoding and advances the batch ID on success; it is not the empty-slice no-op. The zero-row UTF8 test explicitly reopens batch0. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:985-1014)

Schema comparison retains normal ordered name/logical-type/child matching, with the shared blob-child comparison exception inherited from Field. Recursive nullability checks zip field children with ArrayData child_data and inspect physical null counts without ancestor masks or list-child logical-span slicing. They do not independently validate counts; normal schema comparison occurs first. Dictionary equality is assumed by a comment to have been checked earlier, but this writer performs no comparison or unification. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:83-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:423-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:930-980; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:144-199)

Statistics traversal uses a LIFO stack: roots and struct children are visited in reverse schema order, structs are expanded without emitting their own node, and other nested types are skipped with descendants. It uses borrowed arrays, allocates per-field vectors and does no task spawning or ancestor-validity combination. Collector output ordering instead follows its BTreeMap by original field ID. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:654-692; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:612-670)

## Page grammar and recursive writes

```text
one nonempty write(slice)
+-- scalar/null root -> one (field ID, batch ID) PageInfo
+-- struct root
|   `-- each child recursively; no parent payload/validity page
+-- list root
|   +-- parent Int32 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
|   `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
`-- large-list root
    +-- parent Int64 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
    `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
```

Dispatch uses the first actual array DataType. Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary adapters assert the corresponding field.encoding rather than return a validation error. Arrays are processed sequentially; boxed async recursion does not spawn a task. Unsupported final match returns Schema error. The earlier fixed-stride guard already covers FixedSizeList/FixedSizeBinary, so the later explicit arm adds no extra support. The binary-like predicate includes view types; the concrete legacy BinaryEncoder rejects views as InvalidInput and does not normalize them. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:292-391; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:406-459; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105)

| Adapter | Stored position and length | Additional contract |
|---|---|---|
| Null | Current cursor; logical row count | No payload or encoding-tag check |
| Plain | Encoder return at value bytes; logical elements | Assert Plain and nonempty input; validity is delegated to frozen codec semantics |
| Binary | Offset table after payload; logical elements | Assert VarBinary; absolute i64 offsets rather than a separate validity bitmap |
| Dictionary | Key bytes; logical keys | Values come from stored schema at footer time, not batch arrays |
| Struct | No parent page | Assert child count, find children by name and recurse; no parent validity |
| List/LargeList | Parent offset bytes; rows+1 | Normalize selected child spans; recursively write children[0]; no parent validity |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-586; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-87. PageInfo length is not encoded byte length. Counts and offsets use unchecked casts/sums; encoding errors may occur after bytes are written but before the current page entry is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

List writers retain each sliced values array from first through final offset, excluding outside tails but retaining storage inside null-list spans. They append initial zero and normalized offsets using usize arithmetic, then cast to i32/i64. Builder capacity is rows although rows+1 positions are appended. Position bytes/table entry precede child writes, so child failure leaves partial output. children[0] is unchecked, and no list validity is persisted. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:491-586)

## Footer, provider and shutdown

```text
ordinary data pages, written across calls
`-- finish()
    +-- ordinary dense PageTable, minimum schema field ID
    +-- optional statistics arrays and separate PageTable at batch 0
    +-- schema dictionary values; update stored offset/length metadata
    +-- M::store_schema -> optional schema/manifest position
    +-- u32 LE framed Metadata protobuf
    +-- i64 LE metadata position, i16 LE 0, i16 LE 2, "LANC"
    `-- Writer::shutdown -> authoritative size_bytes
```

The minimum schema field ID includes struct roots and is unwrapped; an empty schema panics. A nonempty schema with no page entries returns the page-table empty InvalidInput. Holes and parent fields are represented by the dense page-table contract; the writer does not add alignment padding. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:83-106; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

Statistics finish mutates builders before writing any statistics bytes. A debug assertion compares stats rows to the next batch ID. Every root is written recursively under batch0 in a separate table; the field list named leaf_field_ids actually comes from all preorder schema IDs, including struct roots. Original data field IDs are encoded as statistics root names; newly converted statistics-schema IDs index statistics pages. None/zero-row collector output omits metadata; errors propagate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-625; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:600-604; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:635-670)

ManifestProvider is a public static async hook accepting &mut dyn Writer and &Schema, returning Result<Option<usize>>. The caller writes dictionaries first and trusts the returned position. Table ManifestDescribing creates a V1 Manifest with no fragments, then calls do_write_manifest directly with no indices/transaction, so dictionaries are not written a second time. The test-only NotSelfDescribing returns None and writes nothing. Metadata serialization maps None to zero; it is not an on-disk option-presence bit. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:35-64; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:639-650; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-250; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-75)

finish uses shutdown's authoritative size and the last cumulative row count, returning FileWriteSummary. It does not call tell afterward or retain other object identity fields. finish_with_metadata extends schema metadata first; both it and add_metadata overwrite duplicate keys. Failed/repeated finish is not locally guarded, and stats/dictionary/schema/footer side effects are not rolled back. No local abort or deletion follows cancellation; underlying Writer behavior remains a separate dependency. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:238-290; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-651)

A contextual read of open_v1_writer shows path preparation followed by FileWriter<ManifestDescribing>::try_new with cloned schema/default statistics options. GenericWriter's default add_schema_metadata is a no-op for this adapter, distinct from the concrete writer's public add_metadata. This narrow trace does not establish full Dataset write scheduling, dispatch selection, compaction, commit or cleanup. ## Manifest read lifecycle

read_manifest trusts optional size or HEADs for it, requests last64KiB, retries once without known size only after successful bytes fail minimum16/magic checks, then uses signed LE footer offset as usize. It does not inspect footer version bytes or invoke feature capability gates. Bounds arithmetic is unchecked: malformed offsets or a trimmed body too short for prefix+footer can panic via arithmetic/slices. Length mismatch after trimming is InvalidInput; short-tail/wrong-magic and slow-path minimum20 are CorruptFile(path). GET errors and decode errors do not trigger cached-size retry. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:32-128)

For a larger body it opens a sized reader and accumulates16MiB chunks in file order under bounded concurrency, appends tail and decodes through ChunkedBuf without one full concatenation. All body chunks are retained before Prost decoding, so this is not bounded-memory streaming parsing. Within-chunk Bytes fields can share backing; cross-boundary copy_to_bytes allocates. After conversion detach_sparse_inline_row_ids copies nonzero inline total when less than one quarter of recorded message length, reducing retained backing at a transient copy cost. Performance numbers in source comments are not measurements here. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:75-127; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:19-159; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:396-424)

read_manifest_indexes has a different retry: only a known size plus exact error-text substring file size is too small causes a second read without hint. Missing index_section returns empty without IO. It converts every metadata entry but does not verify uniqueness or dataset feature compatibility. Private read_index_section opens the selected view and invokes length-prefixed generic read_message. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:129-175; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:161-199)

## Manifest write lifecycle

V1 default format first writes schema dictionaries; exact V2 variants skip that step. do_write_manifest writes Some index vector even if empty, or clears inherited offset for None; then does the same for optional inline transaction; finally writes manifest. Successful earlier writes and offset mutations are not rolled back by later error/cancellation. The returned position is where the manifest length prefix begins. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:53-63; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:84-92)

Contextual canonical writer creates ObjectWriter, calls this body writer, appends footer via WriteExt, shuts down and only then logs create. It uses lance-file footer constants0/2/LANC, whereas table format facade declares0/1/LANC; read_manifest checks neither pair. Commit handler selection and local publication are now covered in the [commit supplement](rust-lance-table-commit.md). ManifestDescribing is a legacy V1 schema-only provider and directly calls do_write_manifest on a fresh V1 envelope. (rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:31-40; rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:199-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:95-107; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33; rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:51-56; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-251)

## Deletion path and representation

Paths combine supplied base with _deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{random_id}.arrow or .bin. base_id is ignored locally; caller must select directory/store. NoDeletions returns None; explicit Set(empty) and Bitmap(empty) still write. Representation is chosen by enum arm, not density at IO time. Set serialization uses unspecified HashSet order and a single Arrow IPC ZSTD batch with nonnullable row_id:UInt32. Bitmap serializes Roaring as-is with no explicit run optimization. Every payload is built in Vec before one put. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-134)

Array reader loads full object and all batches before checking exactly one batch and exact schema equality. It deduplicates offsets into HashSet, rejects nulls, and returns Set without normalization. Bitmap reader wraps Roaring errors with path and returns Bitmap. Neither validates physical bounds or num_deleted_rows, resolves base_id, or explicitly checks trailing bytes after Roaring decode. A malformed Arrow iterator error becomes CorruptFile(path), while constructor error uses generic conversion. Guarded unwraps rely on count/schema checks. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:135-216)

Contextual dataset reader resolves directory before cache lookup, uses DeletionFileKey, and on miss resolves store, reads and inserts Arc vector. It is get-then-read-then-insert, with no explicit single-flight in that wrapper. Fragment write_deletions drops a fully deleted fragment; when count>=physical but coverage differs it errors; otherwise writes metadata. That count-conditional check does not locally reject every out-of-range offset in a smaller set. These callers are contextual and remain pending whole-file analysis. (rust/lance/src/io/deletion.rs:11-43; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:3005-3036)

Manifest depends on ObjectStore/Writer/CommitHandler location metadata, Prost and table codecs; chunk concurrency follows Reader::io_parallelism with minimum1. Deletion depends on Arrow IPC ZSTD and Roaring formats, core DeletionVector and audit tracing. Object-store implementations and Writer trait are storage extension boundaries; neither reviewed file declares environment settings or an index/encoding registry. Legacy ManifestProvider adapts the old writer and remains frozen compatibility scope.
