## Representation selection and memory

Choose probing only if estimated merge rows > 1,048,576 and maximum inclusive fragment-envelope overlap <= 64. Plain Range segments in a fragment with no deletions contribute zero to merge rows; any fragment deletion makes every segment's physical length count. Sparse/holed segments count their stored rows. The depth sweep counts overlapping envelopes, not live-ID intersection. Exact row budget or depth 65 chooses merging. These constants express a heuristic, not a measured crossover guarantee. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:15-27; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:352-376; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:411-435)

Construction is not merely a bounds scan: unsorted Array segments build a sorted/deduplicated (ID,u32 position) directory; bitmap segments scan bytes into u32 prefix ranks every 256 bytes. Array duplicate IDs retain the first physical position in that accelerator, while sequence length remains unchanged. Bitmap ranks count backing bytes, relying on zeroed padding and valid logical shape. Native segment lookups delegate to the encoding. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:253-338)

The end tree pads to a power of two, stores maximum ends and keeps index zero unused. DeepSizeOf accounts for retained Arc contents, sidecar capacities, tree/fragment capacities and an estimated per-merged-entry footprint; it does not measure range-map node allocation overhead or process RSS. Building a merged map adds eager chunk/pair/sort vectors and keeps probe structures too. Physical offsets and rank prefixes use unchecked casts/additions, so valid fragment-size/storage invariants remain caller obligations. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:352-390; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:437-548)

## Single and batch lookup

Merged get locates an inclusive range, finds the exact row-ID position and obtains the paired address. Envelopes may contain absent IDs. Probe get bounds candidate starts with partition_point, then walks the max-end tree without a stack, skipping subtrees whose ends cannot cover the ID. Each candidate scans its segments and checks deletion offsets; the traversal continues after a hit to detect a second live fragment entry. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:116-129; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:185-304; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:391-408)

get_many allocates output in input order, sorts (ID,original position), and preserves duplicate requests. In merged mode a forward chunk walk amortizes range traversal; in probe mode it still performs a separate probe for each sorted ID with no explicit cross-ID cursor. Therefore the doc's O(F+N) statement describes only part of the merged path: total cost includes O(N log N) sorting and segment-specific lookup. Empty input immediately returns an empty Vec. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:131-183)

Cross-chunk duplicates produce Internal during merged construction; probe mode reports Internal only when querying an ID with two surviving fragment-entry hits. Neither path is a complete within-fragment uniqueness validator. FragmentEntry::resolve stops at its first live segment hit, and single nonoverlapping chunk construction has no explicit duplicate check. Supplied deletion vectors allow a moved row to remain physically in an old fragment while only its new live location resolves. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:185-243; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:308-319; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:391-408; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:535-548; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:719-743; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:1554-1610)

## Building the merged map

For each fragment, track physical offsets across every sequence segment. A no-deletion plain Range maps to arithmetic ID/address ranges without enumerating rows. Other encodings enumerate and sort pairs; deletion-aware decomposition filters entries but advances original physical offsets, retaining holes. Adjacent sequence holes are already absent physical positions, whereas deletion offsets remain physical positions. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:502-593; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:1101-1231)

Sort chunks by start, group transitively overlapping inclusive envelopes and preserve nonoverlapping chunks. For an overlapping group, enumerate ID/address pairs, sort by ID, reject duplicates and rebuild compressed segments. Do not infer corruption from envelope overlap or failure to tile its span: sparse live sets and deletion holes are valid. Pair cardinality/nonempty assumptions justify local zip and unwrap; they are not independently checked at every helper. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/index.rs:612-743)

## Alignment and shared future lifecycle

MergeStream keeps one pending chunk from each input. It emits the minimum remaining count, splitting bigger chunks with shared futures and Arrow slices. A whole unsplit task moves its original future directly. Split errors become Wrapped with the original Error reachable through SharedReadError::source. Input task order determines column merge order; FuturesOrdered yields component results in that order. Any input stream ending stops the merge without checking remaining totals. Zero-row tasks are allowed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:41-216)

The outer stream does not await batch data; emitted futures perform the actual merge. Dropping one split future does not itself invalidate another shared handle, and retained slices can retain the whole source batch. Declared sizes must match actual data or slicing can panic; equal actual lengths are checked by RecordBatchExt::merge. Matching field names are not simple concatenation: nested structures may merge and other conflicts keep the left column. Left schema metadata survives. Certain nested-list merge branches can panic; those dependency internals are only contextually read, not fully analyzed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:90-159; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:653-673; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1227-1328)

## Ordered expansion, read-ahead and schema reuse

The wrapper chooses dense versus ordinary row-ID cursor expansion once, then expands IDs and multi-run versions while pulling tasks in order. Batch futures may complete concurrently without sharing mutable cursors. Metadata Results are captured in those futures: an input batch error propagates first and can mask a precomputed metadata error. Work done while pulling can be discarded if a future is never consumed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:648-691; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-848)

Uniform nonzero task sizes enable a 65,536-row read-ahead target and shared output-schema cache. Chunks are aligned to whole batches, capped by selected rows left; a larger task can exceed the target. A nonfinal size change permanently disables both fast paths after draining any usable cached ID chunk. Zero-size tasks do not alter the inferred size; a different final size is allowed. A batch straddling chunks copies its prefix and suffix; fitting slices share storage. Retained output futures/batches can hold multiple old buffers, so the current chunk is not a global memory cap. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:378-405; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-798)

The OnceLock caches the first completing batch's input/output schemas. Pointer-identical or structurally equal later schemas reuse its output Arc; differing schemas receive a fresh schema without replacing the cache. This path appends fields directly. The incremental fallback instead calls try_with_column repeatedly, which explicitly rejects duplicate names. Do not assume identical malformed-input behavior for both assembly paths. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:592-634; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:639-644; rust/lance-arrow/src/schema.rs:146-157)

## Selection, errors and deletion semantics

Selection offsets count rows in the requested selection, while ranges/indices identify physical positions in the sequence. Helpers slice params then often unwrap Results, so invalid selection can panic despite a Result-returning public transformer. ReadBatchParams materializers use raw index values and unchecked u32 endpoint conversions; the local total count is primarily a read-ahead estimate. The wrapper checks decoded stable-ID count and returns named CorruptFile on truncation. The direct fallback lacks that exact chunk check. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:407-545; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:156-219; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:248-277)

A one-run version sequence repeats its value without validating the run length against selection. Its O(1) comment concerns locating a version, not allocating/filling the output vector. Multi-run streaming reuses version cursors; direct calls create a new cursor and repeat selection construction. System columns appear in ID, address, last-updated, created order after payload. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:553-591; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:681-690)

Deletion predicates use physical addresses regardless of stable IDs. Some(NoDeletions) is normalized away. Filter mode removes rows from every column; null mode keeps physical length and combines existing validity with deletion validity only for _rowid/_rowaddr. Payload and version values remain present under deleted rows. If no ID/address field is present, null mode has no identifying null output; test code treats that as an upstream-invalid configuration, but production code does not reject it. Empty filtered batches are returned. ## Index, overlay and conflict-key metadata

[Index metadata](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md), [overlay metadata](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs.md) and [key existence](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs.md) now have full physical-line analysis. Index types/codec/listing are facade reexports from a private module; overlay and key_existence are public modules. (rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:7-30)

IndexMetadata separates all dependency fields from the keyed prefix: covering_fields must be a duplicate-free proper suffix unless empty. Decode validates missing IDs first, duplicates second, all-fields coverage third and exact suffix order last. keyed_fields only subtracts lengths saturating at zero; direct construction bypasses validation. keyed_field is Some only for exactly one keyed column. No schema membership or overall fields uniqueness is checked. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:160-247; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:265-321)

Coverage None means unknown; effective/deleted bitmap methods compute intersection/difference with caller-supplied live fragments. Files None means unknown, but repeated-field encoding also loses Some(empty). file_size_map overwrites duplicate paths whereas total_size_bytes counts them all. list_index_files_with_sizes collects the recursive-list stream, aborts on error and derives paths with string prefix stripping; store traversal implementation remains pending. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:96-135; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:277-290; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:342-354; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:421-446)

results_are_row_addrs recognizes ZoneMap/Bloom by case-sensitive suffix and FM by a slash-delimited, case-insensitive full protobuf type name. It inspects only Any.type_url, not contents or ScalarIndex behavior. The Vec metadata codec uses type ID lance.table.IndexMetadataList, body version1, and a length-prefixed protobuf IndexSection. Wrong-type serialization and invalid timestamp conversion can panic; ordinary conversion errors propagate. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:137-158; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:303-317; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:375-419; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:62-71)

Overlay metadata covers physical offsets including deleted rows. Value rows correspond to zero-based rank in a field's bitmap; equal versions resolve by later list position. Shared coverage applies to all fields, while PerField must remain position-aligned. sort_overlays_newest_last is stable; verification rejects only descending versions. coverage_for_field bounds-checks the bitmap Vec only for PerField and never checks DataFile field bounds. Required protobuf options and bitmap syntax are checked, but shape/rank/physical bounds are not. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:192-240; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:297-327)

tombstone_overlay_fields replaces selected nonnegative IDs with-2 without moving coverage or column slots, then removes overlays with no field unequal to-2. It rebuilds every field array and performs no physical deletion. Roaring serialization clones/optimizes bitmaps; parsing errors carry a data-file path for protobuf and an empty path for isolated serde. DeepSizeOf counts each Arc bitmap once per Context plus sparse handle capacity, using serialized bytes as a heap proxy. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:76-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:242-295)

KeyExistenceFilterBuilder uses a fixed8192-item/0.00057 Sbbf configuration and counts insert calls, not unique keys. build preserves that configuration, serializes bitmap bytes and clones field IDs. KeyValue explicitly encodes little-endian64-bit integers, raw string/binary bytes, or child-byte concatenations with zero delimiters. No type tags or escaping make this encoding non-injective. hash_value uses DefaultHasher on these bytes; Sbbf uses its own xxHash64 path. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:26-148; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:297-337)

intersects Exact/Exact returns shared-hash presence with false-positive flag false; mixed filters always return(true,true); Bloom/Bloom checks configuration and equal byte lengths through the core helper, then any shared bit returns(true,true), otherwise(false,false). It ignores field IDs and num_bits. Protobuf decode defaults only zero capacity/probability and maps missing data to empty exact set without bitmap validation. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:150-280; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:399-417)

extract_key_value_from_batch resolves ordered top-level names; missing name, outer/child NULL, no columns or unsupported type returns None. Supported values are Utf8/LargeUtf8, Binary/LargeBinary, signed/unsigned32/64-bit integers, List/LargeList and Struct recursively. A single ON column remains scalar; multiple become Composite. Row bounds are not checked locally. These helpers do not enforce primary-key eligibility or define transaction retry/abort behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:282-389)

## Overlay-induced index staleness

[Staleness L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs.md) calculates exclusion sets using metadata only. Newer means overlay.committed_version > segment.dataset_version, not > index_version algorithm revision. Fields are segment.fields including covering dependencies. For each changed field it matches exact ID, indexed ancestor or indexed descendant using Schema ancestry; siblings alone do not match. Union only that field position's coverage. No deleted-row removal or actual flat-path query occurs here. overlaid_fragments scans all fragments into borrowed HashMap keyed by truncating id as u32; duplicates overwrite. ## Row versions: positional values and preloaded lineage

[Version L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs.md) covers public rowids::version; format reexports RowDatasetVersionMeta, RowDatasetVersionRun and RowDatasetVersionSequence. LoadedRowLineage has optional Arc row_ids/created_at/last_updated_at, and SpilledRowLineage maps u64 fragment IDs to those values for synchronous commit preparation. The declaration supplies no IO loader. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:15-17; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42)

Each version run has a U64Segment span and one u64 dataset version. Readers concatenate span lengths, ignoring absolute span coordinates; local tests deliberately use overlapping coordinates. Constructors support empty, uniform and RLE-from-values forms. version_at scans runs linearly; get_version_for_row_id finds a row-ID segment position then calls it. Threshold filtering zips row IDs and versions and silently stops at the shorter sequence. No alignment validation is implicit. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:212-313; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:890-914)

The crate-internal cursor caches position/run length for adjacent requests. First rewind builds O(runs) starts; later nonadjacent requests use binary search plus a walk over duplicate starts. Empty spans are skipped. It appends to a caller Vec and can leave partial output/progress on bounds error; empty/reversed selections are no-ops. The cursor is not tied to a source identity or lifetime, so changing/replacing the sequence invalidates its caches. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:82-210)

VersionsIter differs: it advances at most one run when a run is exhausted. If that next run is empty, it still returns its version once. A length1/version7 run followed by length0/version9 therefore yields7,9; this is a control-flow deduction, not an executed test. mask removes empty spans but direct construction and decoding do not. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:314-390; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:537-559)

Inline metadata shares Arc bytes; Column is a marker for hidden creation/update fields. JSON is an untagged inline byte list or column empty object. Inline decoding can fail; load_sequence(Column) is NotSupported. Protobuf arm conversions copy/move bytes without validation, and write/read sequence functions use repeated protobuf runs with nested spans. Nested codecs now establish LE arrays, LSB bitmap bytes and validated segment conversion; standalone Ranges serialization panics, so version spans with that variant cannot pass this writer. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:98-338) (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:392-559; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:818-847)

| Helper | Count and update behavior | Failure/memory boundary |
|---|---|---|
| build_version_meta | Known positive physical rows -> uniform inline metadata; does not inspect existing version metadata | Panics if row-ID metadata missing; unknown/zero count -> None |
| Full rewrite refresh | Physical count first; otherwise inline row-ID length; column/absent ->0. Positive count overwrites all last-updated versions | Inline row-ID decode unwrap can panic; zero count preserves existing metadata |
| Partial rewrite refresh | Same count priority, but column row IDs without count error. Preserve/pad base values then patch valid offsets and RLE inline | Column versions require preload; inline decode errors silently default. O(rows) vector; excess offsets ignored; old metadata changes only at final assignment |

The table follows rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:654-815. None of these helpers checks monotonic current_version, touches created_at, changes feature flags or deletes a former column file. Complete transaction trigger/retry policy is still pending.

rechunk_version_sequences slices owned run spans by positional length into every requested chunk. allow_incomplete permits short/empty outputs on input exhaustion, but excess input is always an error, including a leftover empty run. Zero-sized requested chunks do not consume runs. It collects all chunk sizes/results and does not merge adjacent equal versions. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:561-652)

## HoleRuns: missing offsets with rank/select

[Runs L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs.md) covers a pub struct inside private rowids::runs. Private fields retain span:u32, starts and present-before prefix counts; ends are reconstructed. try_new rejects unequal bounds, empty/reversed/out-of-span runs, overlap, ordering violations and adjacency. CorruptFile uses the name row ID metadata. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:14-81; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:13-17)

position maps present offset to ordinal; offset_at is its inverse. Both use partition_point and return None for out-of-range/hole values. present_ranges is lazy and double-ended. extend_values clips its ordinal end, searches once and streams base+offset gaps into an existing Vec; arithmetic is unchecked. Bitmap conversion scans whole bytes and only branches per bit at mixed edges, treating padding as present; its documented u32-length precondition is not checked. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:83-215)

## Row-ID bitmaps, arrays and codec boundary

[Bitmap L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs.md), [array L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs.md) and [codec L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs.md) cover private child modules. read_row_ids/write_row_ids have a public reexport, while Bitmap and EncodedU64Array do not have public module routes. The exact signatures below distinguish local pub declarations, crate/super visibility and public trait implementations. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-33)

Bitmap stores Vec bytes plus logical len. Bit i uses byte i/8 and mask1<<(i%8); constructors zero padding. Direct fields/from_parts/slice/access do not enforce logical bounds. Full popcount counts every storage bit, but iteration truncates to len and can underproduce when storage is short. BitmapSlice borrows coordinates and counts edge/middle bytes; converting it back to Bitmap copies selected bits into fresh storage. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-179)

EncodedU64Array owns U16/U32 base-relative offsets or U64 values. Vec conversion uses inclusive max-minus-min thresholds, preserves input order and chooses U16 even for a singleton. Range conversion materializes all values and instead uses strict range-length thresholds. Compressed slicing decodes/rebases; U64 slicing stays U64. min on nonempty deltas returns base without scanning, assuming an offset0 that decoded/direct values need not have. binary_search assumes sortedness. Borrowed/owned iterators are boxed. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-254; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-214)

The decoder checks reverse ranges, required oneofs/holes, packed widths, base+maximum offset overflow, sorted strictness/hole bounds, bitmap length/padding and total u64 length. It hand-parses only outer field1/LengthDelimited and rejects other outer fields; plain positive ranges bypass generated message allocation and feed folding. Adjacent ranges merge; overlap/out-of-order flushes instead of rejecting. Compact grouping accepts at least two ranges whose enclosing span fits u32 and gap validation succeeds; it does not compare wire cost. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:245-266) (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:19-230; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:346-426)

Sequence serialization clones all segments, expands Ranges into ordinary wire Range messages, then encodes protobuf. Standalone U64Segment serialization panics for Ranges; version-run writer calls that path directly. Packed arrays are little-endian. Bitmap bytes are LSB-first in implementation/test, contradicting the MSB-first schema comment; use the implementation evidence to describe this checkout and retain the discrepancy until historical compatibility is examined. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-344; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:436-451; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:520-535; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)

## U64Segment: encoding choices and positional operations

[Segment L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs.md) covers public rowids::segment, including U64Segment and a borrowing SegmentCursor; SegmentCursorState is crate-visible. The nearby parent comment calls structures private, but segment is declared pub. Variants expose bounds and bitmap/array/runs values without an invariant-checking constructor barrier. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:40-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-768)

from_slice/FromIterator collect values and scan min/max/count/nondecreasing order. Unsorted chooses Array. Sorted empty becomes Range0..0, contiguous distinct values become Range when max+1 fits, and values ending at u64MAX always use SortedArray. Other sorted values select the minimum estimated cost below, with ties favoring holes then bitmap then array. The estimate is heuristic: actual compressed array widths and protobuf overhead differ. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:144-243; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:293-299)

| Candidate | Cost estimate | Construction |
|---|---|---|
| RangeWithHoles |24 +4 × missing slots | Scan every inclusive slot; collect/sort missing absolute values and encode array |
| RangeWithBitmap |24 +ceil(inclusive span /8) | Allocate full bitmap then scan/clear missing slots |
| SortedArray |24 +2 × value count | Encode collected values using actual U16/U32/U64 choice |

Cost arithmetic uses u128 and saturates to usizeMAX; it does not validate duplicates, cap allocations or ensure32-bit span fit. Distinctness is a documented precondition. For example sorted[0,0,2] is counted as three contiguous slots and becomes0..3; this is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed test. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:97-239)

from_sorted_ranges creates Ranges for at least two intervals with u32 enclosing span and validated hole runs, without a cost threshold. Arithmetic before validation is unchecked for malformed intervals. as_ranges instead converts only bitmaps with logical length<=u32MAX when16 × (missing runs+1) is strictly smaller than bitmap byte length. It allocates HoleRuns even when rejected and has no table opt-in parameter. RowIdSequence::use_range_segments also has no gate; a narrowly inspected manifest-builder caller supplies the table config policy, with full candidate assembly now covered in the manifest-builder supplement and complete storage commit integration pending. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:245-289)

| Operation | Observed contract |
|---|---|
| len/is_empty | Range span minus hole count or bitmap zero count; Ranges uses present count; arrays use length. Public malformed state can underflow or disagree with iteration |
| range | Stored bounding interval for range-backed arms, even if no values remain; sorted array endpoints; arbitrary array extrema |
| slice | Positional skip/take, silently short at EOF, retains numeric values, copies and reselects; zero request ignores offset |
| position/get | Translate value↔present ordinal; holes and Ranges use searches; bitmap position counts prefix bits, bitmap get uses select1 scan |
| contains | Hole membership scans holes linearly; sorted arrays search, arbitrary arrays scan |
| with_new_high | Consumes self, requires value above reported bound; range-backed val+1 unchecked; gaps can allocate proportional to distance |
| delete/mask | Assumed ordered existing values or ordered unique valid positions; rebuild/reselect, no Result validation |

These contracts follow rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:301-747. The doc claim that range excludes tombstones is broader than implementation: all-zero bitmap with bounds0..8 reports Some0..=7 despite len0. mask also clears everything whenever the supplied list length equals segment length, regardless of duplicate/invalid entries. Constructor max protection does not extend to range-backed with_new_high. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:330-376; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:520-580; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:694-710)

## Segment cursors and dense byte expansion

Cursor state is byte index plus count of set bits in preceding bytes. Backward requests reset only when requested ordinal precedes that count; an early return in a target byte keeps state at its beginning. Ordinary extension walks set bits; dense extension uses whole-byte or contiguous-one-run expansion when a fully selected byte has at least six set bits. Both rely on zero padding and can emit malformed padding past logical end. Requests past EOF silently truncate. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)

The density advisory uses caller-supplied segment_len>=logical_len-floor(logical_len/4). It is separate from dense extension, which never checks density itself. SegmentCursor binds a shared borrow to one segment; SegmentCursorState accepts a new source on every call without resetting by identity, and nonbitmap operations leave old bitmap state intact. RowIdSequence cursor reset and density selection are now documented below; full stream ownership is now covered in the stream supplement. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:346-354; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-855; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:925-954)

## RowIdSequence public contract

[Complete sequence L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs.md) covers all 2,309 lines. RowIdSequence owns a private segment Vec; RowIdSeqSlice borrows segments; RowIdSequenceCursor is crate-visible and owns counters only. No function in this file performs IO. The facade reexports RowIdIndex/FragmentRowIdIndex and byte codecs, all now covered in their supplements and L2 entries. find_ids examines every segment for every requested ID despite its cycling optimization comment; matches do not break the loop. It sorts but does not deduplicate requests. Duplicate delete IDs can leave a stale peek in segment.delete and prevent later requested removals; callers need uniqueness. A no-match delete still clones every segment. Display is also not canonical: it concatenates up to11 front values without separators and appends up to11 tail values. ## Cursor policy and ReadBatchParams adapter

get/range cursor operations rewind on backward requests, cache each segment length and reset SegmentCursorState when advancing. Reusing a cursor with changed/different sequence can retain wrong cached lengths/counters. Dense policy applies only to a single bitmap segment and seeds its computed cardinality; multi-segment sequences use sparse mode. Range selection preallocates requested cardinality even when EOF clips output. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:67-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:538-591)

| ReadBatchParams | Validation and order |
|---|---|
| Indices | Reads values buffer without validity check; sorted path validates last and uses cursor; unsorted path independent get; preserves duplicates |
| Range / RangeTo | Checks end only; reversed Range subtraction is unchecked |
| Ranges | Preallocates sum before per-range end validation; preserves supplied range order; casts u64 to usize |
| RangeFrom | No explicit start bound check; subtracting an excessive start can panic |
| RangeFull | Collects all values |

These exact branches are at rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:1055-1127. Error diagnostics convert endpoints to u32 and may truncate large values. This adapter is stricter on ordinary EOF than select/cursor methods, but it is not comprehensive malformed-input validation. The fully analyzed stream adapter calls cursor methods and rejects decoded-length mismatch; its ordered expansion and concurrent future lifecycle are covered in the stream supplement. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:407-444; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:648-666)

## ID masks, set conversion and rechunking

mask_to_offset_ranges returns ordered half-open ordinals grouped within each segment; adjacent groups across segment boundaries stay separate. Plain ranges walk tree-map runs. Holes remove missing IDs, sort decoded holes and subtract earlier-hole count. Bitmaps use finite allow IDs when allowed cardinality<=summed bitmap span: a single bitmap filters the iterator, multiple bitmaps cache sorted IDs once and binary-search subranges. Other masks fall back to a full-span set/bitmap scan. Ranges inserts present gaps and translates rank; arrays test mask membership in stored order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-798)

The bitmap helper popcounts only intervals between selected present IDs, retaining the prior position so the next interval includes that selected bit. RowAddrMask cannot carry both allow and block lists simultaneously. The dependency row_addrs allocates a Vec of iterators even on the streaming path, so no-copy of all IDs is not zero allocation. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:843-863; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:24-79; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:497-515)

Set conversion unions independently built segment sets so one bitmap's holes cannot erase IDs belonging to another overlapping segment. Order and multiplicity disappear. Contextual dependency inspection exposes two edge cases: empty Range0..0 inserts0 through saturating excluded-end conversion, and mask's plain-range run-end expression mishandles a low32 carry for odd high32 values. These are source-derived, unexecuted counterexamples requiring dedicated regressions before any fix. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:621-646; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:545-588; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:801-810; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:1014-1019)

rechunk_sequences returns one sequence per requested size, consuming owned inputs. It slices/re-encodes even whole segments, so range input can materialize every row; it is not a metadata-only split. allow_incomplete permits short/empty outputs but not excess input. Empty input segments are skipped only while filling a positive remaining count; a trailing empty after the final full chunk still triggers too-many error. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:959-1052; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:378-387)

The narrowly read manifest helper gates use_range_segments through config key lance.row_ids.range_segments and str_is_truthy. It skips prior opted-in inline data by fragment ID and byte-start pointer, decodes other inline sequences and rewrites only if conversion changed; column metadata is skipped. The reviewed truthy helper accepts ASCII-case-insensitive 1/true/on/yes/y without trimming; other strings return false. Full manifest preparation is now covered in the manifest-builder supplement; local commit publication is covered in its supplements; full Dataset integration and released-fixture compatibility evidence remain pending. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:73-122; rust/lance-core/src/utils/parse.rs:4-11)

## Transaction row-ID allocation and creation lineage

[Complete row-version L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs.md) covers1,461 lines. The private transaction::row_version module exposes has_writer_placed_lineage through the public transaction facade; resolve_update_version_metadata and the two Transaction methods are pub(super), usable within transaction. All are synchronous and operate on supplied metadata/preloads. No store, feature gate, lock, retry or atomic commit appears in this file. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:29-54; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:12-19; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:73-96; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:298-405)

| New-fragment metadata | Creation behavior | Last-update behavior / validation |
|---|---|---|
| Creation Column, any row-ID state | Retain marker without decoding | build_version_meta(new_version); positive count without row-ID metadata can panic |
| Row-ID Column + creation Inline | Preserve supplied creation bytes | Decode and require creation count==physical_rows.unwrap_or(0); stamp new_version |
| Row-ID Column + no creation | Error | NotSupported |
| Row-ID Inline + creation Inline/None | Decode row IDs; recompute every creation value | Found source -> cached version or1; absent source -> new_version; debug-only count check |
| No row IDs or inline decode failure, with no creation Column | Uniform creation via build_version_meta | Uniform last update; malformed row-ID bytes remain unchanged; absent IDs with positive count can panic |

The table follows ordered match arms at rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:206-295 and delegated count/panic behavior at rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:655-678. Creation Column overrides other classification. Zero/unknown rows clear latest metadata to None through build_version_meta, while valid empty inline row IDs produce Some(empty creation sequence). These are local contracts; builder preparation can exclude malformed combinations.

Source discovery materializes distinct needed IDs in HashSet, sorts existing-fragment references by ID, and scans row sequences whose inclusive bounds overlap. Inline row-ID corruption is ignored; Column rows require preload even before bounds can be checked. First matching source in ascending fragment order wins, including soft-deleted older copies because deletion vectors are not consulted. No early exit occurs after all IDs are found. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:97-171)

Creation sequences are decoded once per chosen source with unique fragment IDs; Column preload is cloned into owned sequences, and missing preload errors before output mutation. Missing or corrupt inline creation metadata gives fallback1 on found rows. Every row then performs a linear version_at scan over runs; the cache saves decoding but does not create a row-to-version array. Output creation versions do materialize one u64 per row before run compression and protobuf serialization. Duplicate fragment IDs can invalidate the exactly-once assumption and overwrite cache entries. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:173-205; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:258-288; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:230-254; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:272-282)

assign_row_ids requires physical_rows for every fragment. Column or complete Inline count is left unchanged; excess Inline count is Internal. A partial Inline prefix is decoded twice, expanded, followed by fresh consecutive IDs, rebuilt and serialized; absent metadata uses a direct Range without per-row expansion. next_row_id additions are unchecked and assume a collision-free counter. The helper updates fragments and counter incrementally and does not roll back after a later error. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:332-405)

collect_pure_rewrite_row_update_frags_ids is a cardinality filter: absent row metadata is excluded, Column always qualifies and Inline qualifies if decoded length equals physical count. It does not inspect source membership. Narrow builder context establishes assign -> resolve -> cardinality filter/index registration -> assign again for Update, and uniform stamping after assignment for Append/Overwrite. The filter therefore cannot independently distinguish already filled INSERT rows. Local index effects, operation validation and full candidate-builder ordering are now covered; complete dataset integration remains pending and no runtime defect is asserted from this ordering alone. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:298-330; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:767-781; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:952-1009; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1024-1045)

Direct tests cover assignment states, writer-placed preservation, strict placed-inline length, missing preloads and source resolution. Manifest fixtures distinguish preserved3 from inserted5, source corruption fallback1, bounds and multiple sources. Decode-once and prefilter comments are not backed by operation counters. Tests were read, not executed; none proves full commit retry or disk behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:420-884; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:886-1461)

SPDX license, proto3 syntax, lance.encodings namespace, and protobuf Empty import establish the schema. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:1-9)

### Lines 10-35

The specification maps Arrow arrays to array encodings (potentially multiple buffers) and single-buffer encodings. Encoding applies the root then feeds child encodings, decoding reverses that tree. Structs/lists may span multiple physical columns, although an encoding here describes a single column. The superseding filename in the comment is encodings21.proto, whereas the checked-in next schema is encodings_v2_1.proto; the comment is not an actual import (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:6-9). (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:10-35)

### Lines 36-58

Buffer is a reference by buffer_index uint32=1 and BufferType buffer_type=2, where page=0, column=1, file=2 choose the buffer collection. Writers may choose placement for sharing, e.g. a dictionary in column metadata; this schema does not impose a placement strategy. These indices are not raw file offsets. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:36-58)

### Lines 59-81

Nullable wraps an ArrayEncoding. NoNull contains values=1; SomeNull contains validity=1 and values=2; AllNull is empty. nullability oneof selects no_nulls=1, some_nulls=2, all_nulls=3. The comments describe one versus two versus no buffers, but child array encodings can themselves expand to multiple buffers, so these are logical components rather than a proven universal physical-buffer count (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:16-19). (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:59-81)

### Lines 82-112

List.offsets encodes num_rows non-null end offsets with the leading Arrow zero omitted. For row i, base is zero for i=0, otherwise previous offset modulo null_offset_adjustment. Non-null offset is base+list length; null offset adds the adjustment. Example [[A,B],null,[],[C,D,E]] with adjustment 7 becomes [2,9,2,5]. A single-list lookup needs only current and previous offset, enabling random access without a separate validity read. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:82-112)

The text says an offset greater than the adjustment denotes null and otherwise length is offset minus base. There is a boundary ambiguity: the preceding null formula can produce exactly the adjustment for a first null/empty value, so the strict greater-than wording cannot be assumed correct without decoder evidence (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:99-104). The range examples recover item spans using previous/end offsets modulo adjustment, with zero start requiring only the end index. Their 0..3-style notation appears to include list index 3 and must not be copied as Rust half-open range semantics. Offset scalar type is flexible and can be delta-bitpacked independently of the destination Arrow offset width. offsets is ArrayEncoding tag 1. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:113-138)

null_offset_adjustment uint64=2 must exceed total item length so a null marker does not collide with a valid end offset; the proposed optimal choice is 1+number of items to minimize required bits. num_items uint64=3 counts items referenced by this offsets page, allowing it to map to child item pages. ArrayEncoding.array_encoding is the union of 21 declared alternatives: flat=1, nullable=2, fixed_size_list=3, list=4, struct=5, binary=6, dictionary=7, fsst=8, packed_struct=9, bitpacked=10, fixed_size_binary=11, bitpacked_for_non_neg=12, constant=13, inline_bitpacking=14, out_of_line_bitpacking=15, variable=16, packed_struct_fixed_width_mini_block=17, block=18, rle=19, general_mini_block=20, byte_stream_split=21. ZoneIndex wraps ColumnEncoding inner=3 with rows_per_zone uint32=1 and Buffer zone_map_buffer=2 for filter pushdown. No executable encoder/decoder, active-version dispatch, or bit layout is implemented by these message declarations. Legacy policy and current writer use require tracing each consumer. ## Role and visibility

Public lance.encodings21 schema for structural page layouts and recursive compressive encodings. Despite its 2.1 name, it explicitly contains 2.2 and 2.3 extensions. The schema records contracts; actual runtime version checks, encoder selection, allocation limits, and byte serialization must be verified separately. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:1-675)

## Complete range analysis

### Lines 1-18

License, proto3 syntax, and lance.encodings21 package establish a separate namespace. Structural encodings describe Arrow list/struct structure; compressive encodings describe actual value compression. These layers replace the older array-versus-buffer framing for the described 2.1 format. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:1-18)

### Lines 19-42

Counting terms are deliberately distinct. num_rows is top-level user rows; num_elements multiplies rows by fixed-size-list wrapper dimensions and is the flattened FSL input to structural encoding; num_items counts fully flattened repetition/definition events; num_visible_items removes events with no value. A FIXED_SIZE_LIST<LIST<INT32>> example shows why replacing one count with another breaks nested-array interpretation. Blank lines delimit the next section. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:19-42)

### Lines 43-70

Structural encodings are called layouts. RepDefLayer records each peeled list/struct layer's interpretation: UNSPECIFIED=0 is invalid/debug; ALL_VALID_ITEM=1, ALL_VALID_LIST=2, NULLABLE_ITEM=3, NULLABLE_LIST=4 (null but no empty lists), EMPTYABLE_LIST=5 (empty but no null), NULL_AND_EMPTY_LIST=6. ITEM includes primitives or structs. Null and empty list layers are distinct even when neither emits a child value. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:43-70)

### Lines 71-103

MiniBlockLayout targets small values where per-value transposition is expensive; comments describe sector-sized compressed chunks and bulk compression tradeoffs. Its prose also says an entire page must be read, which requires checking against the actual mini-block reader rather than treating it as established scheduling behavior. Optional-in-presence rep_compression=1 and def_compression=2 describe levels, value_compression=3 values, dictionary=4 optional dictionary encoding, num_dictionary_items uint64=5, and repeated RepDefLayer layers=6. Omitted rep/def/dictionary messages mean those components are absent. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:71-103)

### Lines 104-129

MiniBlock num_buffers uint64=7 excludes repetition/definition buffers, whose existence follows their compression messages. repetition_index_depth uint32=8 must be at least one when repetition exists; greater depth enables nested random access (example depth at least three for rows[50][17][3] through five layers). Positive depth requires depth+1 u64 index values per mini-block, including leftover-item count so final-item validity can be known. num_items uint64=9 differs from page rows with lists. has_large_chunk bool=10 is documented as a 2.2 extension for chunk sizes at least 64 KB; this schema does not implement the gate. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:104-129)

### Lines 130-161

FullZipLayout targets large values where transposition cost is relatively low, zipping buffers. bits_rep uint32=1 and bits_def=2 use zero for none. details oneof selects fixed bits_per_value=3 or variable bits_per_offset=4; prose favors byte multiples for large values but does not declare a validation rule. num_items uint32=5 and num_visible_items=6 are separately stored; value_compression=7 and layers=8 describe values/structure. These counts are uint32, unlike MiniBlock's uint64 num_items. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:130-161)

### Lines 162-189

SparseLayout stores Arrow structure in layer-local slot domains, ordered outermost to innermost, with independently readable compressed value chunks. Fields: value_compression=1, num_buffers uint64=2 excluding structure, num_items uint64=3, num_visible_items uint64=4, has_large_chunk bool=5 choosing u32 versus u16 chunk-local value-buffer sizes, structural_layers repeated=6. num_items equals visible leaf slots plus one placeholder per list slot without children; null primitive slots remain visible slots. Thus a 100-slot primitive with 30 nulls has both counts 100. Structural layers can be empty for a flat non-null leaf when scheduling domain equals visible items. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:162-189)

### Lines 190-210

Domains are [0,num_slots) coordinates. Outermost means page rows; each layer's child domain is the next layer's parent; the final domain has num_visible_items slots. SparseStructuralLayer.layer requires exactly one validity=1, list=2, or fixed_size_list=3 arm. SparseValidityLayer preserves num_slots uint64=1 across parent/child and records SparseValiditySet validity=2. The requirement for exactly one is a semantic constraint; oneof alone also admits unset. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:190-210)

### Lines 211-232

SparseListLayer uses num_slots=1, num_child_slots=2, SparsePositionSet non_empty_positions=3, SparseCountSet counts=4, validity=5. Counts are positive and parallel non-empty positions; valid parents absent from that set are empty. SparseFixedSizeListLayer uses num_slots=1, dimension=2, validity=3, with child cardinality num_slots*dimension. Parent nullness and child coordinates are separate, and multiplication/consistency checks belong to implementation. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:211-232)

### Lines 233-254

SparseValiditySet has Meaning meaning=1 and SparsePositionSet positions=2. Meaning UNSPECIFIED=0, NULL_POSITIONS=1 (stored positions null, all others valid), VALID_POSITIONS=2 (inverse). Empty and All position markers are separate empty messages. SparsePositionRange has uint64 start=1 and length=2; it is a start/count representation, not start/end. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:233-254)

### Lines 255-269

SparsePositionSet.positions selects explicit CompressiveEncoding=1 for delta-compressed u64 positions, nonempty contiguous range=2, all=3, or empty=4. num_positions uint64=5 records semantic cardinality for every alternative. Explicit cardinality, range length, all-domain size, and empty-zero consistency are obligations implied by the contract, not validated by the schema. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:255-269)

SparseCountEmpty is empty. SparseCountConstant.value uint64=1 is the common positive child count. SparseCountSet.counts selects explicit compressed u64 counts=1 with cardinality inherited from the containing position set, constant=2, or empty=3 allowed only when no nonempty list slots exist. ConstantLayout generalizes prior all-null semantics at file_version >=2.2 to any page whose visible values are the same scalar. Repetition/definition buffers may still be required to explain visibility/null kinds. layers repeated=5; optional inline_value bytes=6 must be absent for all-null pages, at most 32 bytes when present, and only for a non-null scalar representable by one fixed-width Arrow value buffer without offsets or children. ### Lines 310-323

ConstantLayout rep_compression=7 and def_compression=8 are optional message fields; absence means raw u16 levels, not no levels. num_rep_values uint64=9 and num_def_values=10 count decompressed entries. Presence semantics here differ from MiniBlockLayout's absent-level compression meanings (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:82-91). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:310-323)

BlobLayout externalizes large binary payloads and stores position/size descriptions. (position=0,size=0) means empty; (nonzero position,size=0) means null and position carries repdef. inner_layout PageLayout=1 encodes descriptions with exactly one all-valid-item repdef layer, while outer layers repeated=2 describe original structure. Conflating zero-length null and empty corrupts semantics. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:324-340)

### Lines 341-358

PageLayout.layout selects MiniBlockLayout=1, ConstantLayout=2, FullZipLayout=3, BlobLayout=4, SparseLayout=5. The sparse arm explicitly requires file version 2.3 or later. Constant's non-null extension and MiniBlock large-chunk extension have their own 2.2 statements; the file's 2.1 name is not a universal gate (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290). ### Lines 359-378

Compressive encodings form a recursive tree: an initial array becomes interpreted data blocks and finally fully compressed page buffers at leaves. Data-block kinds are fixed-width, variable-width, and packed struct; ordinary structs belong to structural encoding. A buffer has no further interpreted decomposition at this layer. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:359-378)

### Lines 379-409

CompressionScheme enumerates UNSPECIFIED=0, LZ4=1, ZSTD=2. BufferCompression.scheme=1 and optional signed level=2 apply to a whole buffer. Absent level uses a scheme-specific default whose number is not stated. General buffer compression makes a parent opaque even if its ordinary encoding is transparent. Higher levels generally trade CPU for compression, but no measured complexity is given. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:379-409)

### Lines 410-446

Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:410-446)

### Lines 447-479

Compressive Constant accepts any block, stores optional bytes value=1 in metadata, emits no output buffers, and leaves literal encoding as a TODO. OutOfLineBitpacking reduces fixed-width values by removing redundant upper bits; uncompressed_bits_per_value uint64=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3 describe the result. Prose says compressed width is fixed and stored in this message, but there is no direct compressed-width scalar here; it must be recovered through nested encoding/implementation. Do not copy the old package's compressed_bits_per_value tag into this schema. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:447-479)

### Lines 480-496

InlineBitpacking stores original width uint64=1 and optional BufferCompression values=2. Compressed widths live inline per chunk, allowing variation to tolerate outliers; the encoding is opaque and turns a fixed-width data block into one buffer. Chunk header byte layout is not specified here. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:480-496)

### Lines 497-514

Fsst uses one page-wide symbol table stored in bytes symbol_table=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=2 for the transformed variable-width block. The contract calls the transform transparent. It does not specify symbol-table serialization or the FSST algorithm itself. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:497-514)

### Lines 515-533

Dictionary maps a data block of any kind to a same-kind dictionary and fixed-width indices, recursively compressed by indices=1 and items=2; num_dictionary_items uint32=3 stores dictionary size. It is opaque unless dictionary content is considered metadata. Index widths, null conventions, invalid-index errors, and metadata placement require implementation evidence. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:515-533)

### Lines 534-549

Rle emits same-kind run values and fixed-width run lengths, represented by CompressiveEncoding values=1 and run_lengths=2. It is opaque unless lengths are metadata. Unlike the older Rle declaration, it does not directly carry bits_per_value; the value-width description lives in the nested encoding. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:534-549)

### Lines 550-567

FixedSizeList is a transparent structural flattening transform within the compressive tree, converting wide/fewer fixed-width items to narrower/more items without itself compressing. items_per_value uint64=1 is this layer's dimension, values CompressiveEncoding=2 encodes flattened output, and has_validity bool=3 records validity buffer presence. This differs from SparseFixedSizeListLayer's parent/child-domain description. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:550-567)

### Lines 568-603

PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:568-603)

### Lines 604-637

General wraps the output of its inner encoding, unlike other encodings' input-oriented composition. In mini-block layout it compresses the whole mini-block; in full-zip it compresses individual values. In the FSST/Variable/bitpacked-offset example, compression can apply to offsets alone, value bytes alone, or the combined mini-block, or combinations. General has BufferCompression compression=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3, preserving data-block kind. Choosing placement changes random-access granularity and what must be decompressed together, as an inference from the documented units. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:604-637)

### Lines 638-657

ByteStreamSplit transposes fixed-width values into byte streams without reducing size by itself, then recursively encodes them using CompressiveEncoding values=1. It is opaque and keeps fixed-width block kind. The prose's attribution of upper bits to mantissa is not sufficient to define a numeric representation; this KB retains the text but requires implementation-level bit mapping before giving an exact algorithm. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:638-657)

### Lines 658-675

CompressiveEncoding.compression selects flat=1, variable=2, constant=3, out_of_line_bitpacking=4, inline_bitpacking=5, fsst=6, dictionary=7, rle=8, byte_stream_split=9, general=10, fixed_size_list=11, packed_struct=12, variable_packed_struct=13. These tags and nested types are different from the older ArrayEncoding union. No unknown/unset variant handling is implemented here. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675)

## Interaction and interpretation limits

Version markers are schema evidence only: 2.2 large mini-block chunks, generalized constants, variable packed structs; 2.3 sparse page layout (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:354-355; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:580-602). Runtime gating, structure buffer order/endianness, codec implementation, limits, and validation need further review. Multiple prose/declaration tensions are recorded above rather than silently resolved.

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table persisted metadata contracts for fragments, data/overlay/deletion files, row lineage, and fragment-tree routing and mutations. It defines state and ordering rules, with no executable mutation or reader implementation. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:1-455)

## Complete range analysis

### Lines 1-7

SPDX license and ownership, proto3 syntax, and lance.table package establish the schema without imports. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:1-7)

### Lines 8-33

DataFragment groups column files for the same rows. Missing schema columns within a fragment read as all-null. id=1 is dataset-unique, files=2 is the file list, deletion_file=3 identifies tombstones, and overlays=11 must be empty unless manifest flag 64 is set. The overlay list is ordered: later entries win ties in committed_version for the same cell. The inline-tombstone bitmap question is a TODO, not an implemented arm. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-33)

### Lines 34-53

row_id_sequence holds serialized RowIdSequence bytes inline_row_ids=5, or an empty RowLineageColumn marker column_row_ids=12 referring to a file field -3. Row IDs follow physical row order, including unsorted example [1,42,3]. The comments say current writers keep inline bytes regardless of size. Any column arm requires manifest spilled-lineage flag 2048; otherwise an older reader could see an unset oneof and falsely infer no row IDs. This is a schema contract; current writer behavior still needs source confirmation. Empty marker declaration: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-53)

### Lines 54-73

last_updated_at_version_sequence uses inline bytes=7 or column marker=13 with reserved field ID -5. created_at_version_sequence uses inline bytes=9 or marker=14 with field ID -4. Both comments say current writers store inline regardless of size, and both column variants share the 2048 gate. Shared feature-bit requirement: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:54-73)

### Lines 74-89

Former external byte-range arms reserve numeric tags 6,8,10 and the three external_* names. The comment says no Lance writer ever emitted them and column arms replaced the design; do not interpret these reservations as readable active fields. physical_rows=4 counts original rows including deleted rows; logical count subtracts deletion_file.num_deleted_rows. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-89)

### Lines 90-125

DataFile.path=1 is dataset-relative. fields=2 lists signed field IDs: in-memory -1 is unassigned and must not persist; -2 is tombstoned; all negatives are reserved system values rather than schema fields and projection skips them, including -3/-4/-5 lineage IDs. The v1 comment assigns IDs by file position plus existing maximum and counts nested struct/list fields but one ID for a fixed-size list; v1 IDs are sorted but need not be contiguous. For v2 the field ID cannot determine the physical column because encoding choices change column count, so use column_indices. The example's wording about second fragments versus files is retained as a comment-level account, not confirmed allocator behavior. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:90-125)

### Lines 126-170

column_indices=3 is empty for v1, otherwise parallels fields exactly. -1 marks a field without its own top-level column; every other column index must be unique. The packed-struct/list/FSL example maps nine fields to [0,-1,-1,1,3,4,5,6,7], illustrating packed children and optional FSL structural columns. file_major_version=4 and file_minor_version=5 record file version; both zero identify historical 0.1 or 0.2 and do not uniquely choose one. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:126-170)

### Lines 171-184

file_size_bytes=6 supplies known disk length for fast footer lookup; zero means unknown rather than a known empty file. Optional base_id=7 refers to Manifest.base_paths for imported/referenced files. Presence must survive serialization; this declaration does not fully define absence resolution. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:171-184)

### Lines 185-221

DataOverlayFile stores replacement cell values without rewriting base files. Consult overlays newest to oldest, falling through to base when absent; deletions take precedence and suppress overlay values. data_file=1 contains one value column per declared field, no row-offset key column. Value position equals the count of coverage bits below the physical offset (zero-based rank), and columns can differ in length. coverage selects shared_offset_bitmap bytes=2 (32-bit Roaring offsets shared by every field) or FieldCoverage=4 (independent field offsets). Dense UPDATE and sparse MERGE are motivating examples, not different file types. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:185-221)

### Lines 222-239

committed_version=3 is the commit that made the overlay effective, not its read version. It is stamped at commit and restamped on retry. An index built at dataset_version >= committed_version incorporates the overlay; an older index must exclude affected cells for those fields and reevaluate current values. Greater committed_version wins across overlays; equal versions use later DataFragment.overlays position. Incorrect stamping or sorting changes query results. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:222-239)

### Lines 240-250

FieldCoverage.offset_bitmaps=1 is a repeated bytes list with one 32-bit Roaring bitmap per data_file.fields entry in the same order. A present offset whose value is NULL overrides to NULL; an absent offset falls through to base. A sparse NULL update must not be encoded by simply omitting the offset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:240-250)

### Lines 251-287

DeletionFile path is {root}/_deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{id}.{extension}. Nested DeletionFileType is ARROW_ARRAY=0 or BITMAP=1. Schema comments describe one Arrow IPC batch with an Int32Array column and .arrow, or Roaring bitmap and .bin. The current Rust implementation instead requires row_id:UInt32; this source/comment discrepancy is explicit in rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-34 and rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:162-195. Comments motivate sparse versus dense selection but provide no threshold. Fields are file_type=1, read_version=2, concurrent-writer differentiating id=3, num_deleted_rows=4, and optional base_id=7 for Manifest.base_paths. Deletions operate on offsets, not stable logical IDs. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:251-287)

### Lines 288-306

RowLineageColumn is an empty marker. Exactly one DataFragment.files entry carries the relevant reserved field ID (-3 row ID, -4 creation version, -5 update version), and its column_indices identifies the column. It may share a data file or be separate; values are non-null uint64, exactly physical_rows long in physical order. Only v2 data files support this mapping; v1 datasets keep sequences inline. Metadata is stored once in files, not repeated in the marker. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-306)

### Lines 307-323

ExternalFile is a table-relative path=1 plus byte offset=2 and size=3, documented for fragment reuse index details rather than the removed external lineage arms. FragmentTreeMetadata.layout currently has one tree=1 alternative; it selects the fragment storage layout. Removed external lineage arms: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-81. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:307-323)

### Lines 324-349

FragmentTree selects inline_root=1 or root_uuid bytes=2. UUID must be exactly 16 display-order bytes and resolves to _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root under this dataset. mutations_since_root=3 carries mutations absent from that root; next_action_sequence=4 is the next unused sequence for this version. FragmentTreeRoot stores children=1, buffer=2, and next_action_sequence=3 meaning the first action not represented by the root. Confusing root and version watermarks risks replaying or skipping mutations. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:324-349)

### Lines 350-391

FragmentTreeChild routing is ordered by min_key and owns [min_key,next min_key), with the final upper bound inherited. path=1 is relative to resolved dataset; optional base_id=2 inherits the containing object's dataset when absent and otherwise matches Manifest.base_paths, including valid ID zero. min_key=3 need not exist in the child. num_keys=4, total_rows=7, and visible_rows=10 include the object's buffered mutations; height=5 counts edges to leaves, num_children=6 direct children, both zero for leaves; object_size=8 is stored byte length. materialized_through_action_sequence=9 records a leaf's fully applied watermark with no qualifying mutations above it, zero meaning none; interiors must use zero. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:350-391)

### Lines 392-406

FragmentTreeNode holds children=1 and buffered mutations=2. FragmentTreeMutation holds action_sequence=1, FragmentAction action=2, and signed after-minus-before aggregate deltas fragment_count_delta=3, total_rows_delta=4, visible_rows_delta=5. Signed deltas preserve removals and deletions; these are validated changes by contract, not validation code. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:392-406)

### Lines 407-421

FragmentAction.action oneof selects complete upsert_fragment=1, remove_fragment ID=2, AddDataFile=3, RemoveDataFile=4, AddDeletionFile=5, ClearDeletionFile=6, or ReplaceDataFile=7. Upsert replaces the entire fragment and covers changes lacking narrower actions, including overlays, version sequences, and row IDs. Treating it as a partial patch would retain obsolete state. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:407-421)

### Lines 422-442

AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:422-442)

### Lines 443-455

ReplaceDataFile carries frag_id=1, expected_path=2, path=3, file_size_bytes=4, optional base_id=5. Replace only the first expected-path match, changing path/size/base while retaining column mapping and file version. An absent base inherits the dataset resolved for the tree object or version manifest containing the mutation; present base matches Manifest.base_paths. This differs deliberately from RemoveDataFile's all-match rule. Supporting all-match rule: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:428-432. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:443-455)

## Interaction and interpretation limits

This schema supplies file/tree state and explicit ordering invariants (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-455). It does not demonstrate actual reader/writer support, transaction conflict handling, tree balancing, mutation validation, or format stability of each feature. The inline-writer comments and column-arm definitions coexist; support must be traced rather than equating declared fields with emitted files (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81).

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table contracts for dataset manifests, index metadata, fragment-reuse mappings, and MemWAL shard/index state. This is a broad persisted-state schema; it records conflict-sensitive metadata but does not execute commits, recovery, fencing, or index catch-up. (protos/table.proto:1-769)

Enabling bit 13 reinterprets every index entry, so normalize all legacy entries atomically (or enable only when none covers), retain the bit in descendants until an atomic reverse conversion. ## Interaction and interpretation limits

This document analyzes every schema line, not the algorithms alluded to in those comments. Current feature support, stable/unstable designation, commit conflict matrices, writer fencing, recovery listing, and catch-up/cleanup safety require Rust source. In particular, covering declarations may legally exceed payload availability (protos/table.proto:380-386), snapshots are not current shard truth (protos/table.proto:642-650), and absence is not zero progress (protos/table.proto:628-633).

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table.Transaction persisted/wire representation for reconstructing a manifest during commit retries and deciding transaction compatibility. Nested messages encode proposed changes; no actual conflict matrix, atomic storage commit, retry loop, or validation implementation appears in this file. (protos/transaction.proto:1-433)

Transaction exists to rebuild a manifest on retry and determine compatibility after conflict. read_version uint64=1 is the snapshot used for planning/evaluating predicates; uuid string=2 identifies the transaction; tag string=3 is described as optional but lacks scalar presence; transaction_properties string map=4 reserves __lance_commit_message. These fields are not the newly assigned commit version. (protos/transaction.proto:12-38)

Append.fragments repeated DataFragment=1 contains new fragments whose IDs are not assigned yet. Delete has updated_fragments=1 with existing IDs, deleted_fragment_ids uint64 list=2 for whole-fragment removal, and predicate string=3 that may determine whether a concurrent write would have matched. The predicate string alone does not encode the actual conflict algorithm. (protos/transaction.proto:39-64)

Overwrite creates/replaces a dataset: new fragments=1 with IDs not yet assigned, schema repeated Field=2, bytes-valued schema_metadata=3, string config_upsert_values=4 merged with existing config, and initial_bases repeated BasePath=5 for creation. Overwrite does not imply every configuration map is blindly replaced according to these field comments. (protos/transaction.proto:65-81)

CreateIndex carries new_indices=1 and removed_indices=2. It supports addition/replacement and removal by an empty new list; removed entries are the replaced indices. Names, IDs, duplicate handling, and conflicts are not validated here. (protos/transaction.proto:82-93)

Rewrite is documented as rearranging storage without changing table data. Deprecated old_fragments=1 carries existing IDs; deprecated new_fragments=2 carries unassigned IDs. RewriteGroup holds old_fragments=1 with existing IDs and new_fragments=2 whose IDs were reserved by a prior reserve operation. Merge adds a column/schema, using existing-ID fragments=1, schema=2, schema_metadata=3, preserves_nullability bool=4. True asserts no field is introduced that earlier-schema staged data cannot safely omit. False or historical absence conservatively conflicts with concurrent value writes and may force retries; this is an optimization assertion, not a general no-conflict flag. Project.schema=1 is the new field projection, preserves_nullability bool=2 asserts no nullability-affecting change. Rename/drop are examples eligible for true; tightening nullability must not set it. Restore.version uint64=1 identifies the target historical version; its materialization and feature reconciliation remain runtime questions. (protos/transaction.proto:172-190)

UpdateMode REWRITE_ROWS=0 deletes old-fragment rows and writes new fragments, motivated by many changed columns or few affected rows. `copy_blob_columns` is crate-internal deep-clone support. Commit clone invokes it before publishing a managed-blob target. ## Data flow and invariants

1. Construct a target Dataset view using the target store/base/URI, refreshed manifest and empty base-store cache. Enumerate and deduplicate managed `(Option<base ID>, URI)` references. A local managed reference copies to the same relative path; an explicit-base reference copies to a fresh `_blobs/<uuid>.blob` path. Copy payload objects before rewriting descriptors. Errors propagate to clone orchestration. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:215-259`.
2. `replace_array` recursively rebuilds struct/list/large-list containers while preserving nulls. For copied explicit references it emits local Managed descriptors, nulls the base-ID slot and changes the URI; position and size remain intact. Unmatched descriptors remain unchanged. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:30-128`.
3. `rewrite_blob_columns` returns immediately if no replacements/blob fields exist. Otherwise it projects blob-bearing top-level columns and row addresses per fragment, prepares a preserving BlobV2 rewrite plan, and writes updated arrays through the fragment updater. Replaced file fields are tombstoned with -2; empty data files are removed. Fragment identity and unrelated file columns survive. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:132-213`.

Keep `(base, URI)` identity distinct even when URI strings match across bases. Preserve descriptor offsets/sizes and container null layout. ## Interface and ownership

Public TopKLateMaterialization implements PhysicalOptimizerRule; ReadEligibility and PassThrough are caller closures. new() accepts eligible reads and only built-in pass-through nodes by default. with_read_eligibility can exclude reads; with_pass_through adds certified custom nodes. The caller must register this optimizer in its session. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:67-132,320-347`.

## Rewrite trace

1. Recognize fetched SortExec, or fetched merge directly above a partition-preserving fetched sort. Walk single-input nodes until a non-row-stream FilteredReadExec. Drop intermediate takes/row-stream reads only after checking the dataset URI and version agree. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:134-193`.
2. Reject deleted-row reads, caller-ineligible reads and known limits that keep every input row. Retain blob handling and requested system-column behavior while narrowing to sort keys plus row ID. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:194-229`.
3. Rebind sort expressions by name to narrowed schemas; preserve sort/merge fetch limits. Take deferred columns after the top-k, project original names/order, reapply certified metadata-changing wrappers, and require exact output schema equality. If all columns were already needed, decline the transformation. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:231-261,403-440`.
4. Optimization is top-down. A successful rewrite skips descent through its rewritten node; rejection logs a debug reason and retains the old plan. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:320-347`.

## Modification invariants

Column projections cannot compute or rename; hash repartition is rejected. Custom wrappers must preserve row values and column meanings, use one child, retain fields, report equal cardinality, carry no fetch, and hold no schema column indices. Equal cardinality alone is insufficient. Rebuild projection lists retain internal row ID. `rust/lance/src/io/exec/topk_late_materialization.rs:120-125,264-316,349-400`.

Take ordering propagation lives in a separate file and must not claim unchanged orderable fields after extending an input struct. SPDX/module overview directs most callers to LanceCache. Migration docs require opaque16-byte physical keys plus CACHE_KEY_FORMAT namespace and permit codec type-id routing. Prefix invalidation/key inventory are intentionally absent because digests discard logical strings. Documented migrations use with_backend then with_key_prefix, shared-backend clear or namespace rotation, and removal of prefix/keys/inventory methods; none of these higher-level bodies is defined here.
