Imports Any/Pin/Arc, async_trait, futures::Future, crate Result/deepsize Context, sibling codec/key. Public CacheEntry=Arc<dyn Any+Send+Sync> erases type while retaining thread-safe shared ownership. Lifetime is the trait-object default rather than a named borrowed payload lifetime. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:33-47)

### Lines 48-66

Public #[async_trait] CacheBackend requires Send+Sync+Debug. get takes &InternalCacheKey and Option<CacheCodec>, returns Option<CacheEntry> with no Result error channel. Docs permit memory backends to ignore codec; None requires in-memory storage because serialization unsupported. Proposed eventual removal of Option is aspiration only. Key construction and type safety are assigned to LanceCache. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:48-66)

### Lines 67-77

Required async insert takes key, owned CacheEntry, declared size_bytes:usize and optional codec and returns unit. Declared size is for eviction; interface does not itself measure, validate, persist or expose insertion errors. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:67-77)

### Lines 78-94

Required async get_or_insert has loader lifetime a separate from self/key: Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output=Result<(CacheEntry,usize)>>+Send+a>>. Result returns(entry,was_cached). Docs expect deduplication for same key unless cache disabled, and define was_cached as entry already present/loader not invoked. Whether waiting on another load is flagged cached must be checked per backend. Errors originate via Result; no cancellation or retry guarantee is specified here. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:78-94)

### Lines 95-103

clear,num_entries,size_bytes are required async methods. clear removes all entries; counts and weighted bytes may flush pending operations according to docs. No prefix/key-specific deletion or key enumeration methods exist. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:95-103)

### Lines 104-119

Synchronous approx_num_entries and approx_size_bytes default to0, explicitly meaning cannot cheaply report, not proof of an empty backend. Approximate bytes is also the DeepSizeOf fallback and can overcount buffers shared between entries. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:104-119)

### Lines 120-126

capacity_bytes defaults None: no fixed capacity or unavailable report. Some capacity can inform callers to skip values that cannot be retained, but this default method neither rejects nor enforces size limits. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/backend.rs:120-126)

deep_size_of_entries takes a mutable shared Context plus borrowed callback(&CacheEntry,&mut Context)->Option<usize>, defaults None. ## Interaction and interpretation limits

The source calls the outer envelope stabilized/stability-critical while the CacheCodecImpl format documentation explicitly remains experimental. This file alone does not resolve a released stable-format guarantee; repository compatibility rules take precedence over speculative preservation of intermediate unstable builds. Exact wrapper behavior is established, but concrete production body codecs, backend Miss handling and lance_arrow IPC implementation remain pending. No tests executed or external specifications fetched.   425 |     ///   both a true cache hit on an already-populated entry and a coalesced
  426 |     ///   concurrent load where an in-flight loader started by a different
  427 |     ///   caller produced the value.
  428 |     /// - `false` means the loader ran on this call (a real cache miss).
  429 |     ///
  430 |     /// Callers that want strict "served from cache" semantics should treat
  431 |     /// coalesced loads as misses; the current backend does not distinguish the
  432 |     /// two cases. Prefer this over rolling a caller-side `Arc<AtomicBool>`
  433 |     /// when the caller needs per-query hit/miss counters — the backend already
  434 |     /// tracks this bit internally and this method just exposes it.
  435 |     pub async fn get_or_insert_with_key_hit<K, F, Fut>(
  436 |         &self,
  437 |         cache_key: K,
  438 |         loader: F,
  439 |     ) -> Result<(Arc<K::ValueType>, bool)>
  440 |     where
  441 |         K: CacheKey,
  442 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  443 |         F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send,
  444 |         Fut: Future<Output = Result<K::ValueType>> + Send,
  445 |     {
  446 |         let key = self.sized_key(&cache_key);
  447 |         let state = self.state.clone();
  448 |         let typed_loader = Box::pin(async move {
  449 |             let value = Arc::new(loader().await?);
  450 |             let size = state.entry_size(value.as_ref());
  451 |             Ok((value as CacheEntry, size))
  452 |         });
  453 | 
  454 |         let (entry, was_cached) = self
  455 |             .state
  456 |             .backend
  457 |             .get_or_insert(&key, typed_loader, K::codec())
  458 |             .await?;
  459 |         let entry = entry.downcast::<K::ValueType>().map_err(|_| {
  460 |             self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  461 |             Error::io(format!(
  462 |                 "cache backend returned a value with the wrong concrete type for key type {:?}",
  463 |                 K::stable_type_id()
  464 |             ))
  465 |         })?;
  466 |         if was_cached {
  467 |             self.state.hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  468 |         } else {
  469 |             self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  470 |         }
  471 |         Ok((entry, was_cached))
  472 |     }
  473 | 
  474 |     pub async fn insert_unsized_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K, metadata: Arc<K::ValueType>)
  475 |     where
  476 |         K: UnsizedCacheKey,
  477 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  478 |     {
  479 |         let metadata = Arc::new(metadata);
  480 |         let size = self.state.entry_size(metadata.as_ref());
  481 |         let key = self.unsized_key(cache_key);
  482 |         self.state.backend.insert(&key, metadata, size, None).await;
  483 |     }
  484 | 
  485 |     pub async fn get_or_insert_unsized_with_key<K, F, Fut>(
  486 |         &self,
  487 |         cache_key: K,
  488 |         loader: F,
  489 |     ) -> Result<Arc<K::ValueType>>
  490 |     where
  491 |         K: UnsizedCacheKey,
  492 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  493 |         F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send,
  494 |         Fut: Future<Output = Result<Arc<K::ValueType>>> + Send,
  495 |     {
  496 |         let key = self.unsized_key(&cache_key);
  497 |         let state = self.state.clone();
  498 |         let typed_loader = Box::pin(async move {
  499 |             let value = loader().await?;
  500 |             let size = state.entry_size(&value);
  501 |             Ok((Arc::new(value) as CacheEntry, size))
  502 |         });
  503 | 
  504 |         let (entry, was_cached) = self
  505 |             .state
  506 |             .backend
  507 |             .get_or_insert(&key, typed_loader, None)
  508 |             .await?;
  509 |         let entry = entry.downcast::<Arc<K::ValueType>>().map_err(|_| {
  510 |             self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  511 |             Error::io(format!(
  512 |                 "cache backend returned a value with the wrong concrete type for unsized key type {:?}",
  513 |                 K::stable_type_id()
  514 |             ))
  515 |         })?;
  516 |         if was_cached {
  517 |             self.state.hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  518 |         } else {
  519 |             self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  520 |         }
  521 |         Ok(entry.as_ref().clone())
  522 |     }
  523 | 
  524 |     pub async fn get_unsized_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K) -> Option<Arc<K::ValueType>>
  525 |     where
  526 |         K: UnsizedCacheKey,
  527 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  528 |     {
  529 |         let key = self.unsized_key(cache_key);
  530 |         let Some(entry) = self.state.backend.get(&key, None).await else {
  531 |             self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  532 |             return None;
  533 |         };
  534 |         match entry.downcast::<Arc<K::ValueType>>() {
  535 |             Ok(value) => {
  536 |                 self.state.hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  537 |                 Some(value.as_ref().clone())
  538 |             }
  539 |             Err(_) => {
  540 |                 // Type mismatch: the backend returned a different concrete
  541 |                 // type than expected (e.g. a disk cache may store
  542 |                 // intermediate state). Treat as a miss.
  543 |                 log::warn!(
  544 |                     "cache backend returned a value with the wrong concrete type for unsized key type {:?}",
  545 |                     K::stable_type_id()
  546 |                 );
  547 |                 self.state.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  548 |                 None
  549 |             }
  550 |         }
  551 |     }
  552 | 
  553 |     fn sized_key<K: CacheKey>(&self, cache_key: &K) -> InternalCacheKey {
  554 |         let mut builder = KeyBuilder::new(self.namespace, K::stable_type_id(), K::schema());
  555 |         cache_key.write_key(&mut builder);
  556 |         builder.finish()
  557 |     }
  558 | 
  559 |     fn unsized_key<K: UnsizedCacheKey>(&self, cache_key: &K) -> InternalCacheKey {
  560 |         let mut builder = KeyBuilder::new(self.namespace, K::stable_type_id(), K::schema());
  561 |         cache_key.write_key(&mut builder);
  562 |         builder.finish()
  563 |     }
  564 | }

  570 | /// A weak reference to a LanceCache, used by indices to avoid circular references.
  571 | /// When the original cache is dropped, operations on this will gracefully no-op.
  572 | #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  573 | pub struct WeakLanceCache {
  574 |     state: Weak<CacheState>,

  577 | 
  578 | impl WeakLanceCache {
  579 |     pub fn from(cache: &LanceCache) -> Self {
  580 |         Self {
  581 |             state: Arc::downgrade(&cache.state),
  582 |             namespace: cache.namespace,
  583 |         }
  584 |     }
  585 | 
  586 |     pub fn with_key_prefix(&self, prefix: &str) -> Self {
  587 |         Self {
  588 |             state: self.state.clone(),
  589 |             namespace: self.namespace.child(prefix),
  590 |         }
  591 |     }

  593 |     /// Weighted capacity in bytes, if the cache is alive and its backend
  594 |     /// reports one.

  599 |     pub async fn get_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K) -> Option<Arc<K::ValueType>>
  600 |     where
  601 |         K: CacheKey,
  602 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  603 |     {
  604 |         self.upgrade()?.get_with_key(cache_key).await
  605 |     }
  606 | 
  607 |     pub async fn insert_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K, value: Arc<K::ValueType>) -> bool
  608 |     where
  609 |         K: CacheKey,
  610 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  611 |     {
  612 |         let Some(cache) = self.upgrade() else {
  613 |             log::warn!("WeakLanceCache: cache no longer available, unable to insert item");
  614 |             return false;
  615 |         };
  616 |         cache.insert_with_key(cache_key, value).await;
  617 |         true
  618 |     }
  619 | 
  620 |     /// Get or insert an item, computing it if necessary.
  621 |     ///
  622 |     /// Deduplication of concurrent loads is handled by the backend.
  623 |     pub async fn get_or_insert_with_key<K, F, Fut>(
  624 |         &self,
  625 |         cache_key: K,
  626 |         loader: F,
  627 |     ) -> Result<Arc<K::ValueType>>
  628 |     where
  629 |         K: CacheKey,
  630 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  631 |         F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send,
  632 |         Fut: Future<Output = Result<K::ValueType>> + Send,
  633 |     {
  634 |         self.get_or_insert_with_key_hit(cache_key, loader)
  635 |             .await
  636 |             .map(|(value, _)| value)
  637 |     }
  638 | 
  639 |     /// Same as [`get_or_insert_with_key`](Self::get_or_insert_with_key), but
  640 |     /// also returns a boolean indicating whether the loader was skipped for
  641 |     /// this call. See [`LanceCache::get_or_insert_with_key_hit`] for the
  642 |     /// coalesced-load caveat.
  643 |     pub async fn get_or_insert_with_key_hit<K, F, Fut>(
  644 |         &self,
  645 |         cache_key: K,
  646 |         loader: F,
  647 |     ) -> Result<(Arc<K::ValueType>, bool)>
  648 |     where
  649 |         K: CacheKey,
  650 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  651 |         F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send,
  652 |         Fut: Future<Output = Result<K::ValueType>> + Send,
  653 |     {
  654 |         let Some(cache) = self.upgrade() else {
  655 |             log::warn!("WeakLanceCache: cache no longer available, computing without caching");
  656 |             return loader().await.map(|value| (Arc::new(value), false));
  657 |         };
  658 |         cache.get_or_insert_with_key_hit(cache_key, loader).await
  659 |     }

  661 |     pub async fn get_unsized_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K) -> Option<Arc<K::ValueType>>
  662 |     where
  663 |         K: UnsizedCacheKey,
  664 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  665 |     {
  666 |         self.upgrade()?.get_unsized_with_key(cache_key).await
  667 |     }
  668 | 
  669 |     pub async fn insert_unsized_with_key<K>(&self, cache_key: &K, value: Arc<K::ValueType>)
  670 |     where
  671 |         K: UnsizedCacheKey,
  672 |         K::ValueType: DeepSizeOf + Send + Sync + 'static,
  673 |     {
  674 |         let Some(cache) = self.upgrade() else {
  675 |             log::warn!("WeakLanceCache: cache no longer available, unable to insert unsized item");
  676 |             return;
  677 |         };
  678 |         cache.insert_unsized_with_key(cache_key, value).await;
  679 |     }

  681 |     fn upgrade(&self) -> Option<LanceCache> {
  682 |         Some(LanceCache {
  683 |             state: self.state.upgrade()?,
  684 |             namespace: self.namespace,
  685 |         })
  686 |     }

  693 | #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  694 | pub struct CacheStats {
  695 |     /// Number of times `get`, `get_unsized`, or `get_or_insert` found an item in the cache.
  696 |     pub hits: u64,
  697 |     /// Number of times `get`, `get_unsized`, or `get_or_insert` did not find an item in the cache.
  698 |     pub misses: u64,
  699 |     /// Number of entries currently in the cache.
  700 |     pub num_entries: usize,
  701 |     /// Total size in bytes of all entries in the cache.
  702 |     pub size_bytes: usize,
  703 | }

  705 | impl CacheStats {
  706 |     pub fn hit_ratio(&self) -> f32 {
  707 |         if self.hits + self.misses == 0 {
  708 |             0.0
  709 |         } else {
  710 |             self.hits as f32 / (self.hits + self.misses) as f32
  711 |         }
  712 |     }
  713 | 
  714 |     pub fn miss_ratio(&self) -> f32 {
  715 |         if self.hits + self.misses == 0 {
  716 |             0.0
  717 |         } else {
  718 |             self.misses as f32 / (self.hits + self.misses) as f32
  719 |         }
  720 |     }
  721 | }

  970 |             codec: Option<CacheCodec>,

  989 |             self.entries
  990 |                 .lock()
  991 |                 .await
  992 |                 .values()

  203 |     /// the correct order of fields
  204 |     ///
  205 |     /// For each child in the reference field we look for a matching child
  206 |     /// in self and other.
  207 |     ///
  208 |     /// If we find a match in both we recursively merge the children.

  211 |     /// Primitive fields we simply clone self and return.

  213 |     /// Matches are determined using field names and so ids are not required.
  214 |     pub fn merge_with_reference(&self, other: &Self, reference: &Self) -> Self {
  215 |         let mut new_children = Vec::with_capacity(reference.children.len());
  216 |         let mut self_children_itr = self.children.iter().peekable();
  217 |         let mut other_children_itr = other.children.iter().peekable();
  218 |         for ref_child in &reference.children {
  219 |             match (self_children_itr.peek(), other_children_itr.peek()) {
  220 |                 (Some(&only_child), None) => {
  221 |                     // other is exhausted so just check if self matches
  222 |                     if only_child.name == ref_child.name {
  223 |                         new_children.push(only_child.clone());
  224 |                         self_children_itr.next();
  225 |                     }
  226 |                 }
  227 |                 (None, Some(&only_child)) => {
  228 |                     // Self is exhausted so just check if other matches
  229 |                     if only_child.name == ref_child.name {
  230 |                         new_children.push(only_child.clone());
  231 |                         other_children_itr.next();
  232 |                     }
  233 |                 }
  234 |                 (Some(&self_child), Some(&other_child)) => {
  235 |                     // Both iterators have potential, see if any match
  236 |                     match (
  237 |                         ref_child.name.cmp(&self_child.name),
  238 |                         ref_child.name.cmp(&other_child.name),
  239 |                     ) {
  240 |                         (Ordering::Equal, Ordering::Equal) => {
  241 |                             // Both match, recursively merge
  242 |                             new_children
  243 |                                 .push(self_child.merge_with_reference(other_child, ref_child));
  244 |                             self_children_itr.next();
  245 |                             other_children_itr.next();
  246 |                         }
  247 |                         (Ordering::Equal, _) => {
  248 |                             // Self matches, other doesn't, use self as-is
  249 |                             new_children.push(self_child.clone());
  250 |                             self_children_itr.next();
  251 |                         }
  252 |                         (_, Ordering::Equal) => {
  253 |                             // Other matches, self doesn't, use other as-is
  254 |                             new_children.push(other_child.clone());
  255 |                             other_children_itr.next();
  256 |                         }
  257 |                         _ => {
  258 |                             // Neither match, field is projected out
  259 |                         }
  260 |                     }
  261 |                 }
  262 |                 (None, None) => {
  263 |                     // Both iterators are exhausted, we can quit, all remaining fields projected out
  264 |                     break;
  265 |                 }
  266 |             }
  267 |         }
  268 |         Self {
  269 |             children: new_children,
  270 |             ..self.clone()
  271 |         }
  272 |     }

  274 |     pub fn apply_projection(&self, projection: &Projection) -> Option<Self> {
  275 |         // Maps and blob descriptors are atomic physical layouts. Map children
  276 |         // must remain together, while projected blob descriptor children may
  277 |         // have synthetic IDs that cannot be selected independently.
  278 |         let is_atomic_layout = self.logical_type.is_map() || self.is_blob();
  279 |         if is_atomic_layout && !projection.contains_field_id(self.id) {
  280 |             return None;
  281 |         }
  282 | 
  283 |         let children = if is_atomic_layout {
  284 |             self.children.clone()
  285 |         } else {
  286 |             self.children
  287 |                 .iter()
  288 |                 .filter_map(|c| c.apply_projection(projection))
  289 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  290 |         };
  291 | 
  292 |         // The following case is invalid:
  293 |         // - This is a nested field (has children)
  294 |         // - All children were projected away
  295 |         // - Caller is asking for the parent field
  296 |         assert!(
  297 |             // One of the following must be true
  298 |             !children.is_empty() // Some children were projected
  299 |                 || !projection.contains_field_id(self.id) // Caller is not asking for this field
  300 |                 || self.children.is_empty() // This isn't a nested field
  301 |         );
  302 | 
  303 |         if children.is_empty() && !projection.contains_field_id(self.id) {
  304 |             None
  305 |         } else {
  306 |             let mut new_field = self.clone();
  307 |             new_field.children = children;
  308 |             Some(projection.blob_handling.unload_if_needed(new_field))
  309 |         }
  310 |     }

  368 |                 self_name
  369 |             ));
  370 |         }
  371 |         let children_differences =
  372 |             if let Some(shared_child_count) = self.blob_v2_logical_shared_child_count(expected) {
  373 |                 explain_fields_difference(
  374 |                     &self.children[..shared_child_count],
  375 |                     &expected.children[..shared_child_count],
  376 |                     options,
  377 |                     Some(&self_name),
  378 |                 )
  379 |             } else {
  380 |                 explain_fields_difference(
  381 |                     &self.children,
  382 |                     &expected.children,
  383 |                     options,
  384 |                     Some(&self_name),
  385 |                 )
  386 |             };
  387 |         if !children_differences.is_empty() {
  388 |             let children_differences = format!(
  389 |                 "`{}` had mismatched children: {}",
  390 |                 self_name,
  391 |                 children_differences.join(", ")
  392 |             );
  393 |             differences.push(children_differences);
  394 |         }
  395 |         differences
  396 |     }

  426 |             .map(|shared_child_count| {

  436 |             && Self::compare_nullability(expected.nullable, self.nullable, options)
  437 |             && children_match
  438 |             && (!options.compare_field_ids || self.id == expected.id)
  439 |             && (!options.compare_dictionary || self.dictionary == expected.dictionary)
  440 |             && (!options.compare_metadata || self.metadata == expected.metadata)

  477 |                 DataType::Int32 => {

  480 |                 DataType::Int64 => {

  483 |                 DataType::UInt8 => {
  484 |                     self.set_dictionary_values(arr.as_dictionary::<UInt8Type>().values())
  485 |                 }
  486 |                 DataType::UInt16 => {

  488 |                 }
  489 |                 DataType::UInt32 => {

  492 |                 DataType::UInt64 => {

  551 |     pub fn is_blob(&self) -> bool {
  552 |         self.metadata.contains_key(BLOB_META_KEY)
  553 |             || self
  554 |                 .metadata
  555 |                 .get(ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY)
  556 |                 .map(|name| name == BLOB_V2_EXT_NAME)

  560 |     /// Returns true if the field is explicitly marked as blob v2 extension.
  561 |     pub fn is_blob_v2(&self) -> bool {
  562 |         self.metadata
  563 |             .get(ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY)
  564 |             .map(|name| name == BLOB_V2_EXT_NAME)
  565 |             .unwrap_or(false)
  566 |             || self.is_blob_v2_descriptor()
  567 |     }

  569 |     /// Represent legacy blobs in this field tree as Blob v2 logical inputs, preserving their identities.
  570 |     ///
  571 |     /// The new logical children have unassigned IDs; callers persisting the schema
  572 |     /// must assign them with [`Self::set_id`]. Existing Blob v2 fields are unchanged.
  573 |     ///
  574 |     /// ```
  575 |     /// # use lance_core::datatypes::Field;
  576 |     /// # fn prepare(field: &mut Field) -> lance_core::Result<()> {
  577 |     /// field.promote_blob_v2()?;
  578 |     /// # Ok(())
  579 |     /// # }
  580 |     /// ```
  581 |     pub fn promote_blob_v2(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  582 |         if !self.is_blob() {
  583 |             for child in &mut self.children {
  584 |                 child.promote_blob_v2()?;
  585 |             }
  586 |             return Ok(());
  587 |         }
  588 |         if self.is_blob_v2() {
  589 |             return Ok(());
  590 |         }
  591 |         self.logical_type = LogicalType::from("struct");
  592 |         self.encoding = None;
  593 |         self.children = super::BLOB_V2_LOGICAL_MINIMAL_FIELDS
  594 |             .iter()
  595 |             .map(|field| Self::try_from(field.as_ref()))
  596 |             .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  597 |         self.metadata.remove(BLOB_META_KEY);
  598 |         self.metadata
  599 |             .insert(ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY.to_string(), BLOB_V2_EXT_NAME.to_string());
  600 |         Ok(())
  601 |     }

  662 |     /// The field keeps its name and id but uses `LargeBinary` with no children.
  663 |     /// Blob v2 fields retain their extension marker internally so scan planning
  664 |     /// can recognize the binary view before exposing a plain Arrow binary field.
  665 |     pub fn binary_blob_mut(&mut self) {
  666 |         if !self.is_blob() {

  669 |         let is_blob_v2 = self.is_blob_v2();
  670 | 
  671 |         self.logical_type = LogicalType::try_from(&DataType::LargeBinary)
  672 |             .expect("LargeBinary is always a valid logical type");
  673 |         self.children.clear();
  674 |         self.encoding = Some(Encoding::VarBinary);
  675 |         if is_blob_v2 {
  676 |             self.metadata.remove(BLOB_META_KEY);

  678 |                 self.metadata.remove(key);

  681 |                 .insert(ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY.to_string(), BLOB_V2_EXT_NAME.to_string());

  690 |         }

  692 |         for child in &mut self.children {

  697 |     pub fn project(&self, path_components: &[&str]) -> Result<Self> {
  698 |         let mut f = Self {
  699 |             name: self.name.clone(),
  700 |             id: self.id,
  701 |             parent_id: self.parent_id,
  702 |             logical_type: self.logical_type.clone(),
  703 |             metadata: self.metadata.clone(),
  704 |             encoding: self.encoding.clone(),
  705 |             nullable: self.nullable,
  706 |             children: vec![],
  707 |             dictionary: self.dictionary.clone(),
  708 |             unenforced_primary_key_position: self.unenforced_primary_key_position,
  709 |             unenforced_clustering_key_position: self.unenforced_clustering_key_position,
  710 |         };
  711 |         if path_components.is_empty() {
  712 |             // Project stops here, copy all the remaining children.
  713 |             f.children.clone_from(&self.children)
  714 |         } else {
  715 |             let first = path_components[0];
  716 |             for c in self.children.as_slice() {
  717 |                 if c.name == first {
  718 |                     let projected = c.project(&path_components[1..])?;
  719 |                     f.children.push(projected);
  720 |                     break;
  721 |                 }
  722 |             }
  723 |         }
  724 |         Ok(f)
  725 |     }

  727 |     /// Create a new field by removing all fields that do not match the filter.
  728 |     ///
  729 |     /// If a child field matches the filter then the parent will be kept even if
  730 |     /// it does not match the filter.
  731 |     ///
  732 |     /// Returns None if the field itself does not match the filter.
  733 |     pub fn project_by_filter<F: Fn(&Self) -> bool>(&self, filter: &F) -> Option<Self> {
  734 |         let children = self
  735 |             .children
  736 |             .iter()
  737 |             .filter_map(|c| c.project_by_filter(filter))
  738 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  739 |         if !children.is_empty() || filter(self) {
  740 |             Some(Self {
  741 |                 children,
  742 |                 ..self.clone()
  743 |             })
  744 |         } else {
  745 |             None
  746 |         }
  747 |     }
  748 | 
  749 |     /// Create a new field by selecting fields by their ids.
  750 |     ///
  751 |     /// If a field has it's id in the list of ids then it will be included
  752 |     /// in the new field. If a field is selected, all of it's parents will be
  753 |     /// and all of it's children will be included.
  754 |     ///
  755 |     /// For example, for the schema:
  756 |     ///
  757 |     /// ```text
  758 |     /// 0: x struct {
  759 |     ///     1: y int32
  760 |     ///     2: l list {
  761 |     ///         3: z int32
  762 |     ///     }
  763 |     /// }
  764 |     /// ```
  765 |     ///
  766 |     /// If the ids are `[2]`, then this will include the parent `0` and the
  767 |     /// child `3`.
  768 |     pub(crate) fn project_by_ids(&self, ids: &[i32], include_all_children: bool) -> Option<Self> {
  769 |         let children = self
  770 |             .children
  771 |             .iter()
  772 |             .filter_map(|c| c.project_by_ids(ids, include_all_children))
  773 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  774 |         if ids.contains(&self.id) && (children.is_empty() || include_all_children) {
  775 |             Some(self.clone())
  776 |         } else if !children.is_empty() {
  777 |             Some(Self {
  778 |                 children,
  779 |                 ..self.clone()
  780 |             })
  781 |         } else {
  782 |             None
  783 |         }
  784 |     }

  786 |     /// Project by a field.
  787 |     ///
  788 |     pub fn project_by_field(&self, other: &Self, on_type_mismatch: OnTypeMismatch) -> Result<Self> {
  789 |         if self.name != other.name {
  790 |             return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  791 |                 "Attempt to project field by different names: {} and {}",
  792 |                 self.name, other.name,
  793 |             )));
  794 |         };
  795 | 
  796 |         if self.is_compatible_blob_projection(other) {
  797 |             return Ok(self.clone());
  798 |         }
  799 | 
  800 |         match (self.data_type(), other.data_type()) {
  801 |             (DataType::Boolean, DataType::Boolean) => Ok(self.clone()),
  802 |             (dt, other_dt)
  803 |                 if (dt.is_primitive() && other_dt.is_primitive())
  804 |                     || (dt.is_binary_like() && other_dt.is_binary_like()) =>
  805 |             {
  806 |                 if dt != other_dt {
  807 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  808 |                         "Attempt to project field by different types: {} and {}",
  809 |                         dt, other_dt,
  810 |                     )));
  811 |                 }
  812 |                 Ok(self.clone())
  813 |             }
  814 |             (DataType::Struct(_), DataType::Struct(_)) => {
  815 |                 // Blob v2 columns are special: they can have different struct layouts
  816 |                 // (logical input vs. descriptor struct). We treat blob v2 structs like primitive
  817 |                 // fields (e.g. a binary column) during schema set operations (union/subtract).
  818 |                 if self.is_blob() {
  819 |                     return Ok(self.clone());
  820 |                 }
  821 |                 let mut fields = vec![];
  822 |                 for other_field in other.children.iter() {
  823 |                     let Some(child) = self.child(&other_field.name) else {
  824 |                         return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  825 |                             "Attempt to project non-existed field: {} on {}",
  826 |                             other_field.name, self,
  827 |                         )));
  828 |                     };
  829 |                     fields.push(child.project_by_field(other_field, on_type_mismatch)?);
  830 |                 }
  831 |                 let mut cloned = self.clone();
  832 |                 cloned.children = fields;
  833 |                 Ok(cloned)
  834 |             }
  835 |             (DataType::List(_), DataType::List(_))
  836 |             | (DataType::LargeList(_), DataType::LargeList(_))
  837 |             | (DataType::Map(_, _), DataType::Map(_, _)) => {
  838 |                 let projected =
  839 |                     self.children[0].project_by_field(&other.children[0], on_type_mismatch)?;
  840 |                 let mut cloned = self.clone();
  841 |                 cloned.children = vec![projected];
  842 |                 Ok(cloned)
  843 |             }
  844 |             (DataType::FixedSizeList(dt, n), DataType::FixedSizeList(other_dt, m))
  845 |                 if dt == other_dt && n == m =>
  846 |             {
  847 |                 Ok(self.clone())
  848 |             }
  849 |             (
  850 |                 DataType::Dictionary(self_key, self_value),
  851 |                 DataType::Dictionary(other_key, other_value),
  852 |             ) if self_key == other_key && self_value == other_value => Ok(self.clone()),
  853 |             (DataType::Null, DataType::Null) => Ok(self.clone()),
  854 |             (DataType::FixedSizeBinary(self_width), DataType::FixedSizeBinary(other_width))
  855 |                 if self_width == other_width =>
  856 |             {
  857 |                 Ok(self.clone())
  858 |             }
  859 |             _ => match on_type_mismatch {
  860 |                 OnTypeMismatch::Error => Err(Error::schema(format!(
  861 |                     "Attempt to project incompatible fields: {} and {}",
  862 |                     self, other
  863 |                 ))),
  864 |                 OnTypeMismatch::TakeSelf => Ok(self.clone()),
  865 |             },
  866 |         }
  867 |     }

  869 |     pub(crate) fn resolve<'a>(
  870 |         &'a self,
  871 |         split: &mut VecDeque<&str>,
  872 |         fields: &mut Vec<&'a Self>,
  873 |     ) -> bool {
  874 |         fields.push(self);
  875 |         if split.is_empty() {
  876 |             return true;
  877 |         }
  878 |         let first = split.pop_front().unwrap();
  879 |         if let Some(child) = self.children.iter().find(|c| c.name == first) {
  880 |             child.resolve(split, fields)
  881 |         } else {
  882 |             false
  883 |         }
  884 |     }
  885 | 
  886 |     /// Case-insensitive version of resolve.
  887 |     /// First tries exact match for each child, then falls back to case-insensitive.
  888 |     pub(crate) fn resolve_case_insensitive<'a>(
  889 |         &'a self,
  890 |         split: &mut VecDeque<&str>,
  891 |         fields: &mut Vec<&'a Self>,
  892 |     ) -> bool {
  893 |         fields.push(self);
  894 |         if split.is_empty() {
  895 |             return true;
  896 |         }
  897 |         let first = split.pop_front().unwrap();
  898 |         // Try exact match first
  899 |         if let Some(child) = self.children.iter().find(|c| c.name == first) {
  900 |             return child.resolve_case_insensitive(split, fields);
  901 |         }
  902 |         // Fall back to case-insensitive match
  903 |         if let Some(child) = self
  904 |             .children
  905 |             .iter()
  906 |             .find(|c| c.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(first))
  907 |         {
  908 |             return child.resolve_case_insensitive(split, fields);
  909 |         }
  910 |         false
  911 |     }

  913 |     pub(crate) fn do_intersection(&self, other: &Self, ignore_types: bool) -> Result<Self> {
  914 |         if self.name != other.name {
  915 |             return Err(Error::arrow(format!(
  916 |                 "Attempt to intersect different fields: {} and {}",
  917 |                 self.name, other.name,
  918 |             )));
  919 |         }
  920 | 
  921 |         if self.is_blob() != other.is_blob() {
  922 |             if ignore_types {
  923 |                 return Ok(if self.id >= 0 {
  924 |                     self.clone()
  925 |                 } else {
  926 |                     other.clone()
  927 |                 });

 1048 |     /// Merge the children of other field into this one.
 1049 |     pub(super) fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) -> Result<()> {
 1050 |         match (self.data_type(), other.data_type()) {
 1051 |             (DataType::Struct(_), DataType::Struct(_)) => {
 1052 |                 for other_child in other.children.as_slice() {

 1058 |                 }
 1059 |             }
 1060 |             (DataType::List(_), DataType::List(_))
 1061 |             | (DataType::LargeList(_), DataType::LargeList(_)) => {
 1062 |                 self.children[0].merge(&other.children[0])?;
 1063 |             }
 1064 |             (
 1065 |                 DataType::FixedSizeList(_, self_list_size),
 1066 |                 DataType::FixedSizeList(_, other_list_size),
 1067 |             ) if self_list_size == other_list_size => {
 1068 |                 // do nothing
 1069 |             }
 1070 |             (DataType::FixedSizeBinary(self_size), DataType::FixedSizeBinary(other_size))
 1071 |                 if self_size == other_size =>
 1072 |             {
 1073 |                 // do nothing
 1074 |             }
 1075 |             _ => {
 1076 |                 if self.data_type() != other.data_type() {
 1077 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1078 |                         "Attempt to merge incompatible fields: {} and {}",
 1079 |                         self, other
 1080 |                     )));
 1081 |                 }
 1082 |             }
 1083 |         }

 1219 |                 .iter()
 1220 |                 .map(|f| Self::try_from(f.as_ref()))
 1221 |                 .collect::<Result<_>>()?,
 1222 |             DataType::List(item) => vec![Self::try_from(item.as_ref())?],
 1223 |             DataType::LargeList(item) => vec![Self::try_from(item.as_ref())?],
 1224 |             DataType::FixedSizeList(item, _) if matches!(item.data_type(), DataType::Struct(_)) => {

 1228 |                 // TODO: We only support keys_sorted=false for now,
 1229 |                 //  because converting a rust arrow map field to the python arrow field will
 1230 |                 //  lose the keys_sorted property.

 1237 |                 let DataType::Struct(struct_fields) = entries.data_type() else {
 1238 |                     return Err(Error::schema(
 1239 |                         "Map entries field must be a Struct<key, value>".to_string(),
 1240 |                     ));
 1241 |                 };
 1242 |                 if struct_fields.len() < 2 {
 1243 |                     return Err(Error::schema(
 1244 |                         "Map entries struct must contain both key and value fields".to_string(),
 1245 |                     ));
 1246 |                 }
 1247 |                 let key_field = &struct_fields[0];

 1250 |                         "Map key field '{}' must be non-nullable according to Arrow Map specification",
 1251 |                         key_field.name()
 1252 |                     )));
 1253 |                 }
 1254 |                 vec![Self::try_from(entries.as_ref())?]
 1255 |             }
 1256 |             _ => vec![],
 1257 |         };

 1259 |             .get(LANCE_UNENFORCED_PRIMARY_KEY_POSITION)
 1260 |             .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())
 1261 |             .or_else(|| {

 1263 |                 metadata
 1264 |                     .get(LANCE_UNENFORCED_PRIMARY_KEY)

 1270 |             .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok());
 1271 |         let is_blob_v2 = has_blob_v2_extension(field);
 1272 | 
 1273 |         if is_blob_v2 {

 1275 |                 .entry(ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY.to_string())

 1304 |                 DataType::List(_) | DataType::LargeList(_) | DataType::Map(_, _) => {

  343 |                 return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  344 |                     "Duplicate field name \"{}\" in schema:\n {:#?}",
  345 |                     field.name, self
  346 |                 )));
  347 |             }
  348 |         }
  349 | 
  350 |         // A negative id is reserved for system use; the only ones a schema may
  351 |         // carry are the hidden row lineage columns a data file stores next to
  352 |         // the user columns, as top-level fields under their own names. A
  353 |         // nested field reusing one of these ids fails the duplicate check.
  354 |         let row_lineage_ids = self
  355 |             .fields
  356 |             .iter()
  357 |             .filter(|field| crate::row_lineage_field_id(&field.name) == Some(field.id))
  358 |             .map(|field| field.id)
  359 |             .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  360 | 
  361 |         // Check for duplicate field ids
  362 |         let mut seen_ids = HashSet::new();
  363 |         for field in self.fields_pre_order() {
  364 |             if field.id < 0 && !row_lineage_ids.contains(&field.id) {
  365 |                 return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  366 |                     "Field {} has a negative id {}",
  367 |                     field.name, field.id
  368 |                 )));
  369 |             }
  370 |             if !seen_ids.insert(field.id) {
  371 |                 return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  372 |                     "Duplicate field id {} in schema {:?}",
  373 |                     field.id, self
  374 |                 )));
  375 |             }
  376 |             // The row count of a fixed-size list is derived by dividing the
  377 |             // number of items by the dimension, so a zero dimension would
  378 |             // panic with a divide-by-zero further down the write path.
  379 |             validate_fixed_size_list_dimensions(&field.name, &field.data_type())?;
  380 |         }
  381 | 
  382 |         Ok(())
  383 |     }

  543 |     /// Given a string column reference, resolve the path of fields with case-insensitive matching.
  544 |     ///
  545 |     /// This first tries an exact match, then falls back to case-insensitive matching.
  546 |     /// Returns the actual fields from the schema (preserving original case).
  547 |     pub fn resolve_case_insensitive(&self, column: impl AsRef<str>) -> Option<Vec<&Field>> {
  548 |         let split = parse_field_path(column.as_ref()).ok()?;
  549 |         if split.is_empty() {
  550 |             return None;
  551 |         }
  552 | 
  553 |         if split.len() == 1 {
  554 |             let field_name = &split[0];
  555 |             // Try exact match first
  556 |             if let Some(field) = self.fields.iter().find(|f| &f.name == field_name) {
  557 |                 return Some(vec![field]);
  558 |             }
  559 |             // Fall back to case-insensitive match
  560 |             if let Some(field) = self
  561 |                 .fields
  562 |                 .iter()
  563 |                 .find(|f| f.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(field_name))
  564 |             {
  565 |                 return Some(vec![field]);
  566 |             }
  567 |             return None;
  568 |         }
  569 | 
  570 |         // Multiple segments - resolve as a nested field path
  571 |         let mut fields = Vec::with_capacity(split.len());
  572 |         let first = &split[0];
  573 | 
  574 |         // Find the first field (try exact match, then case-insensitive)
  575 |         let field = self.fields.iter().find(|f| &f.name == first).or_else(|| {
  576 |             self.fields
  577 |                 .iter()
  578 |                 .find(|f| f.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(first))
  579 |         })?;
  580 | 
  581 |         let mut split_refs: VecDeque<&str> = split[1..].iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
  582 |         if field.resolve_case_insensitive(&mut split_refs, &mut fields) {
  583 |             Some(fields)
  584 |         } else {
  585 |             None
  586 |         }
  587 |     }

  633 |     /// Get the sequence of fields from the root to the field with the given id.
  634 |     pub fn field_ancestry_by_id(&self, id: i32) -> Option<Vec<&Field>> {
  635 |         let mut to_visit = self.fields.iter().map(|f| vec![f]).collect::<Vec<_>>();
  636 |         while let Some(path) = to_visit.pop() {
  637 |             let field = path.last().unwrap();
  638 |             if field.id == id {
  639 |                 return Some(path);
  640 |             }
  641 |             for child in field.children.iter() {
  642 |                 let mut new_path = path.clone();
  643 |                 new_path.push(child);
  644 |                 to_visit.push(new_path);
  645 |             }
  646 |         }
  647 |         None
  648 |     }

  730 |     /// Merge this schema from the other schema.
  731 |     ///
  732 |     /// After merging, the field IDs from `other` schema will be reassigned,
  733 |     /// following the fields in `self`. Schema metadata is combined, with values
  734 |     /// from `self` taking precedence when both schemas contain the same key.
  735 |     pub fn merge<S: TryInto<Self, Error = Error>>(&self, other: S) -> Result<Self> {
  736 |         let mut other: Self = other.try_into()?;
  737 |         other.reset_id();
  738 | 
  739 |         let mut merged_fields: Vec<Field> = vec![];
  740 |         for mut field in self.fields.iter().cloned() {
  741 |             if let Some(other_field) = other.field(&field.name) {
  742 |                 // if both are struct types, then merge the fields
  743 |                 field.merge(other_field)?;
  744 |             }
  745 |             merged_fields.push(field);
  746 |         }
  747 | 
  748 |         // we already checked for overlap so just need to add new top-level fields
  749 |         // in the incoming schema
  750 |         for field in other.fields.as_slice() {
  751 |             if !merged_fields.iter().any(|f| f.name == field.name) {
  752 |                 merged_fields.push(field.clone());
  753 |             }
  754 |         }
  755 |         let mut metadata = other.metadata;
  756 |         metadata.extend(
  757 |             self.metadata
  758 |                 .iter()
  759 |                 .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), value.clone())),
  760 |         );
  761 |         let schema = Self {
  762 |             fields: merged_fields,
  763 |             metadata,
  764 |         };
  765 |         Ok(schema)
  766 |     }

  784 |     /// Returns the path from root to the field using *minimal* quoting.
  785 |     ///
  786 |     /// A segment is wrapped in backticks only when it contains a character that
  787 |     /// [`parse_field_path`] treats specially (a `.` separator or a `` ` `` quote);
  788 |     /// any other character — including hyphens — is left bare. Unlike
  789 |     /// [`Self::field_path`] (which quotes for SQL-expression safety and so wraps
  790 |     /// e.g. `my-col` in backticks), the result here is both human-readable and
  791 |     /// round-trips back through `parse_field_path`, so it is safe to feed into
  792 |     /// field-path APIs such as `drop_columns` / `update_field_metadata`.
  793 |     ///
  794 |     /// This is what should be exposed as the column name in index metadata.
  795 |     ///
  796 |     /// ```
  797 |     /// use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Fields, Schema as ArrowSchema};
  798 |     /// use lance_core::datatypes::{parse_field_path, Schema};
  799 |     ///
  800 |     /// let arrow = ArrowSchema::new(vec![
  801 |     ///     Field::new("my-col", DataType::Int32, false),
  802 |     ///     Field::new(
  803 |     ///         "parent",
  804 |     ///         DataType::Struct(Fields::from(vec![Field::new("child.x", DataType::Int32, true)])),
  805 |     ///         true,
  806 |     ///     ),
  807 |     /// ]);
  808 |     /// let schema = Schema::try_from(&arrow).unwrap();
  809 |     ///
  810 |     /// // A hyphen is not special to `parse_field_path`, so it is left bare
  811 |     /// // (unlike `field_path`, which would quote it as `` `my-col` ``).
  812 |     /// let hyphen_id = schema.field("my-col").unwrap().id;
  813 |     /// assert_eq!(schema.field_path_minimal(hyphen_id).unwrap(), "my-col");
  814 |     ///
  815 |     /// // A `.` in a segment forces quoting so the path still round-trips.
  816 |     /// let dotted_id = schema.field("parent").unwrap().children[0].id;
  817 |     /// let path = schema.field_path_minimal(dotted_id).unwrap();
  818 |     /// assert_eq!(path, "parent.`child.x`");
  819 |     /// assert_eq!(
  820 |     ///     parse_field_path(&path).unwrap(),
  821 |     ///     vec!["parent".to_string(), "child.x".to_string()],
  822 |     /// );
  823 |     /// ```

  828 |                 format_field_path_minimal(&field_refs)

  831 |                 Error::index(format!("Could not find field ancestry for id {}", field_id))

  930 | pub fn compare_fields(
  931 |     fields: &[Field],
  932 |     expected: &[Field],
  933 |     options: &SchemaCompareOptions,
  934 | ) -> bool {
  935 |     if options.allow_missing_if_nullable || options.ignore_field_order || options.allow_subschema {
  936 |         let expected_names = expected
  937 |             .iter()
  938 |             .map(|f| f.name.as_str())
  939 |             .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  940 |         for field in fields {
  941 |             if !expected_names.contains(field.name.as_str()) {
  942 |                 // Extra field
  943 |                 return false;
  944 |             }
  945 |         }
  946 | 
  947 |         let field_mapping = fields
  948 |             .iter()
  949 |             .enumerate()
  950 |             .map(|(pos, f)| (f.name.as_str(), (f, pos)))
  951 |             .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>();
  952 |         let mut cumulative_position = 0;
  953 |         for expected_field in expected {
  954 |             if let Some((field, pos)) = field_mapping.get(expected_field.name.as_str()) {
  955 |                 if !field.compare_with_options(expected_field, options) {
  956 |                     return false;
  957 |                 }
  958 |                 if !options.ignore_field_order && *pos < cumulative_position {
  959 |                     return false;
  960 |                 }
  961 |                 cumulative_position = *pos;
  962 |             } else if options.allow_subschema {
  963 |                 // allow_subschema: allow missing any field
  964 |                 continue;
  965 |             } else if options.allow_missing_if_nullable && expected_field.nullable {
  966 |                 continue;
  967 |             } else {
  968 |                 return false;
  969 |             }
  970 |         }
  971 |         true
  972 |     } else {
  973 |         // Fast path: we can just zip
  974 |         fields.len() == expected.len()
  975 |             && fields
  976 |                 .iter()
  977 |                 .zip(expected.iter())
  978 |                 .all(|(lhs, rhs)| lhs.compare_with_options(rhs, options))
  979 |     }
  980 | }

  982 | pub fn explain_fields_difference(
  983 |     fields: &[Field],
  984 |     expected: &[Field],
  985 |     options: &SchemaCompareOptions,
  986 |     path: Option<&str>,
  987 | ) -> Vec<String> {
  988 |     let field_names = fields
  989 |         .iter()
  990 |         .map(|f| f.name.as_str())
  991 |         .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  992 |     let expected_names = expected
  993 |         .iter()
  994 |         .map(|f| f.name.as_str())
  995 |         .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  996 | 
  997 |     let prepend_path = |f: &str| {
  998 |         if let Some(path) = path {
  999 |             format!("{}.{}", path, f)
 1000 |         } else {
 1001 |             f.to_string()
 1002 |         }
 1003 |     };
 1004 | 
 1005 |     // Check there are no extra fields or missing fields
 1006 |     let unexpected_fields = field_names
 1007 |         .difference(&expected_names)
 1008 |         .cloned()
 1009 |         .map(prepend_path)
 1010 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1011 |     let missing_fields = expected_names.difference(&field_names);
 1012 |     let missing_fields = if options.allow_subschema {
 1013 |         // allow_subschema: don't report any missing fields
 1014 |         Vec::new()
 1015 |     } else if options.allow_missing_if_nullable {
 1016 |         missing_fields
 1017 |             .filter(|f| {
 1018 |                 let expected_field = expected.iter().find(|ef| ef.name == **f).unwrap();
 1019 |                 !expected_field.nullable
 1020 |             })
 1021 |             .cloned()
 1022 |             .map(prepend_path)
 1023 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 1024 |     } else {
 1025 |         missing_fields
 1026 |             .cloned()
 1027 |             .map(prepend_path)
 1028 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 1029 |     };
 1030 | 
 1031 |     let mut differences = vec![];
 1032 |     if !missing_fields.is_empty() || !unexpected_fields.is_empty() {
 1033 |         differences.push(format!(
 1034 |             "fields did not match, missing=[{}], unexpected=[{}]",
 1035 |             missing_fields.join(", "),
 1036 |             unexpected_fields.join(", ")
 1037 |         ));
 1038 |     }
 1039 | 
 1040 |     // Map the expected fields to position of field
 1041 |     let field_mapping = expected
 1042 |         .iter()
 1043 |         .filter_map(|ef| {
 1044 |             fields
 1045 |                 .iter()
 1046 |                 .position(|f| ef.name == f.name)
 1047 |                 .map(|pos| (ef, pos))
 1048 |         })
 1049 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1050 | 
 1051 |     // Check the fields are in the same order
 1052 |     if !options.ignore_field_order {
 1053 |         let fields_out_of_order = field_mapping.windows(2).any(|w| w[0].1 > w[1].1);
 1054 |         if fields_out_of_order {
 1055 |             let expected_order = expected.iter().map(|f| f.name.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1056 |             let actual_order = fields.iter().map(|f| f.name.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1057 |             differences.push(format!(
 1058 |                 "fields in different order, expected: [{}], actual: [{}]",
 1059 |                 expected_order.join(", "),
 1060 |                 actual_order.join(", ")
 1061 |             ));
 1062 |         }
 1063 |     }
 1064 | 
 1065 |     // Check for individual differences in the fields
 1066 |     for (expected_field, field_pos) in field_mapping.iter() {
 1067 |         let field = &fields[*field_pos];
 1068 |         debug_assert_eq!(field.name, expected_field.name);
 1069 |         let field_diffs = field.explain_differences(expected_field, options, path);
 1070 |         if !field_diffs.is_empty() {
 1071 |             differences.push(field_diffs.join(", "))
 1072 |         }
 1073 |     }
 1074 | 
 1075 |     differences
 1076 | }

 1474 |     /// Removes all fields from the projection that are in the given schema
 1475 |     ///
 1476 |     /// Fields are only removed if they exist in the base schema, otherwise they
 1477 |     /// are ignored.
 1478 |     ///
 1479 |     /// Will panic if a field in the given schema has a non-negative id and is not in the base schema.
 1480 |     pub fn subtract_schema(mut self, other: &Schema) -> Self {
 1481 |         for field in other.fields_pre_order() {
 1482 |             if field.id >= 0 {
 1483 |                 self.field_ids.remove(&field.id);
 1484 |             } else if field.name == ROW_ID {
 1485 |                 self.with_row_id = false;
 1486 |             } else if field.name == ROW_ADDR {
 1487 |                 self.with_row_addr = false;
 1488 |             } else if field.name == crate::ROW_LAST_UPDATED_AT_VERSION {
 1489 |                 self.with_row_last_updated_at_version = false;
 1490 |             } else if field.name == crate::ROW_CREATED_AT_VERSION {
 1491 |                 self.with_row_created_at_version = false;
 1492 |             } else {
 1493 |                 debug_assert_eq!(field.id, -1);
 1494 |             }
 1495 |         }
 1496 |         self
 1497 |     }

 1567 | /// Parse a field path that may contain quoted field names.
 1568 | ///
 1569 | /// Field names containing dots must be quoted with backticks.
 1570 | /// For example: "parent.`child.with.dot`" parses to ["parent", "child.with.dot"]
 1571 | ///
 1572 | /// Backticks within quoted fields must be escaped by doubling them.
 1573 | /// For example: "`field``with``backticks`" represents the field name "field`with`backticks"
 1574 | ///
 1575 | /// Returns an error if:
 1576 | /// - The input path is empty
 1577 | /// - The path has malformed quotes (unclosed, misplaced, etc.)
 1578 | /// - The path has empty segments (e.g., "parent..child" or "parent.")
 1579 | ///
 1580 | /// The result is guaranteed to contain at least one element.
 1581 | pub fn parse_field_path(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
 1582 |     if path.is_empty() {
 1583 |         return Err(Error::schema("Field path cannot be empty".to_string()));
 1584 |     }
 1585 | 
 1586 |     let mut result = Vec::new();
 1587 |     let mut current = String::new();
 1588 |     let mut in_quotes = false;
 1589 |     let mut chars = path.chars().peekable();
 1590 | 
 1591 |     while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
 1592 |         match ch {
 1593 |             '`' => {
 1594 |                 if in_quotes {
 1595 |                     // Check if this is an escaped backtick (double backtick)
 1596 |                     if chars.peek() == Some(&'`') {
 1597 |                         // Consume the second backtick and add a single backtick to current
 1598 |                         chars.next();
 1599 |                         current.push('`');
 1600 |                     } else {
 1601 |                         // End of quoted field
 1602 |                         in_quotes = false;
 1603 |                         // After closing quote, we should either see a dot or end of string
 1604 |                         if let Some(&next_ch) = chars.peek()
 1605 |                             && next_ch != '.'
 1606 |                         {
 1607 |                             return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1608 |                                 "Invalid field path '{}': expected '.' or end of string after closing quote",
 1609 |                                 path
 1610 |                             )));
 1611 |                         }
 1612 |                     }
 1613 |                 } else if current.is_empty() {
 1614 |                     // Start of quoted field
 1615 |                     in_quotes = true;
 1616 |                 } else {
 1617 |                     // Quote in the middle of unquoted field name
 1618 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1619 |                         "Invalid field path '{}': unexpected quote in the middle of field name",
 1620 |                         path
 1621 |                     )));
 1622 |                 }
 1623 |             }
 1624 |             '.' if !in_quotes => {
 1625 |                 if current.is_empty() {
 1626 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1627 |                         "Invalid field path '{}': empty field name",
 1628 |                         path
 1629 |                     )));
 1630 |                 }
 1631 |                 result.push(current);
 1632 |                 current = String::new();
 1633 |             }
 1634 |             _ => {
 1635 |                 current.push(ch);
 1636 |             }
 1637 |         }
 1638 |     }
 1639 | 
 1640 |     if in_quotes {
 1641 |         return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1642 |             "Invalid field path '{}': unclosed quote",
 1643 |             path
 1644 |         )));
 1645 |     }
 1646 | 
 1647 |     if !current.is_empty() {
 1648 |         result.push(current);
 1649 |     } else if !result.is_empty() {
 1650 |         return Err(Error::schema(format!(
 1651 |             "Invalid field path '{}': trailing dot",
 1652 |             path
 1653 |         )));
 1654 |     }
 1655 | 
 1656 |     // This check is now redundant since we check for empty input at the beginning,
 1657 |     // but keeping it for extra safety
 1658 |     if result.is_empty() {
 1659 |         return Err(Error::schema(format!("Invalid field path '{}'", path)));
 1660 |     }
 1661 | 
 1662 |     Ok(result)
 1663 | }

 1665 | /// Format a field path, quoting field names that require escaping.
 1666 | ///
 1667 | /// Field names are quoted if they contain any character that is not alphanumeric
 1668 | /// or underscore, to ensure safe SQL parsing.
 1669 | ///
 1670 | /// For example: ["parent", "child.with.dot"] formats to "parent.`child.with.dot`"
 1671 | /// For example: ["meta-data", "user-id"] formats to "`meta-data`.`user-id`"
 1672 | /// Backticks in field names are escaped by doubling them.
 1673 | /// For example: \["field`with`backticks"\] formats to "`field``with``backticks`"
 1674 | pub fn format_field_path(fields: &[&str]) -> String {
 1675 |     fields
 1676 |         .iter()
 1677 |         .map(|field| {
 1678 |             // Quote if the field contains any non-identifier character
 1679 |             // (i.e., anything other than alphanumeric or underscore)
 1680 |             let needs_quoting = field.chars().any(|c| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
 1681 |             if needs_quoting {
 1682 |                 // Escape backticks by doubling them (PostgreSQL style)
 1683 |                 let escaped = field.replace('`', "``");
 1684 |                 format!("`{}`", escaped)
 1685 |             } else {
 1686 |                 field.to_string()
 1687 |             }
 1688 |         })
 1689 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 1690 |         .join(".")
 1691 | }
 1692 | 
 1693 | /// Like [`format_field_path`], but quotes a segment only when strictly required
 1694 | /// for the result to round-trip back through [`parse_field_path`].
 1695 | ///
 1696 | /// `parse_field_path` only treats `.` (segment separator) and `` ` `` (quote)
 1697 | /// specially, so those are the only characters that force quoting here. Notably
 1698 | /// a hyphen does NOT force quoting (`my-col` stays `my-col`), unlike
 1699 | /// `format_field_path` which quotes any non-identifier character for
 1700 | /// SQL-expression safety. Use this for human-readable, round-trippable paths
 1701 | /// (e.g. column names in index metadata); use `format_field_path` when the
 1702 | /// result will be embedded in a SQL expression.
 1703 | ///
 1704 | /// ```
 1705 | /// use lance_core::datatypes::{format_field_path_minimal, parse_field_path};
 1706 | ///
 1707 | /// // Plain identifiers and hyphenated names are left bare.
 1708 | /// assert_eq!(format_field_path_minimal(&["parent", "my-col"]), "parent.my-col");
 1709 | /// // A `.` in a segment forces quoting.
 1710 | /// assert_eq!(format_field_path_minimal(&["parent", "child.x"]), "parent.`child.x`");
 1711 | /// // Embedded backticks are escaped by doubling them.
 1712 | /// assert_eq!(format_field_path_minimal(&["child`x"]), "`child``x`");
 1713 | ///
 1714 | /// // Whatever it produces round-trips back through `parse_field_path`.
 1715 | /// for segments in [vec!["parent", "my-col"], vec!["parent", "child.x"], vec!["child`x"]] {
 1716 | ///     let path = format_field_path_minimal(&segments);
 1717 | ///     assert_eq!(parse_field_path(&path).unwrap(), segments);
 1718 | /// }
 1719 | /// ```
 1720 | pub fn format_field_path_minimal(fields: &[&str]) -> String {
 1721 |     fields
 1722 |         .iter()
 1723 |         .map(|field| {
 1724 |             let needs_quoting = field.contains('.') || field.contains('`');
 1725 |             if needs_quoting {
 1726 |                 // Escape embedded backticks by doubling them, matching parse_field_path.
 1727 |                 let escaped = field.replace('`', "``");
 1728 |                 format!("`{}`", escaped)
 1729 |             } else {
 1730 |                 field.to_string()
 1731 |             }
 1732 |         })
 1733 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 1734 |         .join(".")
 1735 | }
 1736 | 
 1737 | /// Escape a field path for project
 1738 | ///
 1739 | /// Parses the field path and formats it for SQL usage.
 1740 | /// Always quotes all segments with backticks to prevent special characters.
 1741 | ///
 1742 | /// For example:
 1743 | /// - "parent.child" -> “`parent`.`child`”
 1744 | /// - "parent.`child.with.dot`" -> “`parent`.`child.with.dot`”
 1745 | pub fn escape_field_path_for_project(name: &str) -> String {
 1746 |     if name == WILDCARD {
 1747 |         return name.to_string();
 1748 |     }
 1749 |     let segments = parse_field_path(name).unwrap_or_else(|_| vec![name.to_string()]);
 1750 |     segments
 1751 |         .iter()
 1752 |         .map(|s| {
 1753 |             let escaped = s.replace('`', "``");
 1754 |             format!("`{}`", escaped)
 1755 |         })
 1756 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 1757 |         .join(".")
 1758 | }

 3010 |     #[test]
 3011 |     fn test_field_path_minimal() {
 3012 |         // A struct child whose own NAME contains a dot is the case that makes
 3013 |         // "just strip all backticks" wrong: it must stay quoted to round-trip.
 3014 |         let arrow_schema = ArrowSchema::new(vec![
 3015 |             ArrowField::new("mycol", ArrowDataType::Int32, false),
 3016 |             ArrowField::new("my_col", ArrowDataType::Int32, false),
 3017 |             ArrowField::new("my-col", ArrowDataType::Int32, false),
 3018 |             ArrowField::new(
 3019 |                 "parent",
 3020 |                 ArrowDataType::Struct(ArrowFields::from(vec![
 3021 |                     ArrowField::new("child-field", ArrowDataType::Int32, true),
 3022 |                     ArrowField::new("child.x", ArrowDataType::Int32, true),
 3023 |                     ArrowField::new("child`x", ArrowDataType::Int32, true),
 3024 |                 ])),
 3025 |                 true,
 3026 |             ),
 3027 |         ]);
 3028 |         let schema = Schema::try_from(&arrow_schema).unwrap();
 3029 |         let id_of = |path: &str| schema.field(path).unwrap().id;
 3030 |         let child_id = |name: &str| {
 3031 |             schema
 3032 |                 .field("parent")
 3033 |                 .unwrap()
 3034 |                 .children
 3035 |                 .iter()
 3036 |                 .find(|c| c.name == name)
 3037 |                 .unwrap()
 3038 |                 .id
 3039 |         };
 3040 | 
 3041 |         // Plain identifiers: unchanged by either method.
 3042 |         assert_eq!(schema.field_path_minimal(id_of("mycol")).unwrap(), "mycol");
 3043 |         assert_eq!(
 3044 |             schema.field_path_minimal(id_of("my_col")).unwrap(),
 3045 |             "my_col"
 3046 |         );
 3047 | 
 3048 |         // Hyphen is NOT special to parse_field_path, so minimal quoting leaves it
 3049 |         // bare (field_path would quote it for SQL safety).
 3050 |         assert_eq!(schema.field_path(id_of("my-col")).unwrap(), "`my-col`");
 3051 |         assert_eq!(
 3052 |             schema.field_path_minimal(id_of("my-col")).unwrap(),
 3053 |             "my-col"
 3054 |         );
 3055 | 
 3056 |         // Nested hyphenated leaf: bare under minimal quoting.
 3057 |         assert_eq!(
 3058 |             schema.field_path_minimal(child_id("child-field")).unwrap(),
 3059 |             "parent.child-field"
 3060 |         );
 3061 | 
 3062 |         // Nested leaf whose NAME contains a dot: MUST stay quoted so it
 3063 |         // round-trips through parse_field_path (this is the regression guard).
 3064 |         let dotted = schema.field_path_minimal(child_id("child.x")).unwrap();
 3065 |         assert_eq!(dotted, "parent.`child.x`");
 3066 |         assert_eq!(
 3067 |             parse_field_path(&dotted).unwrap(),
 3068 |             vec!["parent".to_string(), "child.x".to_string()]
 3069 |         );
 3070 | 
 3071 |         // Nested leaf whose NAME contains a backtick: it must be quoted AND the
 3072 |         // backtick doubled so it round-trips through parse_field_path.
 3073 |         let backticked = schema.field_path_minimal(child_id("child`x")).unwrap();
 3074 |         assert_eq!(backticked, "parent.`child``x`");
 3075 |         assert_eq!(
 3076 |             parse_field_path(&backticked).unwrap(),
 3077 |             vec!["parent".to_string(), "child`x".to_string()]
 3078 |         );
 3079 |     }

  167 | impl BlobV2Layout {
  168 |     /// Classify blob v2 child fields by name, type, order, and layout-specific
  169 |     /// nullability requirements.
  170 |     ///
  171 |     /// Child metadata is not part of the representation. The complete logical
  172 |     /// layout also accepts non-nullable `position` and `size` fields, matching
  173 |     /// the existing writer-input contract. Descriptor child nullability is
  174 |     /// ignored because it changed across released schemas; row nullness has
  175 |     /// been represented by either parent struct validity or a nullable `kind`
  176 |     /// child.
  177 |     pub fn classify(fields: &Fields) -> Option<Self> {

  182 |         } else if blob_v2_fields_match(fields, &BLOB_V2_DESC_FIELDS, false) {
  183 |             Some(Self::Descriptor)
  184 |         } else {
  185 |             None
  186 |         }
  187 |     }

  200 | fn blob_v2_field_matches(
  201 |     actual: &ArrowField,
  202 |     expected: &ArrowField,
  203 |     compare_nullability: bool,
  204 | ) -> bool {
  205 |     actual.name() == expected.name()

  207 |         && (!compare_nullability || actual.is_nullable() == expected.is_nullable())

  210 | fn blob_v2_fields_match(actual: &Fields, expected: &Fields, compare_nullability: bool) -> bool {
  211 |     actual.len() == expected.len()
  212 |         && actual
  213 |             .iter()
  214 |             .zip(expected.iter())
  215 |             .all(|(actual, expected)| {
  216 |                 blob_v2_field_matches(actual.as_ref(), expected.as_ref(), compare_nullability)

  220 | fn logical_blob_v2_fields_match(fields: &Fields) -> bool {

  226 |             .iter()
  227 |             .zip(BLOB_V2_LOGICAL_FIELDS.iter())
  228 |             .enumerate()
  229 |             .all(|(index, (actual, expected))| {
  230 |                 blob_v2_field_matches(actual.as_ref(), expected.as_ref(), index < 2)

  325 |             DataType::UInt8 => "uint8".to_string(),

  329 |             DataType::UInt32 => "uint32".to_string(),
  330 |             DataType::Int64 => "int64".to_string(),
  331 |             DataType::UInt64 => "uint64".to_string(),
  332 |             DataType::Float16 => "halffloat".to_string(),
  333 |             DataType::Float32 => "float".to_string(),
  334 |             DataType::Float64 => "double".to_string(),
  335 |             DataType::Decimal128(precision, scale) => format!("decimal:128:{precision}:{scale}"),
  336 |             DataType::Decimal256(precision, scale) => format!("decimal:256:{precision}:{scale}"),
  337 |             DataType::Utf8 | DataType::Utf8View => "string".to_string(),
  338 |             DataType::Binary | DataType::BinaryView => "binary".to_string(),
  339 |             DataType::LargeUtf8 => "large_string".to_string(),
  340 |             DataType::LargeBinary => "large_binary".to_string(),

  342 |             DataType::Date64 => "date64:ms".to_string(),
  343 |             DataType::Time32(tu) => format!("time32:{}", timeunit_to_str(tu)),
  344 |             DataType::Time64(tu) => format!("time64:{}", timeunit_to_str(tu)),

  365 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(

  387 |                     format!(
  388 |                         "fixed_size_list:{}:{}",
  389 |                         Self::try_from(field.data_type())?.0,
  390 |                         *len
  391 |                     )
  392 |                 }

  405 |                 "map".to_string()

  424 |             "int8" => Some(Int8),

  431 |             "uint64" => Some(UInt64),
  432 |             "halffloat" => Some(Float16),
  433 |             "float" => Some(Float32),
  434 |             "double" => Some(Float64),
  435 |             "string" => Some(Utf8),
  436 |             "binary" => Some(Binary),
  437 |             "large_string" => Some(LargeUtf8),
  438 |             "large_binary" => Some(LargeBinary),
  439 |             BLOB_LOGICAL_TYPE => Some(LargeBinary),
  440 |             "json" => Some(LargeBinary),
  441 |             "date32:day" => Some(Date32),
  442 |             "date64:ms" => Some(Date64),

  446 |             "time64:ns" => Some(Time64(TimeUnit::Nanosecond)),

  448 |             "duration:ms" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Millisecond)),
  449 |             "duration:us" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Microsecond)),
  450 |             "duration:ns" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Nanosecond)),

  455 |             let splits = lt.0.split(':').collect::<Vec<_>>();
  456 |             match splits[0] {
  457 |                 "fixed_size_list" => {
  458 |                     if splits.len() < 3 {
  459 |                         return Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported logical type: {}", lt)));

  461 | 
  462 |                     let size: i32 = splits
  463 |                         .last()
  464 |                         .unwrap()
  465 |                         .parse::<i32>()
  466 |                         .map_err(|e: _| Error::schema(e.to_string()))?;
  467 | 
  468 |                     let inner_type = splits[1..splits.len() - 1].join(":");
  469 | 
  470 |                     match inner_type.as_str() {
  471 |                         BFLOAT16_EXT_NAME => {
  472 |                             let field = ArrowField::new("item", Self::FixedSizeBinary(2), true)

  485 |                             Ok(FixedSizeList(

  487 |                                 size,
  488 |                             ))
  489 |                         }
  490 |                     }
  491 |                 }
  492 |                 "fixed_size_binary" => {
  493 |                     if splits.len() != 2 {

  558 |     }

  582 |         // offset/length at 0 until the dictionary is persisted, so one append
  583 |         // can legitimately hold the same dictionary at two positions.

  585 |         // the values made that case non-reflexive, so there offset and length
  586 |         // stand in for the content.
  587 |         match (&self.values, &other.values) {
  588 |             (Some(a), Some(b)) => a == b,
  589 |             (None, None) => self.offset == other.offset && self.length == other.length,
  590 |             _ => false,

  183 |         .rle_threshold
  184 |         .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_RLE_COMPRESSION_THRESHOLD);
  185 | 
  186 |     // If the user explicitly provided a threshold then honor it as an additional guard.
  187 |     // A lower threshold makes RLE harder to trigger and can be used to avoid CPU overhead.
  188 |     let passes_threshold = match params.rle_threshold {
  189 |         Some(_) => (run_count as f64) < (data.num_values as f64) * threshold,
  190 |         None => true,
  191 |     };
  192 | 
  193 |     if !passes_threshold {
  194 |         return None;
  195 |     }
  196 | 
  197 |     Some((data.num_values as u128) * (type_size as u128))
  198 | }

  201 |     data: &FixedWidthDataBlock,
  202 |     encoded_bytes: u128,
  203 |     raw_bytes: u128,
  204 | ) -> bool {
  205 |     if encoded_bytes >= raw_bytes {

  210 |     {
  211 |         if let Some(bitpack_bytes) = estimate_inline_bitpacking_bytes(data).map(u128::from)
  212 |             && bitpack_bytes < encoded_bytes
  213 |         {

  215 |         }
  216 |     }
  217 |     true

  235 | fn try_child_rle_for_mini_block(
  236 |     data: &FixedWidthDataBlock,
  237 |     params: &CompressionFieldParams,
  238 | ) -> Option<Box<dyn MiniBlockCompressor>> {
  239 |     let raw_bytes = rle_is_applicable(data, params)?;
  240 |     let (run_length_width, estimated_bytes) =
  241 |         estimate_rle_width_and_size_from_data(data, Some(*MAX_MINIBLOCK_VALUES)).ok()?;
  242 |     let child_compression = rle_child_compression_config(params);
  243 |     let encoder = || {
  244 |         RleEncoder::with_child_encoding(
  245 |             run_length_width,
  246 |             child_compression,
  247 |             child_compression,
  248 |             true,
  249 |         )
  250 |     };
  251 | 
  252 |     #[cfg(feature = "bitpacking")]
  253 |     let bitpack_bytes = estimate_inline_bitpacking_bytes(data).map(u128::from);
  254 |     #[cfg(not(feature = "bitpacking"))]
  255 |     let bitpack_bytes = None::<u128>;

  258 |         && (estimated_bytes >= raw_bytes

  261 |         encoder().selected_payload_size(data).ok()?

  278 | fn try_rle_for_block_with_width(
  279 |     data: &FixedWidthDataBlock,
  280 |     params: &CompressionFieldParams,
  281 |     run_length_width: RunLengthWidth,
  282 |     rle_payload_bytes: u128,
  283 | ) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn BlockCompressor>>> {
  284 |     let bits = data.bits_per_value;
  285 |     if !matches!(bits, 8 | 16 | 32 | 64) {
  286 |         return Ok(None);
  287 |     }
  288 | 
  289 |     let run_count = data.expect_single_stat::<UInt64Type>(Stat::RunCount);
  290 |     let threshold = params
  291 |         .rle_threshold
  292 |         .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_RLE_COMPRESSION_THRESHOLD);
  293 | 
  294 |     let passes_threshold = match params.rle_threshold {
  295 |         Some(_) => (run_count as f64) < (data.num_values as f64) * threshold,
  296 |         None => true,
  297 |     };
  298 | 
  299 |     if !passes_threshold {
  300 |         return Ok(None);
  301 |     }
  302 | 
  303 |     let raw_bytes = (data.num_values as u128) * ((bits / 8) as u128);
  304 |     let rle_bytes = rle_payload_bytes.saturating_add(RLE_BLOCK_HEADER_BYTES);
  305 | 
  306 |     if rle_bytes >= raw_bytes {
  307 |         return Ok(None);
  308 |     }
  309 | 
  310 |     #[cfg(feature = "bitpacking")]
  311 |     {
  312 |         if let Some(bitpack_bytes) = estimate_block_bitpacking_bytes(data)
  313 |             && bitpack_bytes < rle_bytes
  314 |         {
  315 |             return Ok(None);
  316 |         }
  317 |     }
  318 | 
  319 |     Ok(Some(Box::new(RleEncoder::with_run_length_width(
  320 |         run_length_width,
  321 |     ))))
  322 | }

  372 | fn try_bitpack_for_mini_block(_data: &FixedWidthDataBlock) -> Option<Box<dyn MiniBlockCompressor>> {
  373 |     #[cfg(feature = "bitpacking")]
  374 |     {
  375 |         let bits = _data.bits_per_value;
  376 |         if estimate_inline_bitpacking_bytes(_data).is_some() {
  377 |             return Some(Box::new(InlineBitpacking::new(bits)));
  378 |         }
