 2693 |     fn parse_def_desc_one<const WORD_SIZE: u8>(src: &[u8]) -> ControlWordDesc {
 2694 |         match WORD_SIZE {
 2695 |             1 => ControlWordDesc {
 2696 |                 is_new_row: true,
 2697 |                 is_visible: true,
 2698 |                 is_valid_item: src[0] == 0,
 2699 |             },
 2700 |             2 => ControlWordDesc {
 2701 |                 is_new_row: true,
 2702 |                 is_visible: true,
 2703 |                 is_valid_item: u16::from_le_bytes([src[0], src[1]]) == 0,
 2704 |             },
 2705 |             4 => ControlWordDesc {
 2706 |                 is_new_row: true,
 2707 |                 is_visible: true,
 2708 |                 is_valid_item: u32::from_le_bytes([src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3]]) as u16 == 0,
 2709 |             },
 2710 |             _ => unreachable!(),
 2711 |         }
 2712 |     }

 2714 |     /// Returns the number of bytes per control word
 2715 |     pub fn bytes_per_word(&self) -> usize {
 2716 |         match self {
 2717 |             Self::BOTH8(..) => 1,
 2718 |             Self::BOTH16(..) => 2,
 2719 |             Self::BOTH32(..) => 4,
 2720 |             Self::REP8 => 1,
 2721 |             Self::REP16 => 2,
 2722 |             Self::REP32 => 4,
 2723 |             Self::DEF8 => 1,
 2724 |             Self::DEF16 => 2,
 2725 |             Self::DEF32 => 4,
 2726 |             Self::NIL => 0,
 2727 |         }
 2728 |     }

 2730 |     /// Appends the next control word to the rep & def buffers
 2731 |     ///
 2732 |     /// `src` should be pointing at the first byte (little endian) of the control word
 2733 |     ///
 2734 |     /// `dst_rep` and `dst_def` are the buffers to append the rep and def levels to.
 2735 |     /// They will not be appended to if not needed.
 2736 |     pub fn parse(&self, src: &[u8], dst_rep: &mut Vec<u16>, dst_def: &mut Vec<u16>) {
 2737 |         match self {
 2738 |             Self::BOTH8(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => {
 2739 |                 Self::parse_both::<1>(src, dst_rep, dst_def, *bits_to_shift, *mask_to_apply)
 2740 |             }
 2741 |             Self::BOTH16(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => {
 2742 |                 Self::parse_both::<2>(src, dst_rep, dst_def, *bits_to_shift, *mask_to_apply)
 2743 |             }
 2744 |             Self::BOTH32(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => {
 2745 |                 Self::parse_both::<4>(src, dst_rep, dst_def, *bits_to_shift, *mask_to_apply)
 2746 |             }
 2747 |             Self::REP8 => Self::parse_one::<1>(src, dst_rep),
 2748 |             Self::REP16 => Self::parse_one::<2>(src, dst_rep),
 2749 |             Self::REP32 => Self::parse_one::<4>(src, dst_rep),
 2750 |             Self::DEF8 => Self::parse_one::<1>(src, dst_def),
 2751 |             Self::DEF16 => Self::parse_one::<2>(src, dst_def),
 2752 |             Self::DEF32 => Self::parse_one::<4>(src, dst_def),
 2753 |             Self::NIL => {}
 2754 |         }
 2755 |     }
 2756 | 
 2757 |     /// Return true if the control words contain repetition information
 2758 |     pub fn has_rep(&self) -> bool {
 2759 |         match self {
 2760 |             Self::BOTH8(..)
 2761 |             | Self::BOTH16(..)
 2762 |             | Self::BOTH32(..)
 2763 |             | Self::REP8
 2764 |             | Self::REP16
 2765 |             | Self::REP32 => true,
 2766 |             Self::DEF8 | Self::DEF16 | Self::DEF32 | Self::NIL => false,
 2767 |         }
 2768 |     }

 2770 |     /// Temporarily parses the control word to inspect its properties but does not append to any buffers
 2771 |     pub fn parse_desc(&self, src: &[u8], max_rep: u16, max_visible_def: u16) -> ControlWordDesc {
 2772 |         match self {
 2773 |             Self::BOTH8(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => Self::parse_desc_both::<1>(
 2774 |                 src,
 2775 |                 *bits_to_shift,
 2776 |                 *mask_to_apply,
 2777 |                 max_rep,
 2778 |                 max_visible_def,
 2779 |             ),
 2780 |             Self::BOTH16(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => Self::parse_desc_both::<2>(
 2781 |                 src,
 2782 |                 *bits_to_shift,
 2783 |                 *mask_to_apply,
 2784 |                 max_rep,
 2785 |                 max_visible_def,
 2786 |             ),
 2787 |             Self::BOTH32(bits_to_shift, mask_to_apply) => Self::parse_desc_both::<4>(
 2788 |                 src,
 2789 |                 *bits_to_shift,
 2790 |                 *mask_to_apply,
 2791 |                 max_rep,
 2792 |                 max_visible_def,
 2793 |             ),
 2794 |             Self::REP8 => Self::parse_rep_desc_one::<1>(src, max_rep),
 2795 |             Self::REP16 => Self::parse_rep_desc_one::<2>(src, max_rep),
 2796 |             Self::REP32 => Self::parse_rep_desc_one::<4>(src, max_rep),
 2797 |             Self::DEF8 => Self::parse_def_desc_one::<1>(src),
 2798 |             Self::DEF16 => Self::parse_def_desc_one::<2>(src),
 2799 |             Self::DEF32 => Self::parse_def_desc_one::<4>(src),
 2800 |             Self::NIL => ControlWordDesc {
 2801 |                 is_new_row: true,
 2802 |                 is_valid_item: true,
 2803 |                 is_visible: true,
 2804 |             },
 2805 |         }
 2806 |     }

 2808 |     /// Creates a new parser from the number of bits used for the repetition and definition levels
 2809 |     pub fn new(bits_rep: u8, bits_def: u8) -> Self {
 2810 |         let total_bits = bits_rep + bits_def;
 2811 | 
 2812 |         enum WordSize {
 2813 |             One,
 2814 |             Two,
 2815 |             Four,
 2816 |         }
 2817 | 
 2818 |         let word_size = if total_bits <= 8 {
 2819 |             WordSize::One
 2820 |         } else if total_bits <= 16 {
 2821 |             WordSize::Two
 2822 |         } else {
 2823 |             WordSize::Four
 2824 |         };
 2825 | 
 2826 |         match (bits_rep > 0, bits_def > 0, word_size) {
 2827 |             (false, false, _) => Self::NIL,
 2828 |             (false, true, WordSize::One) => Self::DEF8,
 2829 |             (false, true, WordSize::Two) => Self::DEF16,
 2830 |             (false, true, WordSize::Four) => Self::DEF32,
 2831 |             (true, false, WordSize::One) => Self::REP8,
 2832 |             (true, false, WordSize::Two) => Self::REP16,
 2833 |             (true, false, WordSize::Four) => Self::REP32,
 2834 |             (true, true, WordSize::One) => Self::BOTH8(bits_def, get_mask(bits_def as u16) as u32),
 2835 |             (true, true, WordSize::Two) => Self::BOTH16(bits_def, get_mask(bits_def as u16) as u32),
 2836 |             (true, true, WordSize::Four) => {
 2837 |                 Self::BOTH32(bits_def, get_mask(bits_def as u16) as u32)
 2838 |             }
 2839 |         }
 2840 |     }
 2841 | }

  134 | /// contain duplicate field IDs, so an ID may not identify a unique parent. For
  135 | /// those references, reconstruction preserves the legacy
  136 | /// [`Schema::mut_field_by_id`] tie-break by selecting the first matching field
  137 | /// in pre-order depth-first traversal.
  138 | ///
  139 | /// # Examples
  140 | ///
  141 | /// ```

  143 | /// use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};

  146 | ///     id: 0,
  147 | ///     parent_id: -1,

  150 | ///     ..Default::default()
  151 | /// };
  152 | /// let fields = Fields(vec![field]);
  153 | /// let schema = Schema::try_from(&fields)?;
  154 | /// assert_eq!(schema.fields[0].name, "value");
  155 | /// # Ok::<(), lance_core::Error>(())

  158 |     type Error = Error;
  159 | 
  160 |     fn try_from(fields: &Fields) -> Result<Self> {
  161 |         let mut nodes: Vec<FieldNode> = Vec::with_capacity(fields.0.len());
  162 |         let mut root_indices = Vec::with_capacity(fields.0.len());
  163 |         let mut field_indices: HashMap<i32, Option<usize>> = HashMap::with_capacity(fields.0.len());
  164 | 
  165 |         for proto_field in &fields.0 {
  166 |             let parent_index = if proto_field.parent_id == -1 {
  167 |                 None
  168 |             } else {
  169 |                 let parent_index = match field_indices.get(&proto_field.parent_id) {
  170 |                     Some(Some(parent_index)) => *parent_index,
  171 |                     Some(None) => {
  172 |                         // Duplicate IDs are invalid but occur in historical
  173 |                         // manifests. Match the legacy tree traversal only for
  174 |                         // these ambiguous parent references so valid schemas
  175 |                         // retain the linear fast path.
  176 |                         first_field_index_by_id(&nodes, &root_indices, proto_field.parent_id)
  177 |                             .ok_or_else(|| {
  178 |                                 Error::internal(format!(
  179 |                                     "Duplicate field id {} has no existing arena node",
  180 |                                     proto_field.parent_id
  181 |                                 ))
  182 |                             })?
  183 |                     }
  184 |                     None => {
  185 |                         return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  186 |                             "Field '{}' (id={}) references parent id {}, which must appear earlier in the protobuf field list",
  187 |                             proto_field.name, proto_field.id, proto_field.parent_id
  188 |                         )));
  189 |                     }
  190 |                 };
  191 |                 Some(parent_index)
  192 |             };
  193 | 
  194 |             let node_index = nodes.len();
  195 |             if let Some(parent_index) = parent_index {
  196 |                 nodes[parent_index].child_indices.push(node_index);
  197 |             } else {
  198 |                 root_indices.push(node_index);
  199 |             }
  200 |             nodes.push(FieldNode {

  202 |                 child_indices: Vec::new(),

  205 |             field_indices

  212 |         fields_by_node.resize_with(nodes.len(), || None);

  284 | /// Selecting columns from a lance file requires specifying both the
  285 | /// index of the column and the data type of the column
  286 | ///
  287 | /// Partly, this is because it is not strictly required that columns
  288 | /// be read into the same type.  For example, a string column may be
  289 | /// read as a string, large_string or string_view type.
  290 | ///
  291 | /// A read will only succeed if the decoder for a column is capable
  292 | /// of decoding into the requested type.
  293 | ///
  294 | /// Note that this should generally be limited to different in-memory
  295 | /// representations of the same semantic type.  An encoding could
  296 | /// theoretically support "casting" (e.g. int to string, etc.) but
  297 | /// there is little advantage in doing so here.
  298 | ///
  299 | /// Note: in order to specify a projection the user will need some way
  300 | /// to figure out the column indices.  In the table format we do this
  301 | /// using field IDs and keeping track of the field id->column index mapping.
  302 | ///
  303 | /// If users are not using the table format then they will need to figure
  304 | /// out some way to do this themselves.
  305 | #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  306 | pub struct ReaderProjection {
  307 |     /// The data types (schema) of the selected columns.  The names
  308 |     /// of the schema are arbitrary and ignored.
  309 |     pub schema: Arc<Schema>,
  310 |     /// The indices of the columns to load.
  311 |     ///
  312 |     /// The content of this vector depends on the file version.
  313 |     ///
  314 |     /// In Lance File Version 2.0 we need ids for structural fields as
  315 |     /// well as leaf fields:
  316 |     ///
  317 |     ///   - Primitive: the index of the column in the schema
  318 |     ///   - List: the index of the list column in the schema
  319 |     ///     followed by the column indices of the children
  320 |     ///   - FixedSizeList (of primitive): the index of the column in the schema
  321 |     ///     (this case is not nested)
  322 |     ///   - FixedSizeList (of non-primitive): not yet implemented
  323 |     ///   - Dictionary: same as primitive
  324 |     ///   - Struct: the index of the struct column in the schema
  325 |     ///     followed by the column indices of the children
  326 |     ///
  327 |     ///   In other words, this should be a DFS listing of the desired schema.
  328 |     ///
  329 |     /// In Lance File Version 2.1 we only need ids for leaf fields.  Any structural
  330 |     /// fields are completely transparent.
  331 |     ///
  332 |     /// For example, if the goal is to load:
  333 |     ///
  334 |     ///   x: int32
  335 |     ///   y: `struct<z: int32, w: string>`
  336 |     ///   z: `list<int32>`

  338 |     /// and the schema originally used to store the data was:

  341 |     ///   b: int64
  342 |     ///   y: `struct<z: int32, c: int64, w: string>`
  343 |     ///   z: `list<int32>`

  510 | const FOOTER_LEN: usize = 40;
  511 | 
  512 | // Count the V2.1 physical columns required to reconstruct a projected field.
  513 | // This is the same DFS shape consumed by `ColumnInfoIter`: ordinary structural
  514 | // nodes are transparent and leaves contribute columns. Indexed metadata loading
  515 | // can therefore compact any ordinary structural projection into 0..N while
  516 | // preserving this order.
  517 | //
  518 | // Blob and packed-struct fields remain unsupported by indexed projection. Their
  519 | // opaque decode semantics are handled by the existing full-metadata reader.
  520 | fn indexed_projection_column_count(field: &Field) -> Option<usize> {
  521 |     if field.is_blob() || field.is_packed_struct() {
  522 |         return None;
  523 |     }
  524 | 
  525 |     if field.children.is_empty() {
  526 |         return Some(1);
  527 |     }
  528 | 
  529 |     field.children.iter().try_fold(0usize, |count, child| {
  530 |         count.checked_add(indexed_projection_column_count(child)?)
  531 |     })
  532 | }
  533 | 
  534 | // The reader combines a projection's columns into rectangular batches, so they
  535 | // must all have the same length.  Returns that common length, or a descriptive
  536 | // error (naming each column's length) when they differ. Ordinary files always
  537 | // pass; only files written with `FileWriter::write_column` whose columns ended up
  538 | // unequal can fail, and those must be read separately.
  539 | pub(crate) fn normalized_column_num_rows(info: &ColumnInfo) -> Result<u64> {
  540 |     info.page_infos.iter().try_fold(0_u64, |rows, page| {
  541 |         let page_rows = match &page.encoding {
  542 |             PageEncoding::Structural(layout) => match &layout.layout {
  543 |                 Some(pbenc21::page_layout::Layout::SparseLayout(sparse)) => sparse
  544 |                     .structural_layers
  545 |                     .first()
  546 |                     .and_then(|layer| layer.layer.as_ref())
  547 |                     .map_or(page.num_rows, |layer| match layer {
  548 |                         pbenc21::sparse_structural_layer::Layer::Validity(layer) => layer.num_slots,
  549 |                         pbenc21::sparse_structural_layer::Layer::List(layer) => layer.num_slots,
  550 |                         pbenc21::sparse_structural_layer::Layer::FixedSizeList(layer) => {
  551 |                             layer.num_slots
  552 |                         }
  553 |                     }),
  554 |                 _ => page.num_rows,
  555 |             },
  556 |             _ => page.num_rows,
  557 |         };
  558 |         rows.checked_add(page_rows)
  559 |             .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid_input_source("Column row count overflows u64".into()))
  560 |     })
  561 | }

  563 | pub(crate) fn verify_uniform_lengths(field_lengths: &[(&str, u64)]) -> Result<u64> {
  564 |     let first = field_lengths.first().map_or(0, |&(_, len)| len);
  565 |     if field_lengths.iter().all(|&(_, len)| len == first) {
  566 |         return Ok(first);
  567 |     }
  568 |     let columns = field_lengths
  569 |         .iter()
  570 |         .map(|(name, len)| format!("{name}={len}"))
  571 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  572 |         .join(", ");
  573 |     Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  574 |         "cannot read columns of differing lengths together ({columns}); \
  575 |          read each column (or equal-length group) separately"
  576 |     )))
  577 | }

  691 |     async fn read_tail(scheduler: &FileScheduler) -> Result<(Bytes, u64)> {
  692 |         let file_size = scheduler.reader().size().await? as u64;
  693 |         let begin = if file_size < scheduler.reader().block_size() as u64 {
  694 |             0
  695 |         } else {
  696 |             file_size - scheduler.reader().block_size() as u64
  697 |         };

  702 |     async fn read_range_from_tail_or_scheduler(
  703 |         tail_bytes: &Bytes,
  704 |         tail_offset: u64,
  705 |         scheduler: &FileScheduler,
  706 |         range: Range<u64>,
  707 |     ) -> Result<Bytes> {
  708 |         let tail_end = tail_offset + tail_bytes.len() as u64;
  709 |         if range.start >= tail_offset && range.end <= tail_end {
  710 |             let rel_start = (range.start - tail_offset) as usize;
  711 |             let rel_end = (range.end - tail_offset) as usize;
  712 |             Ok(tail_bytes.slice(rel_start..rel_end))
  713 |         } else {
  714 |             scheduler.submit_single(range, 0).await
  715 |         }
  716 |     }

  718 |     fn retained_global_buffers_from_tail(
  719 |         gbo_table: &[BufferDescriptor],
  720 |         tail_bytes: &Bytes,
  721 |         tail_offset: u64,
  722 |         file_len: u64,
  723 |     ) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, Bytes>> {
  724 |         let tail_end = tail_offset
  725 |             .checked_add(tail_bytes.len() as u64)
  726 |             .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid_input_source("Tail byte range overflows".into()))?;
  727 |         let mut retained_buffers = BTreeMap::new();
  728 |         for (index, buffer) in gbo_table.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
  729 |             let range = buffer.checked_range(index, file_len)?;
  730 |             if range.start >= tail_offset && range.end <= tail_end {
  731 |                 let rel_start = (range.start - tail_offset) as usize;
  732 |                 let rel_end = (range.end - tail_offset) as usize;
  733 |                 let bytes = Bytes::copy_from_slice(&tail_bytes[rel_start..rel_end]);
  734 |                 retained_buffers.insert(index as u32, bytes);
  735 |             }
  736 |         }
  737 |         Ok(retained_buffers)
  738 |     }

  740 |     // Checks to make sure the footer is written correctly and returns the
  741 |     // position of the file descriptor (which comes from the footer)
  742 |     fn decode_footer(footer_bytes: &Bytes) -> Result<Footer> {
  743 |         let len = footer_bytes.len();
  744 |         if len < FOOTER_LEN {
  745 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  746 |                 "does not have sufficient data, len: {}, bytes: {:?}",
  747 |                 len, footer_bytes
  748 |             )));
  749 |         }
  750 |         let mut cursor = Cursor::new(footer_bytes.slice(len - FOOTER_LEN..));
  751 | 
  752 |         let column_meta_start = cursor.read_u64::<LittleEndian>()?;
  753 |         let column_meta_offsets_start = cursor.read_u64::<LittleEndian>()?;
  754 |         let global_buff_offsets_start = cursor.read_u64::<LittleEndian>()?;
  755 |         let num_global_buffers = cursor.read_u32::<LittleEndian>()?;
  756 |         let num_columns = cursor.read_u32::<LittleEndian>()?;
  757 |         let major_version = cursor.read_u16::<LittleEndian>()?;
  758 |         let minor_version = cursor.read_u16::<LittleEndian>()?;
  759 | 
  760 |         let magic_bytes = footer_bytes.slice(len - 4..);
  761 |         if magic_bytes.as_ref() != MAGIC {
  762 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  763 |                 "file does not appear to be a Lance file (invalid magic: {:?})",
  764 |                 MAGIC
  765 |             )));
  766 |         }
  767 |         Ok(Footer {
  768 |             column_meta_start,
  769 |             column_meta_offsets_start,
  770 |             global_buff_offsets_start,
  771 |             num_global_buffers,
  772 |             num_columns,
  773 |             major_version,
  774 |             minor_version,
  775 |         })
  776 |     }

  794 |     // TODO: Once we have coalesced I/O we should only read the column metadatas that we need
  795 |     fn read_all_column_metadata(
  796 |         column_metadata_bytes: Bytes,
  797 |         footer: &Footer,
  798 |     ) -> Result<Vec<pbfile::ColumnMetadata>> {
  799 |         let column_metadata_start = footer.column_meta_start;
  800 |         // cmo == column_metadata_offsets
  801 |         let cmo_table_size = 16 * footer.num_columns as usize;
  802 |         if column_metadata_bytes.len() < cmo_table_size {
  803 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  804 |                 "column metadata region has {} bytes but CMO table needs {} bytes for {} columns",
  805 |                 column_metadata_bytes.len(),
  806 |                 cmo_table_size,
  807 |                 footer.num_columns
  808 |             )));
  809 |         }
  810 |         let cmo_table = column_metadata_bytes.slice(column_metadata_bytes.len() - cmo_table_size..);
  811 |         let column_metadata_offsets = Self::decode_cmo_table(cmo_table, footer)?;
  812 | 
  813 |         column_metadata_offsets
  814 |             .iter()
  815 |             .map(|(position, length)| {
  816 |                 let normalized_position = (*position - column_metadata_start) as usize;
  817 |                 let normalized_end = normalized_position + (*length as usize);
  818 |                 Ok(pbfile::ColumnMetadata::decode(
  819 |                     &column_metadata_bytes[normalized_position..normalized_end],
  820 |                 )?)
  821 |             })
  822 |             .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()
  823 |     }
  824 | 
  825 |     fn decode_cmo_table(cmo_table: Bytes, footer: &Footer) -> Result<Arc<[(u64, u64)]>> {
  826 |         let expected_size = 16 * footer.num_columns as usize;
  827 |         if cmo_table.len() != expected_size {
  828 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  829 |                 "column metadata offset table has {} bytes but expected {} bytes for {} columns",
  830 |                 cmo_table.len(),
  831 |                 expected_size,
  832 |                 footer.num_columns
  833 |             )));
  834 |         }
  835 | 
  836 |         let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(footer.num_columns as usize);
  837 |         for col_idx in 0..footer.num_columns {
  838 |             let offset = (col_idx * 16) as usize;
  839 |             let position = LittleEndian::read_u64(&cmo_table[offset..offset + 8]);
  840 |             let length = LittleEndian::read_u64(&cmo_table[offset + 8..offset + 16]);
  841 |             let end = position.checked_add(length).ok_or_else(|| {
  842 |                 Error::invalid_input(format!(
  843 |                     "column metadata range overflows for column index {}, position={}, length={}",
  844 |                     col_idx, position, length
  845 |                 ))
  846 |             })?;
  847 |             if position < footer.column_meta_start || end > footer.column_meta_offsets_start {
  848 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  849 |                     "column metadata range for column index {} is outside metadata region: position={}, length={}, metadata_start={}, cmo_start={}",
  850 |                     col_idx,
  851 |                     position,
  852 |                     length,
  853 |                     footer.column_meta_start,
  854 |                     footer.column_meta_offsets_start
  855 |                 )));
  856 |             }
  857 |             offsets.push((position, length));
  858 |         }
  859 | 
  860 |         Ok(Arc::from(offsets))
  861 |     }

  863 |     async fn optimistic_tail_read(
  864 |         data: &Bytes,
  865 |         start_pos: u64,
  866 |         scheduler: &FileScheduler,
  867 |         file_len: u64,
  868 |     ) -> Result<Bytes> {
  869 |         let num_bytes_needed = file_len.checked_sub(start_pos).ok_or_else(|| {
  870 |             Error::invalid_input_source(
  871 |                 format!(
  872 |                     "Tail read position {} is outside file of size {}",
  873 |                     start_pos, file_len
  874 |                 )
  875 |                 .into(),
  876 |             )
  877 |         })? as usize;
  878 |         if data.len() >= num_bytes_needed {
  879 |             Ok(data.slice((data.len() - num_bytes_needed)..))
  880 |         } else {
  881 |             let num_bytes_missing = (num_bytes_needed - data.len()) as u64;
  882 |             let start = file_len - num_bytes_needed as u64;
  883 |             let missing_bytes = scheduler
  884 |                 .submit_single(start..start + num_bytes_missing, 0)
  885 |                 .await?;
  886 |             let mut combined = BytesMut::with_capacity(data.len() + num_bytes_missing as usize);
  887 |             combined.extend(missing_bytes);
  888 |             combined.extend(data);
  889 |             Ok(combined.freeze())
  890 |         }
  891 |     }

  896 |         let mut global_buffers = Vec::with_capacity(footer.num_global_buffers as usize);

  900 |             global_buffers.push(BufferDescriptor {
  901 |                 position: buf_pos,
  902 |                 size: buf_size,
  903 |             });
  904 |         }

  906 |         Ok(global_buffers)

  954 |     pub(crate) async fn read_raw_metadata_for_dispatch(
  955 |         scheduler: &FileScheduler,
  956 |     ) -> Result<RawFileMetadataOpen> {
  957 |         let (tail_bytes, file_len) = Self::read_tail(scheduler).await?;
  958 |         let tail_offset = file_len - tail_bytes.len() as u64;
  959 |         let footer = Self::decode_footer(&tail_bytes)?;
  960 |         let version =
  961 |             ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers(footer.major_version, footer.minor_version)?;
  962 |         if version == ConcreteFileVersion::V1 {
  963 |             return Ok(RawFileMetadataOpen::Legacy {
  964 |                 major_version: footer.major_version,
  965 |                 minor_version: footer.minor_version,
  966 |             });
  967 |         }
  968 | 
  969 |         let gbo_table =
  970 |             Self::decode_gbo_table(&tail_bytes, file_len, scheduler, &footer, version).await?;
  971 |         if gbo_table.is_empty() {
  972 |             return Err(Error::internal(
  973 |                 "File did not contain any global buffers, schema expected".to_string(),
  974 |             ));
  975 |         }
  976 |         let schema_start = gbo_table[0].position;
  977 |         let schema_size = gbo_table[0].size;
  978 |         let num_footer_bytes = file_len.checked_sub(schema_start).ok_or_else(|| {
  979 |             Error::invalid_input_source(
  980 |                 format!(
  981 |                     "Schema position {} is outside file of size {}",
  982 |                     schema_start, file_len
  983 |                 )
  984 |                 .into(),
  985 |             )
  986 |         })?;
  987 |         let all_metadata_bytes =
  988 |             Self::optimistic_tail_read(&tail_bytes, schema_start, scheduler, file_len).await?;
  989 |         let schema_bytes = all_metadata_bytes.slice(0..schema_size as usize);
  990 |         let (num_rows, schema) = Self::decode_schema(schema_bytes)?;
  991 | 
  992 |         let column_metadata_start = (footer.column_meta_start - schema_start) as usize;
  993 |         let column_metadata_end = (footer.global_buff_offsets_start - schema_start) as usize;
  994 |         let column_metadata_bytes =
  995 |             all_metadata_bytes.slice(column_metadata_start..column_metadata_end);
  996 |         let column_metadatas = Self::read_all_column_metadata(column_metadata_bytes, &footer)?;
  997 | 
  998 |         let num_global_buffer_bytes = gbo_table.iter().map(|buf| buf.size).sum::<u64>();
  999 |         let num_data_bytes = footer.column_meta_start - num_global_buffer_bytes;
 1000 |         let num_column_metadata_bytes = footer.global_buff_offsets_start - footer.column_meta_start;
 1001 |         // The tail read above already pulled in any global buffer that lives within
 1002 |         // the captured window. Copy those user buffers (index >= 1; the schema at 0
 1003 |         // is decoded above and never fetched via read_global_buffer) out of the tail
 1004 |         // so read_global_buffer can serve them without I/O. We copy rather than slice
 1005 |         // so the much larger tail allocation can be released once decoding is done.
 1006 |         let retained_global_buffers = Self::retained_global_buffers_from_tail(

 1031 |     async fn read_raw_metadata_index_with_known_schema(

 1033 |         known_schema: Option<(Arc<Schema>, u64)>,

 1046 |             ));

 1049 |             Some((file_schema, num_rows)) => (file_schema, num_rows),
 1050 |             None => {

 1064 | 
 1065 |         let cmo_table = Self::read_range_from_tail_or_scheduler(
 1066 |             &tail_bytes,
 1067 |             tail_offset,
 1068 |             scheduler,

 1419 |     pub(crate) fn read_prepared_blocking(
 1420 |         &self,
 1421 |         params: ReadBatchParams,
 1422 |         batch_size: u32,
 1423 |         prepared: PreparedProjection,
 1424 |         read_len: u64,
 1425 |         filter: FilterExpression,
 1426 |     ) -> Result<Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send + 'static>> {
 1427 |         let projection = prepared.decoder_projection;
 1428 |         let verify_bound = |params: &ReadBatchParams, bound: u64, inclusive: bool| {
 1429 |             if bound > read_len || (bound == read_len && inclusive) {
 1430 |                 Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
 1431 |                     "cannot read {params:?} from columns with {read_len} rows"
 1432 |                 )))
 1433 |             } else {
 1434 |                 Ok(())
 1435 |             }
 1436 |         };
 1437 |         match &params {
 1438 |             ReadBatchParams::Indices(indices) => {
 1439 |                 for index in indices {
 1440 |                     match index {
 1441 |                         None => return Err(Error::invalid_input("Null value in indices array")),
 1442 |                         Some(index) => verify_bound(&params, index as u64, true)?,
 1443 |                     }
 1444 |                 }
 1445 |                 let indices = indices.iter().map(|index| index.unwrap() as u64).collect();
 1446 |                 self.take_rows_blocking(indices, batch_size, projection, filter)
 1447 |             }
 1448 |             ReadBatchParams::Range(range) => {
 1449 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.end as u64, false)?;
 1450 |                 self.read_range_blocking(
 1451 |                     range.start as u64..range.end as u64,
 1452 |                     batch_size,
 1453 |                     projection,
 1454 |                     filter,
 1455 |                 )
 1456 |             }
 1457 |             ReadBatchParams::Ranges(ranges) => {
 1458 |                 let mut ranges_u64 = Vec::with_capacity(ranges.len());
 1459 |                 for range in ranges.as_ref() {
 1460 |                     verify_bound(&params, range.end, false)?;
 1461 |                     ranges_u64.push(range.start..range.end);
 1462 |                 }
 1463 |                 self.read_ranges_blocking(ranges_u64, batch_size, projection, filter)
 1464 |             }
 1465 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFrom(range) => {
 1466 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.start as u64, true)?;
 1467 |                 self.read_range_blocking(
 1468 |                     range.start as u64..read_len,
 1469 |                     batch_size,
 1470 |                     projection,
 1471 |                     filter,
 1472 |                 )
 1473 |             }
 1474 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeTo(range) => {
 1475 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.end as u64, false)?;
 1476 |                 self.read_range_blocking(0..range.end as u64, batch_size, projection, filter)
 1477 |             }
 1478 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFull => {
 1479 |                 self.read_range_blocking(0..read_len, batch_size, projection, filter)
 1480 |             }
 1481 |         }
 1482 |     }

 1620 |     pub(crate) async fn load_indexed_column_infos<F>(
 1621 |         metadata_index: &FileMetadataIndex,
 1622 |         io: &Arc<dyn EncodingsIo>,
 1623 |         cache: &Arc<LanceCache>,
 1624 |         column_indices: &[u32],
 1625 |         decode_column: F,
 1626 |     ) -> Result<Vec<Arc<ColumnInfo>>>
 1627 |     where
 1628 |         F: Fn(u32, &pbfile::ColumnMetadata) -> Result<Arc<ColumnInfo>>,
 1629 |     {
 1630 |         let mut column_infos = vec![None; column_indices.len()];
 1631 |         let mut missing_columns = Vec::new();
 1632 | 
 1633 |         for (result_index, column_index) in column_indices.iter().copied().enumerate() {
 1634 |             let cache_key = ColumnMetadataCacheKey { column_index };
 1635 |             if let Some(cached) = cache.get_with_key(&cache_key).await {
 1636 |                 column_infos[result_index] = Some(cached.column_info.clone());
 1637 |             } else {
 1638 |                 let range = Self::column_metadata_range(metadata_index, column_index)?;
 1639 |                 missing_columns.push((result_index, column_index, range));
 1640 |             }
 1641 |         }
 1642 | 
 1643 |         missing_columns.sort_by_key(|(_, _, range)| range.start);
 1644 |         if !missing_columns.is_empty() {
 1645 |             let ranges = missing_columns
 1646 |                 .iter()
 1647 |                 .map(|(_, _, range)| range.clone())
 1648 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1649 |             let metadata_bytes = io.submit_request(ranges, 0).await?;
 1650 |             for ((result_index, column_index, _), bytes) in
 1651 |                 missing_columns.into_iter().zip(metadata_bytes)
 1652 |             {
 1653 |                 let column_metadata = pbfile::ColumnMetadata::decode(bytes)?;
 1654 |                 let column_info = decode_column(column_index, &column_metadata)?;
 1655 |                 let cached = Arc::new(CachedColumnMetadata {
 1656 |                     column_metadata,
 1657 |                     column_info: column_info.clone(),
 1658 |                 });
 1659 |                 let cache_key = ColumnMetadataCacheKey { column_index };
 1660 |                 cache.insert_with_key(&cache_key, cached).await;
 1661 |                 column_infos[result_index] = Some(column_info);
 1662 |             }
 1663 |         }
 1664 | 
 1665 |         column_infos
 1666 |             .into_iter()
 1667 |             .enumerate()
 1668 |             .map(|(idx, column_info)| {
 1669 |                 column_info.ok_or_else(|| {
 1670 |                     Error::internal(format!(
 1671 |                         "lazy metadata loader did not load requested projection column at position {}",
 1672 |                         idx
 1673 |                     ))
 1674 |                 })
 1675 |             })
 1676 |             .collect()
 1677 |     }
 1678 | }

 1819 |     pub(crate) async fn read_prepared_tasks(
 1820 |         &self,
 1821 |         params: ReadBatchParams,
 1822 |         batch_size: u32,
 1823 |         prepared: PreparedProjection,
 1824 |         read_len: u64,
 1825 |         filter: FilterExpression,
 1826 |     ) -> Result<Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = ReadBatchTask> + Send>>> {
 1827 |         let verify_bound = |params: &ReadBatchParams, bound: u64, inclusive: bool| {
 1828 |             if bound > read_len || (bound == read_len && inclusive) {
 1829 |                 Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
 1830 |                     "cannot read {params:?} from columns with {read_len} rows"
 1831 |                 )))
 1832 |             } else {
 1833 |                 Ok(())
 1834 |             }
 1835 |         };
 1836 |         match &params {
 1837 |             ReadBatchParams::Indices(indices) => {
 1838 |                 for idx in indices {
 1839 |                     match idx {
 1840 |                         None => {
 1841 |                             return Err(Error::invalid_input("Null value in indices array"));
 1842 |                         }
 1843 |                         Some(idx) => {
 1844 |                             verify_bound(&params, idx as u64, true)?;
 1845 |                         }
 1846 |                     }
 1847 |                 }
 1848 |                 let indices = indices.iter().map(|idx| idx.unwrap() as u64).collect();
 1849 |                 self.take_rows(indices, batch_size, prepared).await
 1850 |             }
 1851 |             ReadBatchParams::Range(range) => {
 1852 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.end as u64, false)?;
 1853 |                 self.read_range(
 1854 |                     range.start as u64..range.end as u64,
 1855 |                     batch_size,
 1856 |                     prepared,
 1857 |                     filter,
 1858 |                 )
 1859 |                 .await
 1860 |             }
 1861 |             ReadBatchParams::Ranges(ranges) => {
 1862 |                 let mut ranges_u64 = Vec::with_capacity(ranges.len());
 1863 |                 for range in ranges.as_ref() {
 1864 |                     verify_bound(&params, range.end, false)?;
 1865 |                     ranges_u64.push(range.start..range.end);
 1866 |                 }
 1867 |                 self.read_ranges(ranges_u64, batch_size, prepared, filter)
 1868 |                     .await
 1869 |             }
 1870 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFrom(range) => {
 1871 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.start as u64, true)?;
 1872 |                 self.read_range(range.start as u64..read_len, batch_size, prepared, filter)
 1873 |                     .await
 1874 |             }
 1875 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeTo(range) => {
 1876 |                 verify_bound(&params, range.end as u64, false)?;
 1877 |                 self.read_range(0..range.end as u64, batch_size, prepared, filter)
 1878 |                     .await
 1879 |             }
 1880 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFull => {
 1881 |                 self.read_range(0..read_len, batch_size, prepared, filter)
 1882 |                     .await
 1883 |             }
 1884 |         }
 1885 |     }
 1886 | }

 2309 |                             }

 2319 |                             }
 2320 |                         }

  463 |     async fn write_struct_array(
  464 |         object_writer: &mut dyn Writer,
  465 |         field: &Field,
  466 |         arrays: &[&StructArray],
  467 |         batch_id: i32,
  468 |         page_table: &mut PageTable,
  469 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  470 |         arrays
  471 |             .iter()
  472 |             .for_each(|a| assert_eq!(a.num_columns(), field.children.len()));
  473 | 
  474 |         for child in &field.children {
  475 |             let mut arrs: Vec<&ArrayRef> = Vec::new();
  476 |             for struct_array in arrays {
  477 |                 let arr = struct_array
  478 |                     .column_by_name(&child.name)
  479 |                     .ok_or(Error::schema(format!(
  480 |                         "FileWriter: schema mismatch: column {} does not exist in array: {:?}",
  481 |                         child.name,
  482 |                         struct_array.data_type()
  483 |                     )))?;
  484 |                 arrs.push(arr);
  485 |             }
  486 |             Self::write_array(object_writer, child, arrs.as_slice(), batch_id, page_table).await?;
  487 |         }
  488 |         Ok(())

  491 |     async fn write_list_array(
  492 |         object_writer: &mut dyn Writer,
  493 |         field: &Field,
  494 |         arrs: &[&dyn Array],
  495 |         batch_id: i32,
  496 |         page_table: &mut PageTable,
  497 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  498 |         let capacity: usize = arrs.iter().map(|a| a.len()).sum();
  499 |         let mut list_arrs: Vec<ArrayRef> = Vec::new();
  500 |         let mut pos_builder: PrimitiveBuilder<Int32Type> =
  501 |             PrimitiveBuilder::with_capacity(capacity);
  502 | 
  503 |         let mut last_offset: usize = 0;
  504 |         pos_builder.append_value(last_offset as i32);
  505 |         for array in arrs.iter() {
  506 |             let list_arr = as_list_array(*array);
  507 |             let offsets = list_arr.value_offsets();
  508 | 
  509 |             assert!(!offsets.is_empty());
  510 |             let start_offset = offsets[0].as_usize();
  511 |             let end_offset = offsets[offsets.len() - 1].as_usize();
  512 | 
  513 |             let list_values = list_arr.values();
  514 |             let sliced_values = list_values.slice(start_offset, end_offset - start_offset);
  515 |             list_arrs.push(sliced_values);
  516 | 
  517 |             offsets
  518 |                 .iter()
  519 |                 .skip(1)
  520 |                 .map(|b| b.as_usize() - start_offset + last_offset)
  521 |                 .for_each(|o| pos_builder.append_value(o as i32));
  522 |             last_offset = pos_builder.values_slice()[pos_builder.len() - 1_usize] as usize;
  523 |         }
  524 | 
  525 |         let positions: &dyn Array = &pos_builder.finish();
  526 |         Self::write_fixed_stride_array(object_writer, field, &[positions], batch_id, page_table)
  527 |             .await?;
  528 |         let arrs = list_arrs.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  529 |         Self::write_array(
  530 |             object_writer,
  531 |             &field.children[0],
  532 |             arrs.as_slice(),
  533 |             batch_id,
  534 |             page_table,
  535 |         )
  536 |         .await
  537 |     }

  588 |     async fn write_statistics(&mut self) -> Result<Option<StatisticsMetadata>> {
  589 |         let statistics = self
  590 |             .stats_collector
  591 |             .as_mut()
  592 |             .map(|collector| collector.finish());
  593 | 
  594 |         match statistics {
  595 |             Some(Ok(stats_batch)) if stats_batch.num_rows() > 0 => {
  596 |                 debug_assert_eq!(self.next_batch_id() as usize, stats_batch.num_rows());
  597 |                 let schema = Schema::try_from(stats_batch.schema().as_ref())?;
  598 |                 let leaf_field_ids = schema.field_ids();
  599 | 
  600 |                 let mut stats_page_table = PageTable::default();
  601 |                 for (i, field) in schema.fields.iter().enumerate() {
  602 |                     Self::write_array(
  603 |                         self.object_writer.as_mut(),
  604 |                         field,
  605 |                         &[stats_batch.column(i)],
  606 |                         0, // Only one batch for statistics.
  607 |                         &mut stats_page_table,
  608 |                     )
  609 |                     .await?;
  610 |                 }
  611 | 
  612 |                 let page_table_position = stats_page_table
  613 |                     .write(self.object_writer.as_mut(), 0)
  614 |                     .await?;
  615 | 
  616 |                 Ok(Some(StatisticsMetadata {
  617 |                     schema,
  618 |                     leaf_field_ids,
  619 |                     page_table_position,
  620 |                 }))
  621 |             }
  622 |             Some(Err(e)) => Err(e),
  623 |             _ => Ok(None),
  624 |         }
  625 |     }

  627 |     async fn write_footer(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  628 |         // Step 1. Write page table.
  629 |         let field_id_offset = *self.schema.field_ids().iter().min().unwrap();
  630 |         let pos = self
  631 |             .page_table
  632 |             .write(self.object_writer.as_mut(), field_id_offset)
  633 |             .await?;
  634 |         self.metadata.page_table_position = pos;
  635 | 
  636 |         // Step 2. Write statistics.
  637 |         self.metadata.stats_metadata = self.write_statistics().await?;
  638 | 
  639 |         // Step 3. Write manifest and dictionary values.
  640 |         write_schema_dictionaries(self.object_writer.as_mut(), &mut self.schema).await?;
  641 |         let pos = M::store_schema(self.object_writer.as_mut(), &self.schema).await?;

  643 |         // Step 4. Write metadata.

  654 | /// Walk through the schema and return arrays with their Lance field.
  655 | ///
  656 | /// This skips over nested arrays and fields within list arrays. It does walk
  657 | /// over the children of structs.
  658 | fn fields_in_batches<'a>(
  659 |     batches: &'a [RecordBatch],
  660 |     schema: &'a Schema,
  661 | ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'a Field, Vec<&'a ArrayRef>)> {
  662 |     let num_columns = batches[0].num_columns();
  663 |     let array_iters = (0..num_columns).map(|col_i| {
  664 |         batches
  665 |             .iter()
  666 |             .map(|batch| batch.column(col_i))
  667 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  668 |     });
  669 |     let mut to_visit: Vec<(&'a Field, Vec<&'a ArrayRef>)> =
  670 |         schema.fields.iter().zip(array_iters).collect();
  671 | 
  672 |     std::iter::from_fn(move || {
  673 |         loop {
  674 |             let (field, arrays): (_, Vec<&'a ArrayRef>) = to_visit.pop()?;
  675 |             match field.data_type() {
  676 |                 DataType::Struct(_) => {
  677 |                     for (i, child_field) in field.children.iter().enumerate() {
  678 |                         let child_arrays = arrays
  679 |                             .iter()
  680 |                             .map(|arr| as_struct_array(*arr).column(i))
  681 |                             .collect::<Vec<&'a ArrayRef>>();
  682 |                         to_visit.push((child_field, child_arrays));
  683 |                     }
  684 |                     continue;
  685 |                 }
  686 |                 // We only walk structs right now.
  687 |                 _ if field.data_type().is_nested() => continue,
  688 |                 _ => return Some((field, arrays)),
  689 |             }
  690 |         }
  691 |     })
  692 | }

  308 |             self.write_batch(batch).await?;
  309 |         }
  310 |         Ok(())
  311 |     }

  366 |             .extend(std::mem::take(&mut schema.metadata));

  379 |     fn field_arrays(&self, batch: &RecordBatch) -> Result<Vec<(usize, ArrayRef)>> {
  380 |         self.schema
  381 |             .as_ref()
  382 |             .unwrap()
  383 |             .fields
  384 |             .iter()
  385 |             .enumerate()
  386 |             .map(|(field_idx, field)| {
  387 |                 let array =
  388 |                     batch
  389 |                         .column_by_name(&field.name)
  390 |                         .ok_or(Error::invalid_input_source(
  391 |                             format!(
  392 |                                 "Cannot write batch.  The batch was missing the column `{}`",
  393 |                                 field.name
  394 |                             )
  395 |                             .into(),
  396 |                         ))?;
  397 |                 Ok((field_idx, array.clone()))
  398 |             })
  399 |             .collect()
  400 |     }
  401 | 
  402 |     // Encode a set of `(field index, array)` pairs, each advancing only its own
  403 |     // column. Each task captures its field's current row offset at encode time,
  404 |     // so `advance_columns` must run after this call (never before); the order of
  405 |     // the returned tasks relative to `write_pages` does not matter.
  406 |     fn encode_columns(
  407 |         &mut self,
  408 |         field_arrays: &[(usize, ArrayRef)],
  409 |         external_buffers: &mut OutOfLineBuffers,
  410 |     ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<EncodeTask>>> {
  411 |         // Snapshot the starting row number of each field before borrowing the
  412 |         // column writers mutably below.
  413 |         let row_numbers = field_arrays
  414 |             .iter()
  415 |             .map(|(field_idx, _)| self.field_rows_written[*field_idx])
  416 |             .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  417 |         field_arrays
  418 |             .iter()
  419 |             .zip(row_numbers)
  420 |             .map(|((field_idx, array), row_number)| {
  421 |                 let repdef = RepDefBuilder::default();
  422 |                 let num_rows = array.len() as u64;
  423 |                 self.column_writers[*field_idx].maybe_encode(
  424 |                     array.clone(),
  425 |                     external_buffers,
  426 |                     repdef,
  427 |                     row_number,
  428 |                     num_rows,
  429 |                 )
  430 |             })
  431 |             .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()
  432 |     }
  433 | 
  434 |     // Advance the per-field row counters after a set of columns has been
  435 |     // written, keeping `rows_written` (the file's logical length) in sync as the
  436 |     // longest column. Only the written fields move, so their new totals fold into
  437 |     // `rows_written` directly without rescanning every field. (`write_batch`
  438 |     // advances every field uniformly and tracks this inline instead.)
  439 |     fn advance_columns(&mut self, field_arrays: &[(usize, ArrayRef)]) {
  440 |         for (field_idx, array) in field_arrays {
  441 |             let new_total = self.field_rows_written[*field_idx] + array.len() as u64;
  442 |             self.field_rows_written[*field_idx] = new_total;
  443 |             self.rows_written = self.rows_written.max(new_total);
  444 |         }
  445 |     }
  446 | 
  447 |     /// Schedule a batch of data to be written to the file
  448 |     ///
  449 |     /// Note: the future returned by this method may complete before the data has been fully
  450 |     /// flushed to the file (some data may be in the data cache or the I/O cache)
  451 |     pub async fn write_batch(&mut self, batch: &RecordBatch) -> Result<()> {
  452 |         debug!(
  453 |             "write_batch called with {} rows, {} columns, and {} bytes of data",
  454 |             batch.num_rows(),
  455 |             batch.num_columns(),
  456 |             batch.get_array_memory_size()
  457 |         );
  458 |         self.ensure_initialized(batch)?;
  459 |         let schema = self
  460 |             .schema
  461 |             .as_ref()
  462 |             .expect("ensure_initialized sets the schema");
  463 |         self.expected_types
  464 |             .get_or_insert_with(|| ExpectedTypes::new(schema))
  465 |             .check_batch(batch)?;
  466 |         let field_arrays = self.field_arrays(batch)?;
  467 |         let field_arrays = self.prepare_field_arrays(field_arrays)?;
  468 |         let num_rows = batch.num_rows() as u64;
  469 |         if num_rows == 0 {
  470 |             return Ok(());
  471 |         }
  472 |         if num_rows > u32::MAX as u64 {
  473 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input_source(
  474 |                 "cannot write Lance files with more than 2^32 rows".into(),
  475 |             ));
  476 |         }
  477 |         // First we push each array into its column writer.  This may or may not generate enough
  478 |         // data to trigger an encoding task.  We collect any encoding tasks into a queue.
  479 |         let mut external_buffers =
  480 |             OutOfLineBuffers::new(self.tell().await?, PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT as u64);
  481 |         let encoding_tasks = self.encode_columns(&field_arrays, &mut external_buffers)?;
  482 |         // Next, write external buffers
  483 |         for external_buffer in external_buffers.take_buffers() {
  484 |             Self::do_write_buffer(&mut self.writer, &external_buffer).await?;
  485 |         }
  486 | 
  487 |         let encoding_tasks = encoding_tasks
  488 |             .into_iter()
  489 |             .flatten()
  490 |             .collect::<FuturesOrdered<_>>();
  491 | 
  492 |         // `write_batch` advances every field by the same amount, so the longest
  493 |         // column simply grows by `num_rows`. Guard against overflowing the row
  494 |         // counter.
  495 |         if self.rows_written.checked_add(num_rows).is_none() {
  496 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input_source(format!("cannot write batch with {} rows because {} rows have already been written and Lance files cannot contain more than 2^64 rows", num_rows, self.rows_written).into()));
  497 |         }
  498 |         for field_rows in self.field_rows_written.iter_mut() {
  499 |             *field_rows += num_rows;
  500 |         }
  501 |         self.rows_written += num_rows;
  502 | 
  503 |         self.write_pages(encoding_tasks).await?;
  504 | 
  505 |         Ok(())
  506 |     }
  507 | 
  508 |     /// Write a single column, advancing only that column's row counter.
  509 |     ///
  510 |     /// Unlike [`write_batch`](Self::write_batch), which advances every column
  511 |     /// from a single shared row counter, this method advances one column
  512 |     /// independently. Used across calls it produces a single file whose columns
  513 |     /// may have different item counts.
  514 |     ///
  515 |     /// `column_index` refers to a top-level field in the writer's schema (the
  516 |     /// same order as the schema's fields); a nested child cannot be targeted on
  517 |     /// its own. Because each call writes the whole field from a single array, the
  518 |     /// children of a struct field always advance together and stay equal-length;
  519 |     /// only different top-level fields can diverge in length. A column may be
  520 |     /// written across multiple calls; its values are appended. A field that is
  521 |     /// never written ends up as a zero-length column. The writer must have been
  522 |     /// created with an explicit schema (via [`try_new`](Self::try_new)); a lazy
  523 |     /// schema cannot be inferred here because individual calls need not cover
  524 |     /// every field.
  525 |     ///
  526 |     /// ```
  527 |     /// # use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array};
  528 |     /// # use std::sync::Arc;
  529 |     /// # use lance_file::writer::FileWriter;
  530 |     /// # async fn example(writer: &mut FileWriter) -> lance_core::Result<()> {
  531 |     /// // Field 0 gets three values, field 1 gets one — a non-rectangular file.
  532 |     /// writer.write_column(0, Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3]))).await?;
  533 |     /// writer.write_column(1, Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![10]))).await?;
  534 |     /// # Ok(())
  535 |     /// # }
  536 |     /// ```
  537 |     pub async fn write_column(&mut self, column_index: usize, array: ArrayRef) -> Result<()> {
  538 |         let schema = self.schema.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
  539 |             Error::invalid_input_source(
  540 |                 "write_column requires the writer to be created with an explicit schema".into(),
  541 |             )
  542 |         })?;
  543 |         if column_index >= schema.fields.len() {
  544 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input_source(
  545 |                 format!(
  546 |                     "write_column: field index {} is out of bounds (schema has {} fields)",
  547 |                     column_index,
  548 |                     schema.fields.len()
  549 |                 )
  550 |                 .into(),
  551 |             ));
  552 |         }
  553 |         if array.len() as u64 > u32::MAX as u64 {
  554 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input_source(
  555 |                 "cannot write Lance files with more than 2^32 rows".into(),
  556 |             ));
  557 |         }
  558 |         self.expected_types
  559 |             .get_or_insert_with(|| ExpectedTypes::new(schema))
  560 |             .check_column(column_index, &array)?;
  561 |         let array = self.column_writers[column_index].prepare_array(array)?;
  562 | 
  563 |         // A never-advanced field simply remains a zero-length column, which the
  564 |         // encoders handle at `finish` time.
  565 |         if array.is_empty() {
  566 |             return Ok(());
  567 |         }
  568 | 
  569 |         let columns = [(column_index, array)];
  570 |         let mut external_buffers =
  571 |             OutOfLineBuffers::new(self.tell().await?, PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT as u64);
  572 |         let encoding_tasks = self.encode_columns(&columns, &mut external_buffers)?;
  573 |         for external_buffer in external_buffers.take_buffers() {
  574 |             Self::do_write_buffer(&mut self.writer, &external_buffer).await?;
  575 |         }
  576 |         let encoding_tasks = encoding_tasks
  577 |             .into_iter()
  578 |             .flatten()
  579 |             .collect::<FuturesOrdered<_>>();
  580 | 
  581 |         self.advance_columns(&columns);
  582 |         self.write_pages(encoding_tasks).await?;
  583 |         Ok(())
  584 |     }

  586 |     async fn write_column_metadata(
  587 |         &mut self,
  588 |         metadata: pbfile::ColumnMetadata,
  589 |     ) -> Result<(u64, u64)> {
  590 |         let metadata_bytes = metadata.encode_to_vec();
  591 |         let position = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;

  597 |     async fn write_column_metadatas(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<(u64, u64)>> {
  598 |         let metadatas = std::mem::take(&mut self.column_metadata);
  599 | 
  600 |         // If spilling, finalize the spill writer and reopen for reading.
  601 |         // The spill file itself is cleaned up by the caller (it lives in a
  602 |         // temp directory managed by the caller's RAII guard).
  603 |         let spill_state = self.page_spill.take();
  604 |         let (spill_chunks, spill_reader) =
  605 |             if let Some(PageSpillState::Active(mut spill)) = spill_state {
  606 |                 spill.shutdown_writer().await?;
  607 |                 let reader = spill.object_store.open(&spill.path).await?;
  608 |                 let chunks = std::mem::take(&mut spill.column_chunks);
  609 |                 (chunks, Some(reader))
  610 |             } else {
  611 |                 (Vec::new(), None)
  612 |             };
  613 | 
  614 |         let mut metadata_positions = Vec::with_capacity(metadatas.len());
  615 |         for (col_idx, mut metadata) in metadatas.into_iter().enumerate() {
  616 |             if let Some(reader) = &spill_reader {
  617 |                 let mut pages = Vec::new();
  618 |                 for &(offset, len) in &spill_chunks[col_idx] {
  619 |                     let data = reader
  620 |                         .get_range(offset as usize..(offset as usize + len as usize))
  621 |                         .await
  622 |                         .map_err(|e| Error::io_source(Box::new(e)))?;
  623 |                     pages.extend(decode_spilled_chunk(&data)?);
  624 |                 }
  625 |                 metadata.pages = pages;
  626 |             }
  627 |             metadata_positions.push(self.write_column_metadata(metadata).await?);
  628 |         }
  629 | 
  630 |         Ok(metadata_positions)
  631 |     }

  647 |     async fn write_global_buffers(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<(u64, u64)>> {
  648 |         let schema = self.schema.as_mut().ok_or(Error::invalid_input("No schema provided on writer open and no data provided.  Schema is unknown and file cannot be created"))?;
  649 |         schema.metadata = std::mem::take(&mut self.schema_metadata);
  650 |         // Use descriptor layout for blob v2 fields in the footer to avoid exposing logical child fields.
  651 |         schema
  652 |             .fields
  653 |             .iter_mut()
  654 |             .for_each(|f| f.unload_blobs_recursive());

  656 |         let file_descriptor = Self::make_file_descriptor(schema, self.rows_written)?;
  657 |         let file_descriptor_bytes = file_descriptor.encode_to_vec();
  658 |         let file_descriptor_len = file_descriptor_bytes.len() as u64;
  659 |         let file_descriptor_position = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  660 |         self.writer.write_all(&file_descriptor_bytes).await?;
  661 |         let mut gbo_table = Vec::with_capacity(1 + self.global_buffers.len());
  662 |         gbo_table.push((file_descriptor_position, file_descriptor_len));
  663 |         gbo_table.append(&mut self.global_buffers);

  681 |     /// `column_metadata` must describe the buffers already persisted by the

  683 |     /// of rows in those buffers.
  684 |     pub fn initialize_with_external_metadata(
  685 |         &mut self,
  686 |         mut schema: lance_core::datatypes::Schema,
  687 |         column_metadata: Vec<pbfile::ColumnMetadata>,
  688 |         rows_written: u64,

  698 |     /// Adds a global buffer to the file
  699 |     ///
  700 |     /// The global buffer can contain any arbitrary bytes.  It will be written to the disk
  701 |     /// immediately.  This method returns the index of the global buffer (this will always
  702 |     /// start at 1 and increment by 1 each time this method is called)
  703 |     pub async fn add_global_buffer(&mut self, buffer: Bytes) -> Result<u32> {
  704 |         let position = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  705 |         let len = buffer.len() as u64;
  706 |         Self::do_write_buffer(&mut self.writer, &buffer).await?;
  707 |         self.global_buffers.push((position, len));
  708 |         Ok(self.global_buffers.len() as u32)
  709 |     }

  711 |     async fn finish_writers(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  712 |         let mut col_idx = 0;
  713 |         for mut writer in std::mem::take(&mut self.column_writers) {
  714 |             let mut external_buffers =
  715 |                 OutOfLineBuffers::new(self.tell().await?, PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT as u64);
  716 |             let columns = writer.finish(&mut external_buffers).await?;
  717 |             for buffer in external_buffers.take_buffers() {
  718 |                 self.writer.write_all(&buffer).await?;
  719 |             }
  720 |             debug_assert_eq!(
  721 |                 columns.len(),
  722 |                 writer.num_columns() as usize,
  723 |                 "Expected {} columns from column at index {} and got {}",
  724 |                 writer.num_columns(),
  725 |                 col_idx,
  726 |                 columns.len()
  727 |             );
  728 |             for column in columns {
  729 |                 for page in column.final_pages {
  730 |                     self.write_page(page).await?;
  731 |                 }
  732 |                 let column_metadata = &mut self.column_metadata[col_idx];
  733 |                 let mut buffer_pos = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  734 |                 for buffer in column.column_buffers {
  735 |                     column_metadata.buffer_offsets.push(buffer_pos);
  736 |                     let mut size = 0;
  737 |                     Self::do_write_buffer(&mut self.writer, &buffer).await?;
  738 |                     size += buffer.len() as u64;
  739 |                     buffer_pos += size;
  740 |                     column_metadata.buffer_sizes.push(size);
  741 |                 }
  742 |                 let encoded_encoding = Any::from_msg(&column.encoding)?.encode_to_vec();
  743 |                 column_metadata.encoding = Some(pbfile::Encoding {
  744 |                     location: Some(pbfile::encoding::Location::Direct(pbfile::DirectEncoding {
  745 |                         encoding: encoded_encoding,
  746 |                     })),
  747 |                 });
  748 |                 col_idx += 1;
  749 |             }
  750 |         }
  751 |         if col_idx != self.column_metadata.len() {
  752 |             panic!(
  753 |                 "Column writers finished with {} columns but we expected {}",
  754 |                 col_idx,
  755 |                 self.column_metadata.len()
  756 |             );
  757 |         }
  758 |         Ok(())
  759 |     }

  761 |     /// Finishes writing the file
  762 |     ///
  763 |     /// This method will wait until all data has been flushed to the file.  Then it
  764 |     /// will write the file metadata and the footer.  It will not return until all
  765 |     /// data has been flushed and the file has been closed.
  766 |     ///
  767 |     /// Returns a summary of the completed file write.
  768 |     pub async fn finish(&mut self) -> Result<FileWriteSummary> {
  769 |         // 1. flush any remaining data and write out those pages
  770 |         let mut external_buffers =
  771 |             OutOfLineBuffers::new(self.tell().await?, PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT as u64);
  772 |         let encoding_tasks = self
  773 |             .column_writers
  774 |             .iter_mut()
  775 |             .map(|writer| writer.flush(&mut external_buffers))
  776 |             .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  777 |         for external_buffer in external_buffers.take_buffers() {
  778 |             Self::do_write_buffer(&mut self.writer, &external_buffer).await?;
  779 |         }
  780 |         let encoding_tasks = encoding_tasks
  781 |             .into_iter()
  782 |             .flatten()
  783 |             .collect::<FuturesOrdered<_>>();
  784 |         self.write_pages(encoding_tasks).await?;
  785 | 
  786 |         if !self.column_writers.is_empty() {
  787 |             self.finish_writers().await?;
  788 |         }
  789 | 
  790 |         // 3. write global buffers (we write the schema here)
  791 |         let global_buffer_offsets = self.write_global_buffers().await?;
  792 |         let num_global_buffers = global_buffer_offsets.len() as u32;
  793 | 
  794 |         // 4. write the column metadatas
  795 |         let column_metadata_start = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  796 |         let metadata_positions = self.write_column_metadatas().await?;
  797 | 
  798 |         // 5. write the column metadata offset table
  799 |         let cmo_table_start = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  800 |         for (meta_pos, meta_len) in metadata_positions {
  801 |             self.writer.write_u64_le(meta_pos).await?;
  802 |             self.writer.write_u64_le(meta_len).await?;
  803 |         }
  804 | 
  805 |         // 6. write global buffers offset table
  806 |         let gbo_table_start = self.writer.tell().await? as u64;
  807 |         for (gbo_pos, gbo_len) in global_buffer_offsets {
  808 |             self.writer.write_u64_le(gbo_pos).await?;
  809 |             self.writer.write_u64_le(gbo_len).await?;
  810 |         }
  811 | 
  812 |         // 7. write the footer
  813 |         self.writer.write_u64_le(column_metadata_start).await?;
  814 |         self.writer.write_u64_le(cmo_table_start).await?;
  815 |         self.writer.write_u64_le(gbo_table_start).await?;

  487 |             (None, _) => 0,
  488 |             (Some(nulls), None) => nulls.null_count(),
  489 |             (Some(nulls), Some(reachable)) => (&!nulls.inner() & reachable).count_set_bits(),

  498 |             return Ok(());

  501 |         // children are addressed through offsets, so the parent's validity
  502 |         // does not map onto them and they are checked as before.
  503 |         let Some(parent) = array.as_any().downcast_ref::<StructArray>() else {

  309 | /// Refuse reads from manifests whose required reader features this build does
  310 | /// not support or whose paired capabilities are inconsistent.
  311 | pub fn ensure_can_read_manifest(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  312 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  313 |     if !can_read_dataset(manifest.reader_feature_flags) {
  314 |         return Err(Error::not_supported_source(
  315 |             format!(
  316 |                 "This dataset cannot be read by this version of Lance. Please upgrade \
  317 |                  Lance to read this dataset. Flags: {}",
  318 |                 manifest.reader_feature_flags
  319 |             )
  320 |             .into(),
  321 |         ));
  322 |     }
  323 |     Ok(())
  324 | }
  325 | 
  326 | /// Refuse writes to manifests whose required writer features this build does
  327 | /// not support or whose paired capabilities are inconsistent.
  328 | pub fn ensure_can_write_manifest(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  329 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  330 |     if !can_write_dataset(manifest.writer_feature_flags) {
  331 |         return Err(Error::not_supported_source(
  332 |             format!(
  333 |                 "This dataset cannot be written by this version of Lance. Please upgrade \
  334 |                  Lance to write this dataset. Flags: {}",
  335 |                 manifest.writer_feature_flags
  336 |             )
  337 |             .into(),
  338 |         ));
  339 |     }
  340 |     Ok(())
  341 | }
  342 | 
  343 | pub fn has_deprecated_v2_feature_flag(writer_flags: u64) -> bool {
  344 |     writer_flags & FLAG_USE_V2_FORMAT_DEPRECATED != 0
  345 | }
  346 | 
  347 | /// Refuse a manifest whose paired reader and writer capability bits disagree.
  348 | ///
  349 | /// One word set and the other not is neither mode: it would let a legacy reader
  350 | /// or a legacy writer through on a table where the other half is enforcing. The
  351 | /// commit path refuses to *produce* this, so seeing it on read means the
  352 | /// manifest was written by something that did not.
  353 | pub fn validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  354 |     if (manifest.reader_feature_flags ^ manifest.writer_feature_flags) & FLAG_FRAGMENT_REUSE_INDEX
  355 |         != 0
  356 |     {
  357 |         return Err(Error::corrupt_file_named(
  358 |             "manifest",
  359 |             "FRI requires both reader and writer feature flags",
  360 |         ));
  361 |     }
  362 | 
  363 |     let reader = manifest.reader_feature_flags & FLAG_MIXED_DATA_FILE_VERSIONS != 0;
  364 |     let writer = manifest.writer_feature_flags & FLAG_MIXED_DATA_FILE_VERSIONS != 0;
  365 |     if reader != writer {
  366 |         return Err(Error::corrupt_file_named(
  367 |             "manifest",
  368 |             "Manifest has only one of the mixed data-file-version reader and writer feature bits set, \
  369 |              so its semantics are undefined",
  370 |         ));
  371 |     }
  372 |     Ok(())
  373 | }
  374 | 
  375 | fn validated_sticky_paired_flags(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<u64> {
  376 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  377 |     Ok(manifest.reader_feature_flags & STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS)
  378 | }

  198 |             }
  199 | 
  200 |             if field.children.is_empty() && mapped_columns.contains_key(&field.id) {
  201 |                 return Some(field.clone());
  202 |             }
  203 | 
  204 |             // V2.0 stores a physical header for structural fields. Keep that
  205 |             // header to preserve the parent's row count and validity, but leave
  206 |             // its children empty so missing descendants are null-filled by the
  207 |             // fragment reader instead of being added to this file's projection.
  208 |             if is_v2_0 && mapped_columns.contains_key(&field.id) {
  209 |                 return Some(lance_core::datatypes::Field {
  210 |                     children: Vec::new(),
  211 |                     ..field.clone()
  212 |                 });
  213 |             }
  214 |             None
  215 |         }
  216 | 
  217 |         if self.uses_v1_data_file_encoding() {
  218 |             return full_schema.project_by_ids(&self.fields, false);
  219 |         }
  220 |         let mapped_columns = self
  221 |             .fields
  222 |             .iter()
  223 |             .copied()
  224 |             .zip(self.column_indices.iter().copied())
  225 |             .filter(|(_, column_index)| *column_index >= 0)
  226 |             .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>();
  227 |         let is_v2_0 = matches!(
  228 |             (self.file_major_version, self.file_minor_version),
  229 |             (0, 3) | (2, 0)
  230 |         );
  231 |         Schema {
  232 |             fields: full_schema
  233 |                 .fields
  234 |                 .iter()
  235 |                 .filter_map(|field| project_field(field, &mapped_columns, is_v2_0))
  236 |                 .collect(),
  237 |             metadata: full_schema.metadata.clone(),
  238 |         }
  239 |     }
  240 | 
  241 |     fn uses_v1_data_file_encoding(&self) -> bool {
  242 |         self.file_major_version == 0 && self.file_minor_version < 3
  243 |     }

  245 |     /// Decode the exact file version stored in this `DataFile` metadata.
  246 |     pub fn file_version(&self) -> Result<ConcreteFileVersion> {
  247 |         ConcreteFileVersion::from_data_file_numbers(

  249 |             self.file_minor_version,

  253 |     pub fn validate(&self, base_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
  254 |         if self.uses_v1_data_file_encoding() {
  255 |             // A tombstone marks a field superseded by a later data file. It is
  256 |             // not a field id, so it carries no ordering; the live ids around it
  257 |             // must still be sorted and distinct.
  258 |             let live: Vec<i32> = self
  259 |                 .fields
  260 |                 .iter()
  261 |                 .copied()
  262 |                 .filter(|field| *field != TOMBSTONE_FIELD_ID)
  263 |                 .collect();
  264 |             if !live.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] < w[1]) {
  265 |                 return Err(Error::corrupt_file(
  266 |                     base_path.clone().join(self.path.clone()),
  267 |                     "contained unsorted or duplicate field ids",
  268 |                 ));
  269 |             }
  270 |         } else if self.column_indices.len() < self.fields.len() {
  271 |             // Every recorded field id must have a column index, but not every column needs
  272 |             // to be associated with a field id (extra columns are allowed).
  273 |             return Err(Error::corrupt_file(
  274 |                 base_path.clone().join(self.path.clone()),
  275 |                 "contained fewer column_indices than fields",
  276 |             ));
  277 |         }
  278 |         Ok(())
  279 |     }
  280 | }

  312 | /// Interns repeated data so that fragments with identical content share a
  313 | /// single heap allocation via `Arc`.
  314 | ///
  315 | /// At 20M fragments the deduplication typically saves multiple GB of heap
  316 | /// because every fragment in a homogeneous table carries the same field list,
  317 | /// and post-compaction fragments share identical version metadata bytes.
  318 | ///
  319 | /// Uses a `Vec`-based linear scan when the cache is small (<=16 entries)
  320 | /// and upgrades to `HashMap` for larger caches. In the common homogeneous
  321 | /// case (1-3 unique values), linear scan avoids per-fragment hashing overhead.
  322 | #[derive(Default)]
  323 | pub struct DataFileFieldInterner {
  324 |     fields: InternCache<i32>,
  325 |     column_indices: InternCache<i32>,
  326 |     inline_bytes: InternCache<u8>,
  327 | }
  328 | 
  329 | /// A cache that uses linear scan for small sizes and HashMap for large.
  330 | /// The threshold is chosen so that scan + compare is cheaper than hash for
  331 | /// typical payload sizes (20-200 bytes).
  332 | enum InternCache<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> {
  333 |     Small(Vec<Arc<[T]>>),
  334 |     Large(HashMap<Arc<[T]>, ()>),
  335 | }
  336 | 
  337 | const INTERN_CACHE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD: usize = 16;
  338 | 
  339 | impl<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> Default for InternCache<T> {
  340 |     fn default() -> Self {
  341 |         Self::Small(Vec::new())
  342 |     }
  343 | }
  344 | 
  345 | impl<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> InternCache<T> {
  346 |     fn intern(&mut self, v: Vec<T>) -> Arc<[T]> {
  347 |         match self {
  348 |             Self::Small(entries) => {
  349 |                 for existing in entries.iter() {
  350 |                     if existing.as_ref() == v.as_slice() {
  351 |                         return existing.clone();
  352 |                     }
  353 |                 }
  354 |                 let arc: Arc<[T]> = Arc::from(v);
  355 |                 entries.push(arc.clone());
  356 |                 if entries.len() > INTERN_CACHE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD {
  357 |                     let mut map = HashMap::with_capacity(entries.len());
  358 |                     for e in entries.drain(..) {
  359 |                         map.insert(e, ());
  360 |                     }
  361 |                     *self = Self::Large(map);
  362 |                 }
  363 |                 arc
  364 |             }
  365 |             Self::Large(map) => {
  366 |                 if let Some((existing, _)) = map.get_key_value(v.as_slice()) {
  367 |                     existing.clone()
  368 |                 } else {
  369 |                     let arc: Arc<[T]> = Arc::from(v);
  370 |                     map.insert(arc.clone(), ());
  371 |                     arc
  372 |                 }
  373 |             }
  374 |         }
  375 |     }
  376 | }

IndexMetadata derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq. Public uuid identifies the index, fields lists dependency IDs, covering_fields is documented as a proper suffix carried but not searched, name is human readable, dataset_version records the training/update snapshot and fragment_bitmap is optional coverage that may include deleted fragments. effective_fragment_bitmap returns None for unknown coverage, otherwise allocates intersection with supplied existing fragments. file_size_map clones paths into a HashMap, with later duplicate paths overwriting earlier sizes; None and Some(empty) both yield empty maps.
