  346 |     /// Build a queryable index directly from serialized FRI details without
  347 |     /// expanding each affected row into a hash map.
  348 |     pub fn try_new(uuid: Uuid, details: FragReuseIndexDetails) -> Result<Self> {
  349 |         let mut version_remaps = Vec::with_capacity(details.versions.len());
  350 |         for (version_idx, version) in details.versions.iter().enumerate() {
  351 |             let mut groups = Vec::with_capacity(version.groups.len());
  352 |             for (group_idx, group) in version.groups.iter().enumerate() {
  353 |                 let changed_row_addrs = RoaringTreemap::deserialize_from(Cursor::new(
  354 |                     &group.changed_row_addrs,
  355 |                 ))
  356 |                 .map_err(|error| {
  357 |                     Error::index(format!(
  358 |                         "failed to deserialize changed row addresses for FRI version {version_idx}, group {group_idx}: {error}"
  359 |                     ))
  360 |                 })?;
  361 |                 let old_frags = group
  362 |                     .old_frags
  363 |                     .iter()
  364 |                     .map(|frag| fragment_layout(frag, "old", version_idx, group_idx))
  365 |                     .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  366 |                 let new_frags = group
  367 |                     .new_frags
  368 |                     .iter()
  369 |                     .map(|frag| fragment_layout(frag, "new", version_idx, group_idx))
  370 |                     .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  371 |                 groups.push(GroupInputWithLayout {
  372 |                     rewritten_old_row_addrs: changed_row_addrs,
  373 |                     old_frags,
  374 |                     new_frags,
  375 |                 });
  376 |             }
  377 |             let remap = RowAddrRemap::compact_with_layout(groups).map_err(|error| {
  378 |                 Error::index(format!(
  379 |                     "failed to build compact remap for FRI version {version_idx}: {error}"
  380 |                 ))
  381 |             })?;
  382 |             version_remaps.push(remap);
  383 |         }
  384 | 
  385 |         Ok(Self {
  386 |             uuid,
  387 |             row_addr_remap: RowAddrRemap::chained(version_remaps),
  388 |             details,
  389 |         })
  390 |     }

  447 | fn remap_row_ids_record_batch(
  448 |     batch: RecordBatch,
  449 |     row_id_idx: usize,
  450 |     remap: impl FnOnce(&mut [Option<u64>]),
  451 | ) -> Result<RecordBatch> {
  452 |     assert_eq!(batch.schema().fields().len(), 2);
  453 |     let other_column_idx = 1 - row_id_idx;
  454 |     let row_ids = batch.column(row_id_idx).as_primitive::<UInt64Type>();
  455 |     let mut remapped_row_ids = row_ids
  456 |         .values()
  457 |         .iter()
  458 |         .copied()
  459 |         .map(Some)
  460 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  461 |     remap(&mut remapped_row_ids);
  462 |     let (val_indices, new_row_ids): (Vec<u64>, Vec<u64>) = remapped_row_ids
  463 |         .iter()
  464 |         .enumerate()
  465 |         .filter_map(|(idx, new_id)| new_id.map(|new_id| (idx as u64, new_id)))
  466 |         .unzip();
  467 |     let new_val_indices = UInt64Array::from_iter_values(val_indices);
  468 |     let new_vals = arrow::compute::take(batch.column(other_column_idx), &new_val_indices, None)?;
  469 | 
  470 |     let mut batch_data: Vec<(usize, ArrayRef)> = vec![
  471 |         (
  472 |             row_id_idx,
  473 |             Arc::new(UInt64Array::from_iter_values(new_row_ids)) as ArrayRef,
  474 |         ),
  475 |         (other_column_idx, Arc::new(new_vals)),
  476 |     ];
  477 |     batch_data.sort_by_key(|(i, _)| *i);
  478 |     Ok(RecordBatch::try_new(
  479 |         batch.schema(),
  480 |         batch_data.into_iter().map(|(_, item)| item).collect(),
  481 |     )?)
  482 | }
  483 | 
  484 | fn remap_row_ids_array(
  485 |     array: ArrayRef,
  486 |     remap: impl FnOnce(&mut [Option<u64>]),
  487 | ) -> PrimitiveArray<UInt64Type> {
  488 |     let primitive_array = array
  489 |         .as_any()
  490 |         .downcast_ref::<PrimitiveArray<UInt64Type>>()
  491 |         .expect("expected row IDs to be uint64 array");
  492 |     let mut remapped = (0..primitive_array.len())
  493 |         .map(|i| {
  494 |             if primitive_array.is_null(i) {
  495 |                 None
  496 |             } else {
  497 |                 Some(primitive_array.value(i))
  498 |             }
  499 |         })
  500 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  501 |     remap(&mut remapped);
  502 |     PrimitiveArray::from(remapped)
  503 | }

  505 | fn remap_fragment_bitmap(
  506 |     details: &FragReuseIndexDetails,
  507 |     fragment_bitmap: &mut RoaringBitmap,
  508 | ) -> Result<()> {
  509 |     for version in details.versions.iter() {
  510 |         for group in version.groups.iter() {
  511 |             let mut removed = 0;
  512 |             for old_frag in group.old_frags.iter() {
  513 |                 if fragment_bitmap.remove(old_frag.id as u32) {
  514 |                     removed += 1;
  515 |                 }
  516 |             }
  517 | 
  518 |             if removed > 0 {
  519 |                 if removed != group.old_frags.len() {
  520 |                     // Straddle: the index covered only part of this rewrite
  521 |                     // group. Caused by the bug fixed in
  522 |                     // <https://github.com/lance-format/lance/pull/6610>.
  523 |                     // We've already removed the indexed old_frags from the
  524 |                     // bitmap above; deliberately do NOT insert new_frags,
  525 |                     // since the merged fragment also contains rows that
  526 |                     // were never indexed. Affected rows fall through to
  527 |                     // flat scan until the next optimize_indices. The fix
  528 |                     // is persisted on the next write via build_manifest.
  529 |                     tracing::warn!(
  530 |                         "Healing straddling fragment-reuse rewrite group in index bitmap: \
  531 |                              group {:?} was only partially indexed ({} of {} old fragments). \
  532 |                              Affected rows will use flat scan until the next optimize_indices.",
  533 |                         group.old_frags,
  534 |                         removed,
  535 |                         group.old_frags.len(),
  536 |                     );
  537 |                     continue;
  538 |                 }
  539 | 
  540 |                 for new_frag in group.new_frags.iter() {
  541 |                     fragment_bitmap.insert(new_frag.id as u32);
  542 |                 }
  543 |             }
  544 |         }
  545 |     }
  546 |     Ok(())
  547 | }

  549 | fn fragment_layout(
  550 |     frag: &FragDigest,
  551 |     role: &str,
  552 |     version_idx: usize,
  553 |     group_idx: usize,
  554 | ) -> Result<(u32, u32)> {
  555 |     let fragment_id = u32::try_from(frag.id).map_err(|_| {
  556 |         Error::index(format!(
  557 |             "FRI version {version_idx}, group {group_idx} has {role} fragment id {} outside the row-address range",
  558 |             frag.id
  559 |         ))
  560 |     })?;
  561 |     let physical_rows = u32::try_from(frag.physical_rows).map_err(|_| {
  562 |         Error::index(format!(
  563 |             "FRI version {version_idx}, group {group_idx} has {role} fragment {fragment_id} with physical_rows={} outside the row-address range",
  564 |             frag.physical_rows
  565 |         ))
  566 |     })?;
  567 |     Ok((fragment_id, physical_rows))
  568 | }

  518 | /// Update `compacted_sstables` in the MemWAL index.
  519 | ///
  520 | /// Called from the final data-changing merge-insert commit for a compaction
  521 | /// target, so the rows and the generation that describes them publish
  522 | /// together.
  523 | ///
  524 | /// A proposed generation must be **strictly greater** than the one the latest
  525 | /// state records for that shard, and a stale one fails the whole transaction.
  526 | /// Accepting it while keeping the larger marker would publish that worker's row
  527 | /// mutations under a generation it did not produce, and anything reading only
  528 | /// the marker could then stop serving SSTables whose rows were never inserted.
  529 | ///
  530 | /// Every other `MemWalIndexDetails` field is carried through untouched.
  531 | pub fn update_mem_wal_index_compacted_sstables(
  532 |     indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  533 |     dataset_version: u64,
  534 |     new_compacted_sstables: Vec<CompactedSsTable>,
  535 | ) -> Result<()> {
  536 |     if new_compacted_sstables.is_empty() {
  537 |         return Ok(());
  538 |     }
  539 | 
  540 |     let mut seen_shards = HashSet::with_capacity(new_compacted_sstables.len());
  541 |     for sstable in &new_compacted_sstables {
  542 |         if !seen_shards.insert(sstable.shard_id) {
  543 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  544 |                 "Duplicate shard {} in one SSTable compaction update; each shard \
  545 |                  may advance at most once per transaction",
  546 |                 sstable.shard_id
  547 |             )));
  548 |         }
  549 |     }
  550 | 
  551 |     // Default details would describe a table with no MemWAL shards at all, so
  552 |     // the recorded generation would name a shard nothing can corroborate.
  553 |     // Refuse instead of inventing metadata.
  554 |     let pos = indices
  555 |         .iter()
  556 |         .position(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  557 |         .ok_or_else(|| {
  558 |             Error::invalid_input(format!(
  559 |                 "Cannot record SSTable compaction progress: the {} system index \
  560 |                  does not exist on this table",
  561 |                 MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME
  562 |             ))
  563 |         })?;
  564 | 
  565 |     // Validated against a copy so a rejected update leaves `indices` exactly as
  566 |     // the caller passed it.
  567 |     let mut details = load_mem_wal_index_details(indices[pos].clone())?;
  568 | 
  569 |     for new_sstable in new_compacted_sstables {
  570 |         match details
  571 |             .compacted_sstables
  572 |             .iter_mut()
  573 |             .find(|sstable| sstable.shard_id == new_sstable.shard_id)
  574 |         {
  575 |             Some(existing) if new_sstable.generation <= existing.generation => {
  576 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  577 |                     "Stale SSTable compaction for shard {}: proposed generation {} \
  578 |                      is not greater than the recorded generation {}",
  579 |                     new_sstable.shard_id, new_sstable.generation, existing.generation
  580 |                 )));
  581 |             }
  582 |             Some(existing) => existing.generation = new_sstable.generation,
  583 |             None => details.compacted_sstables.push(new_sstable),
  584 |         }
  585 |     }
  586 | 
  587 |     // Replaced in place so the index list keeps its order.
  588 |     indices[pos] = new_mem_wal_index_meta(dataset_version, details)?;
  589 |     Ok(())
  590 | }

  385 |                      sibling segment still serves the index; the segment leaves the manifest and \
  386 |                      its files are reclaimed by index cleanup",
  387 |                     index.name,
  388 |                     index.uuid
  389 |                 );
  390 |             }
  391 |             !retired
  392 |         });
  393 |     }

  395 |     /// If an operation modifies one or more fields in a fragment then we need to remove
  396 |     /// that fragment from any indices that cover one of the modified fields.
  397 |     pub fn prune_updated_fields_from_indices(
  398 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  399 |         updated_fragments: &[Fragment],
  400 |         fields_modified: &[u32],
  401 |     ) {
  402 |         if fields_modified.is_empty() {
  403 |             return;
  404 |         }
  405 | 
  406 |         // If we modified any fields in the fragments then we need to remove those fragments
  407 |         // from the index if the index covers one of those modified fields.
  408 |         let fields_modified_set = fields_modified.iter().collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  409 |         for index in indices.iter_mut() {
  410 |             if index
  411 |                 .fields
  412 |                 .iter()
  413 |                 .any(|field_id| fields_modified_set.contains(&u32::try_from(*field_id).unwrap()))
  414 |                 && let Some(fragment_bitmap) = &mut index.fragment_bitmap
  415 |             {
  416 |                 for fragment_id in updated_fragments.iter().map(|f| f.id as u32) {
  417 |                     fragment_bitmap.remove(fragment_id);
  418 |                 }
  419 |             }
  420 |         }
  421 |     }

  423 |     /// Map each (non-tombstoned) field id in a fragment to the path of the data
  424 |     /// file that backs it.
  425 |     fn fragment_field_paths(frag: &Fragment) -> HashMap<i32, &str> {
  426 |         let mut map = HashMap::new();
  427 |         for file in &frag.files {
  428 |             for &field_id in file.fields.iter() {
  429 |                 if field_id >= 0 {
  430 |                     map.insert(field_id, file.path.as_str());
  431 |                 }
  432 |             }
  433 |         }
  434 |         map
  435 |     }

  437 |     /// The columns a `Merge` rewrote in place: for each fragment present in
  438 |     /// both lists, the fields still present whose backing data file path
  439 |     /// changed. Brand-new fragments carry nothing stale.
  440 |     pub fn merge_rewritten_fields(
  441 |         prev_fragments: &[Fragment],
  442 |         new_fragments: &[Fragment],
  443 |     ) -> Vec<(u64, Vec<u32>)> {
  444 |         let prev_by_id: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> =
  445 |             prev_fragments.iter().map(|f| (f.id, f)).collect();
  446 |         new_fragments
  447 |             .iter()
  448 |             .filter_map(|new_frag| {
  449 |                 let prev = prev_by_id.get(&new_frag.id)?;
  450 |                 let prev_paths = Self::fragment_field_paths(prev);
  451 |                 let new_paths = Self::fragment_field_paths(new_frag);
  452 |                 let mut changed: Vec<u32> = prev_paths
  453 |                     .iter()
  454 |                     .filter(|(field_id, prev_path)| {
  455 |                         new_paths
  456 |                             .get(*field_id)
  457 |                             .is_some_and(|new_path| new_path != *prev_path)
  458 |                     })
  459 |                     .map(|(field_id, _)| *field_id as u32)
  460 |                     .collect();
  461 |                 changed.sort_unstable();
  462 |                 (!changed.is_empty()).then_some((new_frag.id, changed))
  463 |             })
  464 |             .collect()
  465 |     }

  467 |     /// After a `Rewrite` fully compacts a fragment, its data overlays are baked
  468 |     /// into the new fragment's base data. An index built *before* one of those
  469 |     /// overlays (`overlay.committed_version > index.dataset_version`) indexed the
  470 |     /// stale pre-overlay values -- and unlike a live overlay, the compacted
  471 |     /// fragment no longer signals that staleness to the query path. Drop each
  472 |     /// rewritten (new) fragment from the coverage of any index covering a field
  473 |     /// such an overlay supplied, so those rows fall back to a flat scan.
  474 |     pub(super) fn prune_overlay_stale_fields_from_indices(
  475 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  476 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  477 |     ) {
  478 |         for group in groups {
  479 |             // field id -> newest overlay committed_version supplying that field
  480 |             let mut overlaid_field_versions: HashMap<i32, u64> = HashMap::new();
  481 |             for old_frag in &group.old_fragments {
  482 |                 for overlay in &old_frag.overlays {
  483 |                     for &field_id in overlay.data_file.fields.iter() {
  484 |                         if field_id < 0 {
  485 |                             // Tombstoned (obsolete) overlay field: supplies nothing.
  486 |                             continue;
  487 |                         }
  488 |                         let entry = overlaid_field_versions.entry(field_id).or_insert(0);
  489 |                         *entry = (*entry).max(overlay.committed_version);
  490 |                     }
  491 |                 }
  492 |             }
  493 |             if overlaid_field_versions.is_empty() {
  494 |                 continue;
  495 |             }
  496 | 
  497 |             let new_fragment_ids = group
  498 |                 .new_fragments
  499 |                 .iter()
  500 |                 .map(|f| f.id as u32)
  501 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  502 |             for index in indices.iter_mut() {
  503 |                 let is_stale = index.fields.iter().any(|field_id| {
  504 |                     overlaid_field_versions
  505 |                         .get(field_id)
  506 |                         .is_some_and(|&overlay_version| overlay_version > index.dataset_version)
  507 |                 });
  508 |                 if is_stale && let Some(fragment_bitmap) = &mut index.fragment_bitmap {
  509 |                     for new_id in &new_fragment_ids {
  510 |                         fragment_bitmap.remove(*new_id);
  511 |                     }
  512 |                 }
  513 |             }
  514 |         }
  515 |     }

  517 |     pub(crate) fn retain_relevant_indices(
  518 |         indices: &mut Vec<IndexMetadata>,
  519 |         schema: &Schema,
  520 |         fragments: &[Fragment],
  521 |     ) {
  522 |         let field_ids = schema
  523 |             .fields_pre_order()
  524 |             .map(|f| f.id)
  525 |             .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  526 | 
  527 |         // Remove indices for fields no longer in schema
  528 |         indices.retain(|existing_index| {
  529 |             existing_index
  530 |                 .fields
  531 |                 .iter()
  532 |                 .all(|field_id| field_ids.contains(field_id))
  533 |                 || is_system_index(existing_index)
  534 |         });
  535 | 
  536 |         let mut indices_by_name: std::collections::HashMap<String, Vec<&IndexMetadata>> =
  537 |             std::collections::HashMap::new();
  538 | 
  539 |         for index in indices.iter() {
  540 |             if index.name != FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME {
  541 |                 indices_by_name
  542 |                     .entry(index.name.clone())
  543 |                     .or_default()
  544 |                     .push(index);
  545 |             }
  546 |         }
  547 | 
  548 |         let mut uuids_to_keep = std::collections::HashSet::new();
  549 | 
  550 |         let existing_fragments = fragments
  551 |             .iter()
  552 |             .map(|f| f.id as u32)
  553 |             .collect::<RoaringBitmap>();
  554 | 
  555 |         // Under a tagged fragment reuse history a segment's stored bitmap is
  556 |         // its provenance (the retired source fragments it was built from),
  557 |         // not the fragments it serves: its live coverage is derived at query
  558 |         // time by translating through the history, and is empty against the
  559 |         // live fragments by construction once its sources were rewritten.
  560 |         // Measuring such a segment here would drop it. Every segment is kept
  561 |         // instead; superseded segments are pruned by the tagged maintenance
  562 |         // path, which reasons on derived coverage.
  563 |         let tagged = indices.iter().any(is_tagged);
  564 | 
  565 |         for (_, same_name_indices) in indices_by_name {
  566 |             if tagged {
  567 |                 for index in same_name_indices {
  568 |                     uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  569 |                 }
  570 |                 continue;
  571 |             }
  572 |             // Unknown coverage is not empty coverage: a segment whose bitmap is
  573 |             // missing has never been measured, and dropping it deletes an index
  574 |             // that migration could not open yet.
  575 |             let (unknown_coverage, same_name_indices): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = same_name_indices
  576 |                 .into_iter()
  577 |                 .partition(|index| index.fragment_bitmap.is_none());
  578 |             for index in unknown_coverage {
  579 |                 uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  580 |             }
  581 | 
  582 |             if same_name_indices.len() > 1 {
  583 |                 let (empty_indices, non_empty_indices): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) =
  584 |                     same_name_indices.iter().partition(|index| {
  585 |                         index
  586 |                             .effective_fragment_bitmap(&existing_fragments)
  587 |                             .as_ref()
  588 |                             .is_none_or(|bitmap| bitmap.is_empty())
  589 |                     });
  590 | 
  591 |                 if non_empty_indices.is_empty() {
  592 |                     // All indices are empty -- keep only the oldest definition.
  593 |                     //
  594 |                     // An empty index definition is still correct: the scanner
  595 |                     // falls back to scanning unindexed fragments, and normal
  596 |                     // index maintenance rebuilds coverage once rows accrue.
  597 |                     // Dropping the definition instead would silently lose the
  598 |                     // index whenever an operation replaces every fragment it
  599 |                     // covered (e.g. a full table rewrite), leaving the dataset
  600 |                     // without its declared index.
  601 |                     let mut sorted_indices = empty_indices;
  602 |                     sorted_indices.sort_by_key(|index: &&IndexMetadata| index.dataset_version);
  603 | 
  604 |                     if let Some(oldest) = sorted_indices.first() {
  605 |                         uuids_to_keep.insert(oldest.uuid);
  606 |                     }
  607 |                 } else {
  608 |                     for index in non_empty_indices {
  609 |                         uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  610 |                     }
  611 |                 }
  612 |             } else {
  613 |                 // Single index whose column is still in schema: keep it, even
  614 |                 // when its coverage is empty (see the all-empty note above).
  615 |                 if let Some(index) = same_name_indices.first() {
  616 |                     uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  617 |                 }
  618 |             }
  619 |         }
  620 | 
  621 |         indices.retain(|index| {
  622 |             index.name == FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME || uuids_to_keep.contains(&index.uuid)
  623 |         });
  624 |     }
  625 | 
  626 |     /// The rewrite groups whose index bitmaps follow the rewrite (source ids
  627 |     /// swapped for destination ids). Groups covered by the stable-partition
  628 |     /// transitions' sources are excluded: they redistribute rows, so their
  629 |     /// bitmaps keep the retired source ids as provenance and the tagged
  630 |     /// fragment reuse index entry records the row-level translation. A group
  631 |     /// must be entirely reordered or entirely order-preserving.
  632 |     pub(super) fn ordered_rewrite_groups(
  633 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  634 |         reordered_sources: Option<&RoaringBitmap>,
  635 |     ) -> Result<Vec<RewriteGroup>> {
  636 |         let Some(sources) = reordered_sources else {
  637 |             return Ok(groups.to_vec());
  638 |         };
  639 |         let mut ordered = Vec::new();
  640 |         for group in groups {
  641 |             let covered = group
  642 |                 .old_fragments
  643 |                 .iter()
  644 |                 .filter(|frag| sources.contains(frag.id as u32))
  645 |                 .count();
  646 |             if covered == 0 {
  647 |                 ordered.push(group.clone());
  648 |             } else if covered != group.old_fragments.len() {
  649 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  650 |                     "a rewrite group mixes transition-covered and order-preserving source fragments",
  651 |                 ));
  652 |             }
  653 |         }
  654 |         Ok(ordered)
  655 |     }
  656 | 
  657 |     pub(super) fn recalculate_fragment_bitmap(
  658 |         old: &RoaringBitmap,
  659 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  660 |     ) -> Result<RoaringBitmap> {
  661 |         let mut new_bitmap = old.clone();
  662 |         for group in groups {
  663 |             let any_in_index = group
  664 |                 .old_fragments
  665 |                 .iter()
  666 |                 .any(|frag| old.contains(frag.id as u32));
  667 |             let all_in_index = group
  668 |                 .old_fragments
  669 |                 .iter()
  670 |                 .all(|frag| old.contains(frag.id as u32));
  671 |             // Any rewrite group may or may not be covered by the index.  However, if any fragment
  672 |             // in a rewrite group was previously covered by the index then all fragments in the rewrite
  673 |             // group must have been previously covered by the index.  plan_compaction takes care of
  674 |             // this for us so this should be safe to assume.
  675 |             if any_in_index {
  676 |                 if all_in_index {
  677 |                     for frag_id in group.old_fragments.iter().map(|frag| frag.id as u32) {
  678 |                         new_bitmap.remove(frag_id);
  679 |                     }
  680 |                     new_bitmap.extend(group.new_fragments.iter().map(|frag| frag.id as u32));
  681 |                 } else {
  682 |                     return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  683 |                         "The compaction plan included a rewrite group that was a split of indexed and non-indexed data",
  684 |                     ));
  685 |                 }
  686 |             }
  687 |         }
  688 |         Ok(new_bitmap)
  689 |     }

  691 |     pub(super) fn handle_rewrite_indices(
  692 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  693 |         rewritten_indices: &[RewrittenIndex],
  694 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  695 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  696 |         let mut modified_indices = HashSet::new();
  697 | 
  698 |         for rewritten_index in rewritten_indices {
  699 |             if !modified_indices.insert(rewritten_index.old_id) {
  700 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  701 |                     "An invalid compaction plan must have been generated because multiple tasks modified the same index: {}",
  702 |                     rewritten_index.old_id
  703 |                 )));
  704 |             }
  705 | 
  706 |             // Skip indices that no longer exist (may have been removed by concurrent operation)
  707 |             let Some(index) = indices
  708 |                 .iter_mut()
  709 |                 .find(|idx| idx.uuid == rewritten_index.old_id)
  710 |             else {
  711 |                 continue;
  712 |             };
  713 | 
  714 |             index.fragment_bitmap = Some(Self::recalculate_fragment_bitmap(
  715 |                 index.fragment_bitmap.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
  716 |                     Error::invalid_input(format!(
  717 |                         "Cannot rewrite index {} which did not store fragment bitmap",
  718 |                         index.uuid
  719 |                     ))
  720 |                 })?,
  721 |                 groups,
  722 |             )?);
  723 |             index.uuid = rewritten_index.new_id;
  724 |             // Update file sizes to match the new index files. When not available
  725 |             // (e.g., from older writers), clear the old file sizes to avoid
  726 |             // using stale sizes from the pre-remap index.
  727 |             index.files = rewritten_index.new_index_files.clone();
  728 |         }
  729 |         Ok(())
  730 |     }

  732 |     pub(super) fn handle_rewrite_fragments(
  733 |         final_fragments: &mut Vec<Fragment>,
  734 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  735 |         fragment_id: &mut u64,
  736 |         version: u64,
  737 |         _next_row_id: Option<&u64>,
  738 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  739 |         for group in groups {
  740 |             // If the old fragments are contiguous, find the range
  741 |             let replace_range = {
  742 |                 let start = final_fragments
  743 |                     .iter()
  744 |                     .enumerate()
  745 |                     .find(|(_, f)| f.id == group.old_fragments[0].id)
  746 |                     .ok_or_else(|| {
  747 |                         Error::commit_conflict_source(
  748 |                             version,
  749 |                             format!(
  750 |                                 "dataset does not contain a fragment a rewrite operation wants to replace: id={}",
  751 |                                 group.old_fragments[0].id
  752 |                             )
  753 |                             .into(),
  754 |                         )
  755 |                     })?
  756 |                     .0;
  757 | 
  758 |                 // Verify old_fragments matches contiguous range
  759 |                 let mut i = 1;
  760 |                 loop {
  761 |                     if i == group.old_fragments.len() {
  762 |                         break Some(start..start + i);
  763 |                     }
  764 |                     if final_fragments[start + i].id != group.old_fragments[i].id {
  765 |                         break None;
  766 |                     }
  767 |                     i += 1;
  768 |                 }
  769 |             };
  770 | 
  771 |             let new_fragments = Self::fragments_with_ids(group.new_fragments.clone(), fragment_id)
  772 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  773 | 
  774 |             // Version metadata for rewritten fragments is handled by the compaction code
  775 |             // (recalc_versions_for_rewritten_fragments) which preserves version information
  776 |             // from the original fragments. We don't modify it here.
  777 | 
  778 |             if let Some(replace_range) = replace_range {
  779 |                 // Efficiently path using slice
  780 |                 final_fragments.splice(replace_range, new_fragments);
  781 |             } else {
  782 |                 // Slower path for non-contiguous ranges
  783 |                 for fragment in group.old_fragments.iter() {
  784 |                     final_fragments.retain(|f| f.id != fragment.id);
  785 |                 }
  786 |                 final_fragments.extend(new_fragments);
  787 |             }
  788 |         }
  789 |         Ok(())
  790 |     }
  791 | }

 1399 |     /// Under a tagged history a translating segment's stored bitmap is its

 1411 |             create_test_index("idx_a", 1, 2, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([1])), false),

 1413 |             create_test_index("idx_a", 1, 3, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([10])), false),
 1414 |             // An all-dead group and an all-empty group: every member kept.
 1415 |             create_test_index("vec_b", 1, 1, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([0])), true),
 1416 |             create_test_index("vec_b", 1, 2, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([1])), true),
 1417 |             create_test_index("idx_c", 2, 1, Some(RoaringBitmap::new()), false),
 1418 |             create_test_index("idx_c", 2, 2, Some(RoaringBitmap::new()), false),

   67 | /// slowly. That is why it is opt-in rather than the default.
   68 | ///
   69 | /// Setting the key back to `false` only stops further conversions. Fragments
   70 | /// already written as `Range` segments keep that encoding until something else
   71 | /// rewrites their row ids (compaction, for example), so coordinate reader
   72 | /// upgrades before enabling it.
   73 | pub const RANGE_SEGMENTS_CONFIG_KEY: &str = "lance.row_ids.range_segments";
   74 | 
   75 | fn range_segments_enabled(manifest: &Manifest) -> bool {
   76 |     manifest
   77 |         .config
   78 |         .get(RANGE_SEGMENTS_CONFIG_KEY)
   79 |         .is_some_and(|value| str_is_truthy(value))
   80 | }
   81 | 
   82 | /// Re-encode inline row id sequences as runs of `Range` segments when the
   83 | /// table has opted in.
   84 | ///
   85 | /// Fragments that the previous manifest already re-encoded are left alone
   86 | /// (their inline bytes are the very same allocation), so a commit pays only
   87 | /// for the fragments it changed; enabling the key re-encodes every fragment
   88 | /// once.
   89 | fn apply_range_segments(
   90 |     manifest: &mut Manifest,
   91 |     current_manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
   92 | ) -> Result<()> {
   93 |     if !range_segments_enabled(manifest) {
   94 |         return Ok(());
   95 |     }
   96 |     let unchanged: HashMap<u64, *const u8> = current_manifest
   97 |         .filter(|current| range_segments_enabled(current))
   98 |         .map(|current| {
   99 |             current
  100 |                 .fragments
  101 |                 .iter()
  102 |                 .filter_map(|fragment| match &fragment.row_id_meta {
  103 |                     Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) => Some((fragment.id, data.as_ptr())),
  104 |                     _ => None,
  105 |                 })
  106 |                 .collect()
  107 |         })
  108 |         .unwrap_or_default();
  109 |     let fragments = Arc::make_mut(&mut manifest.fragments);
  110 |     for fragment in fragments.iter_mut() {
  111 |         let Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) = &fragment.row_id_meta else {
  112 |             continue;
  113 |         };
  114 |         if unchanged.get(&fragment.id) == Some(&data.as_ptr()) {
  115 |             continue;
  116 |         }
  117 |         let mut sequence = read_row_ids(&data[..])?;
  118 |         if sequence.use_range_segments() {
  119 |             fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(write_row_ids(&sequence).into()));
  120 |         }
  121 |     }
  122 |     Ok(())
  123 | }

  207 |     /// Every non-system logical index, mapped to what determines its coverage.
  208 |     ///
  209 |     /// A logical index may be backed by several physical segments, so "did this
  210 |     /// index change" is a question about the whole set. Sorted by UUID so the
  211 |     /// two sides compare positionally.
  212 |     pub fn logical_index_segments(indices: &[IndexMetadata]) -> LogicalIndexSegments {
  213 |         let mut by_name: LogicalIndexSegments = BTreeMap::new();
  214 |         for idx in indices.iter().filter(|idx| !is_system_index(idx)) {
  215 |             by_name
  216 |                 .entry(idx.name.clone())
  217 |                 .or_default()
  218 |                 .push(CoverageIdentity {
  219 |                     uuid: idx.uuid,
  220 |                     fragment_bitmap: idx.fragment_bitmap.clone(),
  221 |                 });
  222 |         }
  223 |         for segments in by_name.values_mut() {
  224 |             segments.sort_unstable_by_key(|segment| segment.uuid);
  225 |         }
  226 |         by_name
  227 |     }

  229 |     /// Apply MemWAL index-coverage rules once the final index list is known.
  230 |     ///
  231 |     /// Coverage records that a base-table index contains the rows a compaction
  232 |     /// copied in, and the WAL pod retires SSTables against it.
  233 |     ///
  234 |     /// It is derived, not reported. An index covering every fragment live at the
  235 |     /// transaction's read version holds every row compaction had copied in by
  236 |     /// then, so it is caught up to that version's `compacted_sstables`. That is
  237 |     /// the only proof available: nothing maps a generation to the fragments its
  238 |     /// rows landed in, so covering the table as the transaction read it is how
  239 |     /// an index shows it covered those rows. Fragments appended since are a
  240 |     /// later gap.
  241 |     ///
  242 |     /// Deriving rather than transmitting means no claim can go stale between
  243 |     /// inspection and commit, the answer survives rebase (`read_version` is
  244 |     /// fixed for a transaction's life), and any operation can earn coverage --
  245 |     /// an ordinary reindex that fully covers no longer has to throw its work
  246 |     /// away and wait for a repair.
  247 |     ///
  248 |     /// Only meaningful once catch-up is required, where a missing entry means
  249 |     /// "not caught up" and the SSTables stay. A legacy table reads a missing
  250 |     /// entry as "fully caught up", so this leaves it untouched rather than
  251 |     /// making the table look more covered than it is.
  252 |     pub fn apply_mem_wal_index_coverage(
  253 |         final_indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  254 |         segments_before: &LogicalIndexSegments,
  255 |         read_version_state: Option<ReadVersionState<'_>>,
  256 |         new_version: u64,
  257 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  258 |         let Some(pos) = final_indices
  259 |             .iter()
  260 |             .position(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  261 |         else {
  262 |             // The system index went away with this transaction (MemWAL disable,
  263 |             // or an overwrite). There is no coverage left to maintain.
  264 |             return Ok(());
  265 |         };
  266 | 
  267 |         let mut details = load_mem_wal_index_details(final_indices[pos].clone())?;
  268 | 
  269 |         // Nothing has ever been compacted, so no index can be behind and there
  270 |         // is no coverage to invalidate.
  271 |         if details.compacted_sstables.is_empty() && details.index_catchup.is_empty() {
  272 |             return Ok(());
  273 |         }
  274 | 
  275 |         let segments_after = Self::logical_index_segments(final_indices);
  276 |         let catchup_before = std::mem::take(&mut details.index_catchup);
  277 | 
  278 |         // Per shard: what this commit records as compacted, and the most the
  279 |         // read version may credit. Generations compacted after that read landed
  280 |         // in fragments no index under consideration has seen; the committed
  281 |         // value caps it in turn, so a read version since rolled back cannot
  282 |         // retire SSTables no live commit copied in.
  283 |         let read_details = read_version_state
  284 |             .map(|state| {
  285 |                 state
  286 |                     .indices
  287 |                     .iter()
  288 |                     .find(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  289 |                     .cloned()
  290 |                     .map(load_mem_wal_index_details)
  291 |                     .transpose()
  292 |             })
  293 |             .transpose()?
  294 |             .flatten();
  295 |         let shards: Vec<(Uuid, u64, u64)> = details
  296 |             .compacted_sstables
  297 |             .iter()
  298 |             .map(|committed| {
  299 |                 let at_read = read_details
  300 |                     .as_ref()
  301 |                     .and_then(|read| {
  302 |                         read.compacted_sstables
  303 |                             .iter()
  304 |                             .find(|s| s.shard_id == committed.shard_id)
  305 |                     })
  306 |                     .map_or(0, |s| s.generation);
  307 |                 (
  308 |                     committed.shard_id,
  309 |                     committed.generation,
  310 |                     at_read.min(committed.generation),
  311 |                 )
  312 |             })
  313 |             .collect();
  314 | 
  315 |         // Every fragment live when the transaction read the table. An index
  316 |         // spanning all of them holds every row compacted by then.
  317 |         let read_fragments: Option<RoaringBitmap> = read_version_state.map(|state| {
  318 |             state
  319 |                 .manifest
  320 |                 .fragments
  321 |                 .iter()
  322 |                 .map(|fragment| fragment.id as u32)
  323 |                 .collect()
  324 |         });
  325 | 
  326 |         let covers_read_version = |segments: &[CoverageIdentity]| -> bool {
  327 |             let Some(required) = read_fragments.as_ref() else {
  328 |                 return false;
  329 |             };
  330 |             if required.is_empty() {
  331 |                 // Subset-of-empty is trivially true, so this would credit every
  332 |                 // index on a table with no fragments. Refused because an empty
  333 |                 // fragment list is not only what an emptied table looks like:
  334 |                 // it is also what a manifest written before #8438 looks like,
  335 |                 // where UpdateMemWalState published no fragments at all. On
  336 |                 // such a table the SSTables are the last copy of those rows,
  337 |                 // and crediting coverage would retire them. The cost is that a
  338 |                 // genuinely emptied table keeps its SSTables.
  339 |                 return false;
  340 |             }
  341 |             let mut covered = RoaringBitmap::new();
  342 |             for segment in segments {
  343 |                 match segment.fragment_bitmap.as_ref() {
  344 |                     Some(bitmap) => covered |= bitmap,
  345 |                     // An unknown bitmap cannot be shown to cover anything.
  346 |                     None => return false,
  347 |                 }
  348 |             }
  349 |             required.is_subset(&covered)
  350 |         };
  351 | 
  352 |         let mut rebuilt: Vec<IndexCatchupProgress> = Vec::new();
  353 |         for (name, after) in segments_after.iter() {
  354 |             // Compared by [`CoverageIdentity`], not segment UUID: an Update
  355 |             // that touches an indexed field prunes a segment's fragment bitmap
  356 |             // in place while keeping its UUID, so a UUID-only comparison would
  357 |             // carry a position forward that the index no longer earns.
  358 |             let unchanged = segments_before.get(name) == Some(after);
  359 |             let carried = unchanged
  360 |                 .then(|| catchup_before.iter().find(|e| e.index_name == *name))
  361 |                 .flatten();
  362 |             let proven = covers_read_version(after);
  363 | 
  364 |             if carried.is_none() && !proven {
  365 |                 // Changed, and nothing shows the new index covers the read
  366 |                 // version. No entry: a missing one reads as "not caught up".
  367 |                 continue;
  368 |             }
  369 | 
  370 |             let generations = shards
  371 |                 .iter()
  372 |                 .map(|&(shard_id, committed, creditable)| {
  373 |                     let prior = carried
  374 |                         .and_then(|entry| entry.caught_up_generation_for_shard(&shard_id))
  375 |                         .unwrap_or(0);
  376 |                     let credited = if proven { creditable } else { 0 };
  377 |                     // Takes the better of what this commit proves and what an
  378 |                     // unchanged index already held, so a commit reading an older
  379 |                     // version does not lower a position it cannot re-prove. The
  380 |                     // clamp is the exception: a position above what this commit
  381 |                     // records as compacted describes rows no live commit copied
  382 |                     // in.
  383 |                     CompactedSsTable::new(shard_id, prior.max(credited).min(committed))
  384 |                 })
  385 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  386 |             if generations.iter().all(|g| g.generation == 0) {
  387 |                 continue;
  388 |             }
  389 |             rebuilt.push(IndexCatchupProgress::new(name.clone(), generations));
  390 |         }
  391 |         rebuilt.sort_by(|a, b| a.index_name.cmp(&b.index_name));
  392 | 
  393 |         let mut before_sorted = catchup_before;
  394 |         before_sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.index_name.cmp(&b.index_name));
  395 |         if rebuilt == before_sorted {
  396 |             return Ok(());
  397 |         }
  398 | 
  399 |         let dropped: Vec<&str> = before_sorted
  400 |             .iter()
  401 |             .map(|e| e.index_name.as_str())
  402 |             .filter(|name| !rebuilt.iter().any(|kept| kept.index_name == *name))
  403 |             .collect();
  404 |         if !dropped.is_empty() {
  405 |             // The first thing to check when SSTables stop becoming trimmable.
  406 |             log::info!(
  407 |                 "MemWAL index catch-up invalidated at version {new_version} for {dropped:?}: \
  408 |                  these indices changed and no longer cover the version this commit read"
  409 |             );
  410 |         }
  411 | 
  412 |         details.index_catchup = rebuilt;
  413 |         final_indices[pos] = new_mem_wal_index_meta(new_version, details)?;
  414 |         Ok(())
  415 |     }
  416 | 
  417 |     /// Drop coverage for indices a post-`build_manifest` step narrowed.
  418 |     ///
  419 |     /// The derivation runs while the manifest is being built, but the index list
  420 |     /// is not final there: `migrate_indices` can recalculate a segment's
  421 |     /// fragment bitmap and keep its UUID, so an index can narrow after its
  422 |     /// position was decided. It reports which ones it touched rather than the
  423 |     /// caller re-snapshotting every bitmap to find out. Only ever removes.
  424 |     pub fn withdraw_coverage_invalidated_after_build(
  425 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  426 |         changed: &[String],
  427 |         new_version: u64,
  428 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  429 |         if changed.is_empty() {
  430 |             return Ok(());
  431 |         }
  432 |         let Some(pos) = indices
  433 |             .iter()
  434 |             .position(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  435 |         else {
  436 |             return Ok(());
  437 |         };
  438 |         let mut details = load_mem_wal_index_details(indices[pos].clone())?;
  439 |         let before = details.index_catchup.len();
  440 |         details
  441 |             .index_catchup
  442 |             .retain(|entry| !changed.contains(&entry.index_name));
  443 |         if details.index_catchup.len() == before {
  444 |             return Ok(());
  445 |         }
  446 |         log::info!(
  447 |             "MemWAL index catch-up withdrawn at version {new_version} for {changed:?}: \
  448 |              these indices were recalculated after their coverage was derived"
  449 |         );
  450 |         indices[pos] = new_mem_wal_index_meta(new_version, details)?;
  451 |         Ok(())
  452 |     }

  454 |     /// Step one of a commit attempt: what the operation settles about the
  455 |     /// index list, computed against the manifest current at the attempt.
  456 |     ///
  457 |     /// Runs the tagged-table write gate (`system_index::frag_reuse::gate`)
  458 |     /// before anything is derived, keeps `current_indices` as the original
  459 |     /// list, and derives the prepared list: on an in-place column rewrite
  460 |     /// (an update with `fields_modified`, a merge swapping a column's data
  461 |     /// file, a data replacement) the coverage it invalidates is withdrawn
  462 |     /// along a tagged fragment reuse history or pruned by fragment id on any
  463 |     /// other table (`withdraw_in_place_rewrites`). Every other operation
  464 |     /// prepares the list unchanged; `Restore` never reaches the builder and
  465 |     /// restores its snapshot's list whole.
  466 |     ///
  467 |     /// `frag_reuse_ledger` is the decoded history of the current entry when
  468 |     /// the caller read it (the commit path decodes it once per attempt for
  469 |     /// the operations above); without it an inline history is decoded from
  470 |     /// the entry and an external one is refused, so a commit never guesses
  471 |     /// at the lineage. A history that does not decode is an error, never
  472 |     /// treated as "no lineage". `frag_reuse` is what the commit path settled
  473 |     /// about the entry itself.
  474 |     pub fn prepare_indices(
  475 |         &self,
  476 |         current_manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
  477 |         current_indices: Vec<IndexMetadata>,
  478 |         config: &ManifestBuildConfig,
  479 |         frag_reuse_ledger: Option<Arc<crate::system_index::frag_reuse::ledger::FragReuseLedger>>,
  480 |         frag_reuse: FragReuseUpdate,
  481 |     ) -> Result<PreparedIndices> {
  482 |         crate::system_index::frag_reuse::gate::classify(
  483 |             &self.operation,
  484 |             current_manifest,
  485 |             &current_indices,
  486 |             &frag_reuse,
  487 |             config.migration_next_row_id,
  488 |         )?;
  489 |         let mut prepared = current_indices.clone();
  490 |         if let Some(manifest) = current_manifest {
  491 |             let rewrites = Self::rewritten_physical_columns(
  492 |                 &self.operation,
  493 |                 &manifest.schema,
  494 |                 &manifest.fragments,
  495 |             );
  496 |             if !rewrites.is_empty() {
  497 |                 let lineage =
  498 |                     crate::system_index::frag_reuse::lineage::TaggedLineage::from_indices_with_ledger(
  499 |                         &current_indices,
  500 |                         frag_reuse_ledger,
  501 |                     )?;
  502 |                 let live: RoaringBitmap = manifest
  503 |                     .fragments
  504 |                     .iter()
  505 |                     .filter_map(|fragment| u32::try_from(fragment.id).ok())
  506 |                     .collect();
  507 |                 Self::withdraw_in_place_rewrites(
  508 |                     &mut prepared,
  509 |                     rewrites,
  510 |                     &manifest.schema,
  511 |                     &live,
  512 |                     lineage.as_ref(),
  513 |                 );
  514 |             }
  515 |         }
  516 |         Ok(PreparedIndices::new(
  517 |             current_manifest.map(|manifest| manifest.version),
  518 |             current_indices,
  519 |             prepared,
  520 |             frag_reuse,
  521 |         ))
  522 |     }

  580 |     /// Build the next manifest from a prepared index list
  581 |     /// (`prepare_indices`): the builder applies the operation to the
  582 |     /// prepared list and publishes only the final list; the original list
  583 |     /// is what MemWAL coverage is compared against. The prepared result must
  584 |     /// have been derived against `current_manifest`.
  585 |     pub fn build_manifest_prepared(
  586 |         &self,
  587 |         current_manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
  588 |         prepared: PreparedIndices,
  589 |         transaction_file_path: &str,
  590 |         config: &ManifestBuildConfig,
  591 |         read_version_state: Option<ReadVersionState<'_>>,
  592 |     ) -> Result<(Manifest, Vec<IndexMetadata>)> {
  593 |         if prepared.manifest_version() != current_manifest.map(|manifest| manifest.version) {
  594 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  595 |                 "the index list was prepared against manifest version {:?} but the manifest \
  596 |                  being built on is at version {:?}; every commit attempt prepares against the \
  597 |                  manifest it builds on",
  598 |                 prepared.manifest_version(),
  599 |                 current_manifest.map(|manifest| manifest.version)
  600 |             )));
  601 |         }
  602 |         // The tagged-table write gate, run again at this chokepoint (it is
  603 |         // pure) so a build cannot skip it whatever prepared the list.

 4150 |     fn test_data_overlay_build_manifest_multi_fragment() {
 4151 |         // Overlays targeting two distinct fragments are each applied and stamped.
 4152 |         // A targeted fragment already carrying an overlay (committed at v3) gets
 4153 |         // the new overlay appended and stamped while its existing overlay is
 4154 |         // preserved, and a fragment the operation does not target is passed
 4155 |         // through with its existing overlays untouched.
 4156 |         let mut frag0 = Fragment::new(0);
 4157 |         frag0.overlays = vec![overlay_with_field(5, 3)]; // targeted, pre-existing at v3
 4158 |         let frag1 = Fragment::new(1);
 4159 |         let mut frag2 = Fragment::new(2);
 4160 |         frag2.overlays = vec![overlay_with_field(9, 3)]; // untargeted, committed at v3
 4161 |         let schema = ArrowSchema::new(vec![ArrowField::new("id", DataType::Int32, false)]);
 4162 |         let mut manifest = Manifest::new(
 4163 |             LanceSchema::try_from(&schema).unwrap(),
 4164 |             Arc::new(vec![frag0, frag1, frag2]),
 4165 |             crate::format::DataStorageFormat::new(ConcreteFileVersion::V2_0),
 4166 |             HashMap::new(),
 4167 |         );
 4168 |         // The pre-existing overlays were committed at v3, so the current
 4169 |         // manifest must be at least that version; the new commit then stamps
 4170 |         // its overlay at v4, keeping the fragment's overlays newest-last.
 4171 |         manifest.version = 3;
 4172 | 
 4173 |         let txn = Transaction::new(
 4174 |             manifest.version,
 4175 |             Operation::DataOverlay {
 4176 |                 groups: vec![
 4177 |                     DataOverlayGroup {
 4178 |                         fragment_id: 0,
 4179 |                         overlays: vec![overlay_with_field(1, 0)],
 4180 |                     },
 4181 |                     DataOverlayGroup {
 4182 |                         fragment_id: 1,
 4183 |                         overlays: vec![overlay_with_field(2, 0)],
 4184 |                     },
 4185 |                 ],
 4186 |             },
 4187 |             None,
 4188 |         );
 4189 | 
 4190 |         let (result, _) = txn
 4191 |             .build_manifest(Some(&manifest), vec![], "txn", &default_build_config())
 4192 |             .unwrap();
 4193 | 
 4194 |         let frag = |id: u64| {
 4195 |             result
 4196 |                 .fragments
 4197 |                 .iter()
 4198 |                 .find(|f| f.id == id)
 4199 |                 .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("fragment {id} missing from result"))
 4200 |         };
 4201 |         // The already-overlaid target keeps its v3 overlay and appends the new
 4202 |         // one, stamped to the new version.
 4203 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays.len(), 2);
 4204 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays[0].committed_version, 3);
 4205 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays[1].committed_version, result.version);

 4209 |         // The untargeted fragment is unchanged: same overlay, original version.
 4210 |         assert_eq!(frag(2).overlays.len(), 1);
 4211 |         assert_eq!(frag(2).overlays[0].committed_version, 3);
 4212 |         assert!(result.version > manifest.version);

  257 | /// Validate that a Merge schema preserves the dataset's field id bindings.
  258 | ///
  259 | /// Readers resolve columns by field id (name -> schema id -> DataFile::fields
  260 | /// position), so renumbered ids silently rebind live columns to other columns'
  261 | /// bytes. Shared ids must keep their field path. Their logical type,
  262 | /// nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary may change only when every
  263 | /// existing base or overlay file carrying the id is replaced and every
  264 | /// proposed fragment materializes the id in a base data file. New ids must
  265 | /// exceed the manifest's max so a dropped field's id is never reused. An
  266 | /// existing path may move to a fresh id only when every proposed fragment
  267 | /// materializes that id in a base data file (the `alter_columns` cast path).
  268 | /// Omitting a field (dropping it) and updating field metadata remain legal.
  269 | fn merge_schema_valid(
  270 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  271 |     new_schema: &Schema,
  272 |     fragments: &[Fragment],
  273 | ) -> Result<()> {
  274 |     let prior_schema = &manifest.schema;
  275 |     let new_fragment_map: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> = fragments
  276 |         .iter()
  277 |         .map(|fragment| (fragment.id, fragment))
  278 |         .collect();
  279 | 
  280 |     // Remap and semantic errors first: a renumbered schema usually violates
  281 |     // both the shared-id and new-id clauses.
  282 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  283 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id) else {
  284 |             continue;
  285 |         };
  286 |         let prior_path = prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  287 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  288 |         if prior_path != new_path {
  289 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  290 |                 "Merge operation remaps field id {} from \"{}\" to \"{}\". \
  291 |                  Merge must preserve the dataset's field ids: derive the new schema \
  292 |                  from the dataset's current schema instead of renumbering fields.",
  293 |                 field.id, prior_path, new_path
  294 |             )));
  295 |         }
  296 |         if let Some(changes) = shared_field_binding_changes(prior_field, field)
  297 |             && !is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(manifest, &new_fragment_map, field.id)
  298 |         {
  299 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  300 |                 "Merge operation changes field id {} (\"{}\") without rewriting it in \
  301 |                  every existing fragment: {}. Merge must preserve each existing field's \
  302 |                  logical type, nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary unless all \
  303 |                  existing base and overlay files carrying that field are replaced.",
  304 |                 field.id, new_path, changes
  305 |             )));
  306 |         }
  307 |     }
  308 | 
  309 |     let max_field_id = manifest.max_field_id();
  310 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  311 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_none() && field.id <= max_field_id {
  312 |             let next_id_msg = match max_field_id.checked_add(1) {
  313 |                 Some(next_id) => format!("New fields must use ids of at least {}.", next_id),
  314 |                 None => {
  315 |                     "No further field id can be allocated because ids are exhausted.".to_string()
  316 |                 }
  317 |             };
  318 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  319 |                 "Merge operation assigns id {} to new field \"{}\", but ids up to {} are \
  320 |                  already used by current or dropped fields. {}",
  321 |                 field.id,
  322 |                 new_schema.field_path(field.id)?,
  323 |                 max_field_id,
  324 |                 next_id_msg
  325 |             )));
  326 |         }
  327 |     }
  328 | 
  329 |     let mut prior_paths = HashMap::with_capacity(prior_schema.fields_pre_order().count());
  330 |     for field in prior_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  331 |         prior_paths.insert(prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?, field);
  332 |     }
  333 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  334 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_some() {
  335 |             continue;
  336 |         }
  337 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  338 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_paths.get(&new_path) else {
  339 |             continue;
  340 |         };
  341 |         let materialized = fragments.iter().all(|fragment| {
  342 |             fragment
  343 |                 .files
  344 |                 .iter()
  345 |                 .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field.id))
  346 |         });
  347 |         if !materialized {
  348 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  349 |                 "Merge operation remaps existing field \"{}\" from id {} to id {} without \
  350 |                  rewriting its data. Every proposed fragment must materialize the new field \
  351 |                  id in a base data file.",
  352 |                 new_path, prior_field.id, field.id
  353 |             )));
  354 |         }
  355 |     }
  356 | 
  357 |     Ok(())
  358 | }
  359 | 
  360 | fn is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(
  361 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  362 |     new_fragment_map: &HashMap<u64, &Fragment>,
  363 |     field_id: i32,
  364 | ) -> bool {
  365 |     manifest.fragments.iter().all(|prior_fragment| {
  366 |         let Some(new_fragment) = new_fragment_map.get(&prior_fragment.id) else {
  367 |             return false;
  368 |         };
  369 | 
  370 |         let is_materialized = new_fragment
  371 |             .files
  372 |             .iter()
  373 |             .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id));
  374 |         if !is_materialized {
  375 |             return false;
  376 |         }
  377 | 
  378 |         prior_fragment
  379 |             .referenced_lance_files()
  380 |             .filter(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id))
  381 |             .all(|prior_file| {
  382 |                 !new_fragment.referenced_lance_files().any(|new_file| {
  383 |                     new_file.fields.contains(&field_id)
  384 |                         && new_file.base_id == prior_file.base_id
  385 |                         && new_file.path == prior_file.path
  386 |                 })
  387 |             })
  388 |     })
  389 | }
  390 | 
  391 | fn shared_field_binding_changes(prior: &Field, new: &Field) -> Option<String> {
  392 |     let mut changes = Vec::with_capacity(4);
  393 |     if prior.logical_type != new.logical_type {
  394 |         changes.push(format!(
  395 |             "logical type {} -> {}",
  396 |             prior.logical_type, new.logical_type
  397 |         ));
  398 |     }
  399 |     if prior.nullable != new.nullable {
  400 |         changes.push(format!("nullable {} -> {}", prior.nullable, new.nullable));
  401 |     }
  402 |     if prior.encoding != new.encoding {
  403 |         changes.push(format!(
  404 |             "storage encoding {:?} -> {:?}",
  405 |             prior.encoding, new.encoding
  406 |         ));
  407 |     }
  408 |     if prior.dictionary != new.dictionary {
  409 |         changes.push("dictionary".to_string());
  410 |     }
  411 |     if changes.is_empty() {
  412 |         None
  413 |     } else {
  414 |         Some(changes.join(", "))
  415 |     }
  416 | }

    4 | //! Transaction definitions for updating datasets
    5 | //!
    6 | //! Prior to creating a new manifest, a transaction must be created representing
    7 | //! the changes being made to the dataset. By representing them as incremental
    8 | //! changes, we can detect whether concurrent operations are compatible with
    9 | //! one another. We can also rebuild manifests when retrying committing a
   10 | //! manifest.
   11 | //!
   12 | //! For more details please refer to the
   13 | //! [Transaction Specification](https://lance.org/format/table/transaction/#transaction-types).
   14 | //!
   15 | //! The work splits along these lines:
   16 | //!
   17 | //! ```text
   18 | //! builder            Transaction: an operation plus the version it was based on
   19 | //! operation          the vocabulary of changes an operation can describe
   20 | //! update_map         incremental edits to the manifest's string maps
   21 | //! validate           pre-commit checks against the manifest being replaced
   22 | //! prepare            what a commit attempt settles about the index list first
   23 | //! manifest_build     applying an operation to produce the next manifest
   24 | //! index_maintenance  how that narrows or drops index metadata
   25 | //! row_version        how it assigns row ids and per-row version metadata
   26 | //! conflicts          whether two operations collide, for the commit retry path
   27 | //! proto              the persisted protobuf encoding of all of the above
   28 | //! ```

   30 | mod builder;
   31 | mod conflicts;

   35 | mod prepare;
   36 | mod proto;

   53 |     UpdateMap, UpdateMapEntry, translate_config_updates, translate_schema_metadata_updates,
   54 | };
   55 | pub use validate::validate_operation;

   57 | use crate::format::{IndexMetadata, Manifest};

   59 | use std::collections::BTreeMap;

   62 | /// Non-system logical index name -> its physical segments, ordered by UUID.
   63 | ///
   64 | /// Whole segment metadata rather than UUIDs alone: operations such as `Rewrite`
   65 | /// prune a segment's fragment bitmap while keeping its UUID, so a UUID-only
   66 | /// comparison would keep coverage for an index that no longer spans the same
   67 | /// base fragments.
   68 | pub type LogicalIndexSegments = BTreeMap<String, Vec<CoverageIdentity>>;
   69 | 
   70 | /// What one physical index segment contributes to coverage.
   71 | ///
   72 | /// Deliberately not the whole [`IndexMetadata`]. It rests on one contract:
   73 | /// changing an index's physical contents mints a new UUID. Of the mutations
   74 | /// sanctioned under an existing UUID, only the fragment bitmap changes which
   75 | /// rows the index answers for -- an `Update` prunes it in place, and
   76 | /// `migrate_indices` recalculates it -- so the UUID alone is not enough and the
   77 | /// bitmap has to be compared too. The rest of the metadata, file lists and
   78 | /// timestamps and inferred details, is filled in by migrations routinely;
   79 | /// comparing it would withdraw coverage for no reason.

   82 |     uuid: Uuid,
   83 |     fragment_bitmap: Option<RoaringBitmap>,
   84 | }

   87 | ///
   88 | /// An index covering every fragment live at this version holds every row
   89 | /// compaction had copied into the base table by then, so it is caught up to
   90 | /// that version's `compacted_sstables`. That is the only proof available:
   91 | /// nothing maps a compaction generation to the fragments its rows landed in.

   96 | /// different head: other commits move the compacted generations and the
   97 | /// positions already recorded.

## SharedStream state transitions

The queue belongs to whichever side lags; the other side must have zero buffered count. A bounded permit is forgotten when a clone is enqueued and restored when that clone is consumed or discarded on dead-side drop. Polling upstream happens with the mutex released, but ownership prevents the peer from polling concurrently. Ready clears ownership; Pending keeps it. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:28-45; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Owned: obtain permit and claim side
    Owned --> Owned: upstream Pending
    Owned --> Idle: item ready; clone for live peer
    Owned --> Exhausted: upstream None
    Owned --> Idle: owning handle dropped
    Exhausted --> Exhausted: drain own buffer, then repeat None
```

This diagram omits per-side queue and permit substates; the transition implementation and ordering are given above, including capacity acquisition before poll-owner arbitration. Bounded(0) cannot reach Owned; upstream panic can remove inner without restoration; clone panic poisons the mutex. These are not recoverable states implemented by the diagram. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:47-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-247)

## CPU runtime publication and child reset

The first caller sets the installation-election flag, optionally registers the child hook, allocates/leaks a Runtime, then publishes its pointer. Other callers yield until non-null publication. The pointer lifetime comments justify unsafe shared references because allocation is never reclaimed; SeqCst is used throughout publication/reset. Child reset clears pointer and election flag without reclaiming the inherited runtime, while retaining the hook-installed flag. Initialization panic and ignored registration errors are limitations, not successful recovery paths. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:89-134)

The full [error API/conversion matrix](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core-errors.md) is part of the core contract. An unknown commit outcome is Wrapped(CommitStatusUnknownError), keeping version and source while preserving the exhaustive Error enum. is_not_found explicitly vetoes that wrapper even if its source says a manifest was missing. ### Raw values and fixed-size lists

ValueEncoder implements three distinct interfaces. Block compression accepts FixedWidth only and returns its unchanged buffer as Some, including empty buffers. Mini-block compression handles FixedWidth and nested FSL, with parallel validity buffers followed by the unchanged leaf buffer. Per-value compression handles FixedWidth or FSL; nullable FSL is copied into row-major validity bytes followed by leaf bytes, while nonnullable FSL moves its leaf storage. None of these paths performs IO. Invalid input handling differs: block/mini-block unsupported variants return errors, while per-value unsupported variants panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:151-309; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:350-512; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:808-823)

Raw mini-block selection starts with two byte-aligned values, or eight nonaligned values using an estimated sixteen-value size. It doubles while estimated bytes remain strictly below 8186 and doubled count stays within the cached maximum. Initial count can already exceed a small configured maximum. Zero width reaches a debug assertion; malformed byte/count relationships are not validated. Full chunks retain a positive count log even when last; only a residual chunk gets log0. Partial FixedWidth chunks account for all remaining bytes, not a recomputed logical byte count. The comment's 4KiB bound is not the actual 8186-byte constant. Mini-block FSL preserves whole outer rows. Cumulative dimensions scale each child validity bit slice and leaf size; buffers are ordered outer validity through inner validity, then leaf data. Nullable leaf AllNull is unsupported here, unlike the per-value route. Per-row validity estimates can overestimate actual chunk-wide bitmap bytes; initial validity-vector capacity omits rows-per-chunk and can grow despite the preallocation comment. Dimension products, slicing and several casts remain unchecked. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:141-309)

Per-value FSL descriptors use every actual dimension. However simple_per_value_fsl repeatedly multiplies by the original outer dimension. For a nonnullable outer dimension2, inner dimension3 and 32-bit leaf, its block reports128 bits per row while its descriptor implies192. This follows directly from source arithmetic; no Lance runtime reproduction was run. Recursive is_nullable sends nullable descendants to the separate helper, which does multiply actual dimensions. Equal-dimension direct tests and nullable randomized tests do not establish coverage of the discrepant nonnullable case. Nullable per-value FSL allocates ceil(cumulative_dimension/8) validity bytes per nullable layer per outer row. Its leaf stride is ceil(leaf_bits/8)*dimension_product, requiring byte-expanded leaf items on this route. Direct bitpacked Boolean input does not satisfy this assumption; caller normalization beyond this local codec contract requires the mapped primitive path in [the encoding protocol](protocol-encoding.md). ### Variable-width interfaces and validation

Binary mini-blocks encode their own offset table at the beginning of each chunk, using signed32/64-bit input offsets rebased to chunk start plus table bytes. Each chunk is padded with0x48 to4/8-byte alignment respectively. The output is one concatenated buffer plus external chunk descriptors; logical num_values is retained from input even though chunk partitioning uses offsets.len()-1. Per-value VariableEncoder and VariableDecoder instead move an existing VariableWidthBlock unchanged. Whole-block VariableEncoder writes a separate width/data-start header, then original offsets and all original value bytes. These interfaces are not interchangeable. It does not validate UTF-8 or unrequested offsets. new asserts32/64, whereas from_variable directly casts a nested Flat width to u8; malformed width can reach division by zero or the fallback32 branch. ### Byte-stream split and entropy

BSS groups each byte position across values in a single chunk: out[j*n+i]=in[i*width+j]. ### Physical V2 envelope

```text
file
  data buffers and applicable padding
  global payloads (including descriptor where present)
  column metadata protobuf payloads
  column metadata offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  global buffer offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  footer: column_metadata_start:u64
          column_table_start:u64
          global_table_start:u64
          global_buffer_count:u32
          column_count:u32
          major:u16, minor:u16, magic:[u8;4] = LANC
```

All footer/table integers are little-endian; footer length is 40 bytes. The tables contain raw offset/size entries, not length-prefixed protobuf messages. A self-described file identifies its schema through the descriptor/global metadata; an embedded mini representation can require an externally supplied schema. Alignment, column mapping and accepted page grammar depend on the exact runtime. Corruption checks are not universally exhaustive: preserve the explicit validation limits in the reader section. (protos/file2.proto:11-115; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:834-921)

The remaining sections retain the verified contracts for every storage family, metadata wrapper, compatibility branch and analyzed codec. Where a component is mapped-only or an implementation detail has a separate protocol (for example [retrying publication](protocol-commit.md)), the boundary is stated rather than expanded into a new per-file analysis obligation.

## Fragment and row lineage state

See the [complete fragment schema analysis](../L2-files/protos/fragment_metadata.proto.md) for every tag and exact declaration. A fragment owns a unique ID, data-file list, optional deletion metadata, overlays, physical row count, and three mutually exclusive inline/column lineage pairs. Column lineage uses -3/-4/-5 system field IDs, one matching file per sequence, non-null uint64 values, and exactly physical_rows values. Only v2 data files supply the needed column mapping; flag 2048 protects old readers from silently interpreting an unknown arm as absence. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-87; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305)

Overlay interpretation is ordered by committed_version, then list position. Deleted offsets never become visible because of an overlay. Rank below an offset in its field bitmap selects a value, so unequal field coverage permits unequal physical value-column lengths. A covered NULL differs from a missing offset. Flag 64 gates use. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:19-27; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:185-249)

Deletion paths combine fragment ID, read version, and opaque concurrent-write ID; protobuf comments describe one Int32Array Arrow IPC column/batch and .arrow, Roaring .bin. The current implementation uses UInt32 instead, as documented in the actual-payload section below. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:251-286)

The [row-ID schema](../L2-files/protos/rowids.proto.md) defines half-open ranges, sorted holes and sorted/general arrays with16/32-bit relative deltas or raw u64 values. Its bitmap comment says MSB-first, but this checkout reads/writes LSB-first and asserts bytes[0xfb,0x03] for ten positions with bit2 cleared. Packed integers use little-endian bytes in implementation; schema alone omits endianness. This is a documented comment/code discrepancy, not a verified historical migration. ## Fragment-tree representation

A version selects an inline root or 16-byte display-order UUID root stored at _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root, plus mutations absent from the root. Children partition fragment IDs by half-open min-key boundaries; counts include buffered changes. Leaf materialization watermarks certify no earlier pending mutation above the leaf, while interiors use zero. Mutations carry exact signed aggregate deltas.
