## V2 envelope and encoding layers

The minimal envelope permits independent item counts per column and stores byte buffers without imposing logical types. Data precedes column metadata, column metadata offset table, global buffer offset table, then the footer. Footer fields in order are three little-endian u64 offsets (column metadata start, column metadata table, global buffer table), two u32 counts (global buffers, columns), two u16 versions (major, minor), and LANC. The shared reader consumes exactly 40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-861). Padding may precede aligned buffers/metadata/table starts. Page buffers may be noncontiguous; 8 MB pages are advice, not a hard validity bound. (protos/file2.proto:11-115)

```text
file2 envelope
  data buffers
  column metadata blocks
    column encoding + optional column buffers
    pages: buffers + length + encoding + priority
  column metadata position/size table
  global buffer position/size table
  footer: A:u64 B:u64 C:u64 globals:u32 columns:u32 major:u16 minor:u16 LANC
```

The tree above reproduces the schema's composition: encoding locations are direct bytes, deferred byte range, or explicit none; page/column buffer offsets and sizes must have matching cardinality. Top-level row priority is distinct from a page's logical length. (protos/file2.proto:117-216)

The older lance.encodings namespace models Nullable/List/FixedSizeList and scalar transformations as ArrayEncoding, with ColumnEncoding wrappers for plain values, zone maps and blob descriptions. Its List encoding folds nullness into end offsets, but a strict greater-than null test in the comments conflicts with the formula at an equality boundary; see the [full analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_0.proto.md). This must be resolved from the decoder before implementing compatible list bytes. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:59-155; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:307-358)

The newer lance.encodings21 namespace separates structural layouts from compressive blocks. Layouts are MiniBlock, Constant, FullZip, Blob and Sparse; recursive compression alternatives include Flat, Variable, Constant, both bitpacking forms, FSST, Dictionary, RLE, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and both packed-struct forms. Exact fields and tag identities are in the [complete encoding analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_1.proto.md). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:341-357; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675)

## Generic split-block Bloom filters

Local SBBF raw bytes contain only concatenated32-byte blocks; each is eight little-endian u32 words. new accepts any multiple of32, including0, and no power-of-two/minimum/maximum check is imposed. There is no magic,version,seed,type,NDV orFPP header. to_bytes and write_bitset preserve block then lane order. Empty input is structurally accepted but membership methods panic because no block exists. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:243-269; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:290-352)

Membership identity is xxHash64(seed0) over the exact AsBytes representation. high32 selects floor(high32*block_count/2^32) via saturating multiplication; low32 x sets bit ((x*salt_i wrapping u32)>>27) in each lane. All eight selected bits are required for a positive membership result. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:98-151; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:290-317; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:419-425)

## Ownership and publication

A transaction describes intent relative to `read_version`. Data-file completion is not dataset publication. `InsertBuilder` writes fragments, constructs an Overwrite or Append transaction, then supplies it to `CommitBuilder`; `execute_uncommitted` stops before that publication. `CommitBuilder` selects new, existing or detached commit paths and constructs a new Dataset handle from the committed manifest. For an existing dataset, the normal publication loop is:

1. Retain the transaction's read-version Dataset and index state. A strict Overwrite (`num_retries == 0`) skips automatic rebase; otherwise restore the original read snapshot when required. There are `max(num_retries, 1)` attempts, not `num_retries + 1`. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1649-1705)

|---|---|---|
| Publication `CommitConflict` | The commit loop may catch up, rebase and publish a new candidate within its attempt/time budget. This is not automatically an operation-level conflict. | rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1866-1951 |
| Resolver retryable conflict (**R** below) | Current operation payload cannot safely merge as-is. Error propagates from `check_txn`/finish; an outer operation may need to reread/recompute. | Resolver incompatible conflict (**I** below) | Reject this stale/incompatible intent. Do not resubmit it unchanged as a publication collision. | rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:456-513 |
| `CommitStatusUnknown` | Publication could have succeeded. Preserve evidence/files, inspect durable table state, and reconcile before retrying or destructive cleanup. After a handler error, the commit path reads the target manifest and its durable transaction and compares **serialized protobuf transaction values**, not transient in-memory payloads. Outcomes are Ours, Foreign, Absent or Unknown. A manifest without our recorded transaction is Foreign. Missing manifest is definitive Absent only if the handler says version-not-found is definitive; otherwise bounded read retries may end Unknown. Recovery makes at most three read attempts. Ours normally becomes success, with caches/cleanup updated. On `OtherError`, a handler may explicitly request that the original error still propagate after confirmed success. Foreign/Absent permit cleaning the stale transaction file; Unknown forbids that cleanup. Exhausted publication conflicts clean the attempt's transaction file and return conflict. Therefore “returned error” is not proof that nothing committed, and blanket file deletion in a caller's error path is unsafe. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1866-2006)

Read each row as **our uncommitted operation against an intervening committed operation**. Rules are asymmetric. Global guards run before the table: a Project/Merge that does not preserve nullability versus a value-supplying Append/Update/DataReplacement/DataOverlay is R in either order; Merge versus an effective schema/field metadata update is R in either order; Restore versus such a metadata update is I in either order. ### Row updates, deletes and overlays

Delete/Update first accept disjoint modified-fragment sets. An overlap requires an affected-row map; without one it is R. For tracked fragments, changed data-file identity or disappearance of the initial fragment is R. A changed deletion file marks the fragment for finish-time reconciliation. If the operation already removed entire fragments and supplied no updated fragments, initialization can discard the affected-row map as a full-fragment shortcut. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:240-453; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:620-984)

Finish-time reconciliation loads current deletion vectors for marked fragments. Any intersection between current deletions and our affected rows (or an indeterminate intersection size) is R. Otherwise union deletions, remove fully deleted fragments or write/cache replacement deletion files, update transaction fragment metadata and advance `read_version` to the current manifest. A marked fragment without the required affected-row map is an internal error. The operation is not safe merely because the earlier fragment-level test returned P. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2463-2623)

Update has additional guards: with a primary-key filter, a concurrent Append is R; another Update without a filter is R; mismatched filter fields, comparison failure or possible overlap is R. Project removing a modified field is R. Against an Overlay, RewriteColumns conflicts when the same updated fragment and modified field overlap, regardless of actual row overlap. A row-moving update (new fragments with RewriteRows or unspecified mode) requires affected rows and rejects intersection with overlay coverage. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:726-984)

Overlay ordering is deliberately asymmetric. Our Overlay after another Overlay or RewriteColumns update is permitted by this checker; the newer overlay can win. Against a row-moving Update, mark affected fragments, then compare `(current deleted offsets − original deleted offsets)` with the union of our overlay coverage across fields. Intersection or missing current fragment is R; otherwise advance read version. A concurrent Delete alone does not mark a fragment for this calculation, but removing an entire target fragment already conflicts. A Delete combined with a marked Update may cause a conservative retry. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1960-2060; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2637-2707; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:3142-3171)

DataReplacement rejects removal of a nonnegative replacement field or target fragment as I. A partial Delete can coexist. Update conflicts when it removes the target (I), or when a matching updated fragment is row-moving or modifies a replacement field (R). Another replacement conflicts only on both fragment and field overlap. A new index on a replaced field conflicts irrespective of its fragment bitmap. (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1778-1943)

CreateIndex detects duplicate new ordinary names, two installations of either system singleton, append-versus-drop of the same name, and conflicting replacement of a shared removed UUID. Pure duplicate removal is idempotent. CreateIndex after Update/Merge/DataReplacement may withdraw coverage through current tagged lineage; a bitmap must never keep claiming rows whose indexed values changed. Without the tagged withdrawal path, affected-field DataReplacement is R. Merge installing MemWal or removing/retyping indexed fields in the tagged path is R. Do not place a new operation only in the top-level matcher. **Trust: synthesized from frozen deep records plus selected primitive dispatch ranges.** This is the decision contract; [format-spec](format-spec.md) owns persisted grammar and exact version matrices. [Encoding Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md) owns type/file navigation. Uncovered implementation details remain source-readable, not a transcription backlog.

## The four decisions must stay separate

1. **Choose exact file version.** Public selectors and strict persisted-version parsing differ. Current stable default is V2_2; next is unstable V2_3. File footer identity, dataset version, blob representation version and index version are different domains. Use the [exact identity table](format-spec.md#exact-file-identity-and-acceptance). (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:25-262)
2. **Choose structural field behavior.** Version composition supplies ordered field/page behaviors to the version-free mechanism. Primitive, blob, list, FSL, map and struct factories decide logical shape/column allocation. A metadata tag alone does not make every shape legal in every format. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:24-288; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:95-134; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:95-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:103-139)
3. **Choose page layout.** Dense-u16/u32, constant and sparse mechanisms interpret normalized rep/def structure and the selected version's behavior sequence. Sparse automatic selection is a lazy fallback when dense rep/def planning requires page splitting or one row exceeds budget, and any explicit setting suppresses that automatic path. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs:8-24; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7695-7880)
4. **Choose physical compression inside that layout.** `CompressionStrategy` has distinct block, mini-block and per-value factories. Production version modules compose helper selectors. A codec offered by one interface or generic decoder is not proof of admission in another interface or exact file reader. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:86-152; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:896-1236; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-93)

### Stable and unstable gates

V2_1 selects dense-u16, raw complex-null levels and a fixed-width dictionary policy excluding 64-bit values. It allows an all-null ConstantLayout without an inline scalar or compressed levels, but rejects scalar constants and sparse pages. V2_2 adds dense-u32 framing, compressed levels, scalar constants and the 64-bit dictionary policy, but still rejects sparse pages. V2_3 composes sparse planning before constant/dense-u32 fallbacks. The exact reader grammar remains the authority: enabling a writer mechanism without admitting its exact metadata on read creates unreadable output. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7730-7799; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:121-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:129-139; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:93-162; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:93-160)

Explicit sparse requests are case-insensitive. A format without sparse behavior rejects them. In sparse-capable composition, explicit sparse planning can defer constant-layout cases to later behavior. Automatic sparse checks supported value blocks, treats unavailable value preparation as dense fallback, but propagates actual sparse planning errors. A field marked sparse is therefore not a guarantee that every page is physically sparse. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7690-7705; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7802-7877)

Stable formats preserve backward/forward contracts; no compatibility obligation attaches to earlier unstable V2_3 revisions. Frozen legacy readers retain existing behavior and do not become foundations for new writers. Capability flags are an additional gate independent of the numeric file version; paired sticky mixed-version/tagged-FRI flags and unknown reader/writer flag checks are specified in the [frozen feature-flag contract](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs.md). ## Configuration and codec policy

Compression parameter precedence is exact dtype key → exact column key, otherwise first matching wildcard in HashMap iteration order → version strategy's field metadata overlay. An exact empty column entry suppresses wildcard selection; None cannot clear an inherited value. Multiple wildcard matches have no specificity ordering. Numeric metadata parse failures can be ignored, and BSS/chunk-size failures warn; do not describe this parser as strict validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:45-169; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:554-585; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-38)

The existing [shared compression contract](behavior-contracts.md#shared-compression-selection-and-decoder-dispatch) supplies exact RLE/bitpacking benefit comparisons and reader dispatch; [variable/FSST/BSS contract](behavior-contracts.md#variable-fsst-and-bss-behavior-contracts) supplies thresholds. Key decision hazards are:

- Mini-block and per-value `compression=none` shortcuts occur at different stages of validation. Explicit codec names are interpreted differently by the two factories. A named codec is not a universal promise of that output. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:655-696; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:797-841)
- Automatic FSST requires eligible non-binary values, maximum length at least 5 and data size at least 32,768 bytes. Large per-value compression can take precedence even over explicit FSST. BSS needs a non-none outer compression parameter; forced BSS alone is insufficient. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:148-185; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:655-696; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:797-841)
- RLE must strictly beat raw payload size; equal comparison against bitpacking can prefer RLE. An absent ratio threshold is not the named 0.5 threshold. Estimation and actual encoding can both perform work. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-510)
- Metadata-only output (`None`) differs from an empty payload (`Some(empty)`). Some compressor factories are feature-gated; successful construction can still defer failure to lazy codec initialization. Do not replace these states with one “empty” case. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:896-987; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:141-432)
- Statistics are shared/cached and can include physical null slots or unused values. Mutating a payload without invalidating/rebuilding its statistics can select the wrong codec. They are not uniformly logical-valid-row statistics. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:52-216; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:232-594)

Field lifecycle is construct → prepare all roots → maybe_encode/optional flush → final flush → await page tasks → finish. Preserve per-column page order, complete top-level rows and original top-row counts through nested flattening. `FieldEncoder` is Send, while strategies are Send+Sync; the traits do not enforce a complete state machine for callers. [Frozen encoder](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs.md) contains exact signatures and failure/mutation details. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:39-234)

An encoding extension must choose whether it changes logical structure, page layout, compression, or only policy. Add the mechanism at that seam, descriptor fields where needed, exact-version writer composition **and** reader grammar/decoder dispatch. Keep metadata/data counts, buffer order/alignment, rep/def coordinates, null meaning and optional payload distinctions consistent. Existing unsafe buffer/codec preconditions and corruption-check limits are documented in [behavior contracts](behavior-contracts.md); a new selector does not validate them automatically. `IndexPluginRegistry` stores case-insensitive plugin aliases and full protobuf names. `supports_details` validates the full qualified type suffix after the final slash; lookup-by-details separately derives a short terminal name. The short-name lookup is not a replacement for exact type-identity admission. Historical detail package identities remain stable; put new messages in the current schema rather than relocating old ones. (rust/lance-index/src/registry.rs:26-177; protos/index.proto:6-383; protos/index_old.proto:8-28)

Scalar SearchResult carries set certainty: Exact is exact; AtMost is a superset requiring post-filtering; AtLeast is a subset and matters when composing negation. Row IDs may be opaque stable IDs; an index returning row addresses must advertise that distinction. Old-index filters use fragment membership only for address-style IDs and exact row-ID membership for stable IDs. Reinterpreting an opaque ID's high bits as fragment identity can revive or discard the wrong rows. (rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:398-480; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:531-564; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:628-762)

## Build and publish

`DatasetIndexExt::create_index` configures `CreateIndexBuilder`. It accepts one keyed column at this entry. Before training, vector/FTS requests undergo fragment-reuse admission. Scalar FTS resolves document granularity/nested paths separately. `execute_uncommitted` builds files and metadata without publishing; ordinary execution creates a `CreateIndex {new_indices, removed_indices}` transaction, applies the commit and reloads the committed UUID. Replacement removes the selected prior same-name declarations through that transaction; file creation alone has not made an index visible. Multi-segment FM construction has its own builder branch. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2053-2078; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:167-242; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:687-758)

### Scalar plugin path

Resolve a field and plugin by `ScalarIndexParams.index_type`. The plugin must provide a BasicTrainer or this generic path rejects it. `new_training_request(params, field)` defines ordering and row-ID/address needs; the Dataset prepares a stream satisfying that request (or accepts caller-provided preprocessed data), then `train_index` writes to the new IndexStore and returns `CreatedIndex`. The result's details/version/file list must be persisted; the trainer does not commit a Dataset. FTS training can project resolved nested documents rather than treating every requested name as an ordinary scalar field. (rust/lance/src/index/scalar.rs:349-453; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:29-100; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:483-529)

The plugin contract includes name, exactness, supported version, optional query parser, load/cache behavior, segment-compatibility validation and optional seed hooks. A default segment validator accepts any combination, so plugins needing identical models/hash parameters must override it. Seed-writer construction must derive parameters from details and perform no I/O; `might_use_seeds=false` avoids probing data files; `update_from_seeds=None` requests full-scan fallback. User-visible details JSON is part of the public API. (rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:102-200; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:284-367)

Advertising asynchronous batch row-ID remapping requires implementing `load_index_with_remapping`; its default rejects a present remapper. Cache entries are already namespaced per index by the caller; serialized/store-bound representations must reconstruct against the correct store/remapping context. The load future supplied to single-flight caching is awaited at most once on a miss and may be dropped unawaited on a warm hit. (rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:182-223; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:370-375)

### Vector path, including IVF-PQ

Whole-table builds may retain an index definition without training when the dataset is empty or has too few vectors for its quantizer. Such metadata has empty coverage and records details for later training. A caller-selected vector fragment subset is validated and owns its training-row math; it does not use whole-table definition-only fallback. Do not interpret an empty definition as a fully indexed table. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:658-677; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:1007-1048)

Modern IVF-PQ uses `IvfIndexBuilder<FlatIndex, ProductQuantizer>`. The entry dispatches on index kind, element type and IndexFileVersion, propagates fragment filtering and transpose selection. The retained legacy IVF-PQ route rejects filtered builds; it is a frozen compatibility path, not the route for a new format feature. (rust/lance/src/index/vector.rs:1199-1325)

The modern builder stages are: load/train IVF → load/train quantizer → shuffle input into partitions → build partition streams → merge/write partition files. Pre-supplied IVF/quantizer objects skip their respective training. Quantizer training samples requested fragments, normalizes cosine data, filters nonfinite values, optionally computes IVF residuals, and invokes the quantizer with L2 training distance. These preparation choices must stay consistent with query-time distance/quantization interpretation. This contract does not qualify every numerical kernel. (rust/lance/src/index/vector/builder.rs:553-594; rust/lance/src/index/vector/builder.rs:729-830)

## Query contract

`VectorIndex::search` returns row-ID/distance batches and receives a PreFilter for deleted or otherwise excluded rows. Partition discovery returns partition IDs paired with centroid distances, closest first. A Query specifies k, inclusive lower/exclusive upper distance bounds, minimum/maximum probes, optional HNSW ef, refine factor, metric, index-use flag, parallelism and RQ approximation mode. ApproxMode currently affects RQ only; “Accurate” is not a global exact-search guarantee. Query parallelism 0 is automatic, -1 uses CPU-pool size, 1 is sequential and larger values are bounded by the execution layer. These are interface contracts; concrete implementations may override scheduling. (rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:95-171; rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:205-267)

Default `search_partitions` validates equal partition/distance counts and a valid half-open interval, then searches sequentially, sets each partition's centroid distance and consults optional stop/control callbacks. Prepared-partition and batch-search methods require implementation support; callers must gate batch search with `supports_batch_partition_search` (default false). Partition selection, approximate scoring and later refine/filter work are separate stages. (rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:254-267; rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:296-385)

Dataset Scanner validates incompatible search options and chooses vector/FTS/MinHash/ordinary filtered-read sources before residual filter, ordering, limit and take/projection stages. Scalar-index eligibility is conditional on scanner options and vector prefiltering. Preserve the SearchResult certainty and fragment coverage when composing this plan; a physical index hit is not proof that all rows or predicates are covered. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3498-3663; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:398-480)

## Update, merge and rebuild

`optimize_indices` groups the complete manifest list by name, excluding system indices. Any unknown type or too-new segment skips that whole logical group. Covering-field indices are skipped with a warning for table-wide maintenance but explicitly naming one returns an error, because current rebuilders do not preserve those carried values. A fully covered scalar group can skip work when neither retrain nor explicit merge is requested. A no-file-work optimize can still need a CreateIndex commit to advance MemWal catch-up state. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2831-3002)

### Scalar maintenance

Select old segments and calculate live/deleted coverage. If no unindexed data and at most one selected segment, return no work. Merge old data without a full rebuild only when live old coverage exists, UpdateCriteria does not require old data, NGram fragment reuse does not force rebuilding, and either there is one selected segment or the type has an N:1 merge primitive (BTree/NGram/Bitmap). Otherwise rebuild precisely the intended fragment set. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:530-649)

The merge path tries compatible seeds only when the plugin says they might exist and harvesting succeeds for the relevant unindexed fragments. Otherwise scan new data, merge BTree/NGram/Bitmap with per-segment filters, or call the scalar index's `update` with a mode-correct old-data filter. Return new UUID/files/details/coverage and the minimum selected source dataset version; replacement publication goes through the normal CreateIndex transaction. A new index implementation must honor the old-data filter rather than copying every old posting. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:658-766; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:531-564; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:628-762)

### Vector maintenance

Stored coverage with no live coverage is **dormant**, distinct from a born-empty definition. Dormant stored vectors must be replaced, not merged back under stable row IDs. A deferred definition trains from saved parameters over the current column. Retrain/dormant rebuild checks exact expected coverage; definition-only degradation is accepted only when too-few-vector state is established and no files/coverage were produced. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:820-984; rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:1052-1190)

`num_indices_to_merge=Some(0)` appends a segment for unindexed rows without removing old ones; no unindexed rows makes that explicit append a no-op. The default can also append when existing segments are query-compatible but have different models, reusing the current suffix model. With no new rows, default optimize may rebalance. Ordinary merge selects a suffix, removes only segments actually merged, and derives metadata from those actual sources rather than an incompatible earlier segment. Preserve raw/provenance coverage and effective live coverage distinctions instead of replacing one with the other. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:1193-1437)

Concurrent changes are resolved at commit: CreateIndex/Rewrite ordering can withdraw coverage, preserve partial tagged provenance with scan fallback, or require a rebuild. A new segment's bitmap is a correctness assertion, not just a performance hint. Read the [directional conflict contract](protocol-commit.md#index-coverage-and-rewrite-lineage) before changing that assertion.

## Dataset ownership, version and mutation

A Dataset represents a checked-out manifest snapshot. `Dataset::open(uri)` loads through DatasetBuilder. Numeric checkout stays on the current branch; a named tag resolves its recorded branch/version. Checkout returns a new Dataset, while `checkout_latest(&mut self)` replaces manifest and derived fragment bitmap; it clears base-store caches if base paths changed. `main` is the default-branch alias in reference contexts. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:520-588)

Restore creates a **new** transaction based on the latest version, pointing at the currently checked-out historical version. It is not an in-place rewrite of that historical manifest. Detached commits do not become latest and do not join ordinary history; the builder also enforces existing-dataset/v2-manifest-path requirements. Public commit entry points accept operation/read version/store/handler/session parameters and delegate to the common path. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1459-1474; rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1620-1669; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)

Mutation methods have distinct handle effects: Rust builders commonly return a new Dataset/result; `&mut Dataset` convenience methods replace their state after success. Python native delete/update/restore/compaction/index methods replace the internal Arc after successful execution; an existing independently checked-out handle remains its own snapshot. Do not describe every Python method as returning a new Dataset: delete/update return count dictionaries, create_index returns the facade, and uncommitted index creation does not update the snapshot. (python/src/dataset.rs:2018-2110; python/src/dataset.rs:2281-2295; python/src/dataset.rs:2874-2891; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:509-523; python/python/lance/dataset.py:4607-4638)

Storage mutation is not atomic merely because the public function returns Result: data files can exist before commit, and a storage error can follow successful publication. Use the [commit outcome contract](protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success) before retrying or cleaning files. Cleanup of old versions is separately destructive: removed versions cannot be checked out/restored and their unique data can be lost. The explanation path computes a cleanup plan without deleting files. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1477-1483; python/src/dataset.rs:2298-2345)

## Read/query contracts

Rust `Dataset::scan()` creates a Scanner. `try_into_stream` builds a physical plan and executes it; collecting batches is a separate operation. Plan order is source → filter → sort → limit/offset → late take/projection as required. Source selection and index use depend on search and prefilter options. Invalid combinations fail validation, and requesting projected constants alone is not automatically a supported row-count source. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2889-2932; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3498-3663)

`take` selects logical row positions; `take_rows` selects internal row IDs. IDs and encoded physical addresses are separate when stable IDs are enabled. Unfiltered count sums fragment counts; a filtered count uses a scanner with empty user projection plus row ID. Python's Arrow-expression count uses its scanner directly, whereas string/None count goes through the native Dataset count method. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1705-1778; python/python/lance/dataset.py:2616-2622; python/src/dataset.rs:1668-1697)

Python scanner defaults are applied before explicit non-None options. The final builder forwards options to the native scanner. Projection by names and projection by SQL transforms are mutually exclusive; string and Substrait filters are also mutually exclusive at the binding. Row-ID/address flags are separate; row-address prefilter bytes use the shared RowAddrMask decoder. FTS phrases cannot target multiple columns in the native dict-query route. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:1496-1565; python/python/lance/dataset.py:7391-7428; python/src/dataset.rs:1244-1449)

`LanceScanner.to_table` materializes the entire reader; `to_batches` iterates it. The native LanceReader owns a background stream producer, cancellation channel and bounded output channel. It terminates on first stream error/end or caller/channel cancellation; an unexpectedly closed producer channel becomes an error rather than silent EOF. Retaining all yielded batches can consume unbounded caller memory even though the channel is bounded. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:7442-7452; python/src/reader.rs:48-123)

DataFusion integration parses/qualifies identifiers according to planner options: exact field-name matching precedes ASCII case-insensitive matching; relation qualification is disabled by default and otherwise dots can represent nested access. The Dataset TableProvider translates projection/filter/limit into Scanner and declares Exact filter pushdown. Multiple output partitions are merged preserving known ordering, otherwise coalesced; a single partition executes directly. Preserve declared pushdown exactness when adding expressions. (rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350; rust/lance/src/datafusion/dataframe.rs:132-197; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)

## Vector training maps

- **V01.** count_trainable_vectors is a threshold probe: nonnullable non-multivector columns return total rows; nullable/multivector paths use bounded readahead and stop after enough usable vectors, excluding null rows and null list elements. It need not return the complete population count. `rust/lance/src/index/vector.rs:529-578`.
- **V02.** Streaming coreset training dispatches L2/Cosine to the L2 policy, Dot to its policy, and Hamming to HammingCoresetAlgorithm. The separate float-policy selector rejects Hamming. The new float/Hamming adapters and compact counters are mapped implementation details; no recall or performance result is claimed. `rust/lance/src/index/vector/ivf.rs:3837-3877,5033-5058`.
- **V03.** K-means convergence uses absolute loss scale and a separate zero-loss case; cluster radii begin at negative infinity so negative distances are represented, then empty clusters become zero. `rust/lance-index/src/vector/kmeans.rs:333-339,369-387,1149-1161`.
